arguments.body:
2028 Helio Medical Plan Comparison
Prepared September 21, 2027

Purpose
Neutral side-by-side comparison based only on the preliminary employee-only 2028 preview currently available. This update records the clarified HSA timing and contingency. It does not make or recommend an election. Items marked VERIFY remain unresolved.

Current status
The preview is preliminary, not final, and assumes 24 paychecks. Final network files, final plan documents, and the 2028 election deadline are not posted.

Plan snapshot

| Item | HDHP | PPO |
|---|---:|---:|
| Employee premium per paycheck | $98 | $164 |
| Paychecks | 24 | 24 |
| Preliminary annual employee premium | $2,352 ($98 × 24) | $3,936 ($164 × 24) |
| Premium difference | HDHP is $1,584 lower per year on the preview figures | — |
| Deductible | $2,000 | $750 |
| Out-of-pocket maximum | $4,000 | $3,500 |
| Employer HSA amount shown | $1,000 estimate | No employer HSA shown |

HSA timing and contingency — clarified

The HDHP’s displayed $1,000 employer HSA estimate consists of four $250 quarterly deposits:

- $250 deposit each quarter, for a displayed total of $1,000 if all four deposits are made.
- The deposits are not made upfront.
- Each deposit is contingent on Riley remaining HSA-eligible at that deposit date.
- The $1,000 is therefore not guaranteed if eligibility changes and should not be treated as available at the start of the year.
- Exact deposit dates and any additional administrative conditions still require confirmation in the final plan materials.

Neutral observations

- On the preliminary payroll figures alone, the HDHP employee premium is $1,584 lower annually ($2,352 versus $3,936).
- The HDHP has the higher stated deductible by $1,250 ($2,000 versus $750).
- The HDHP has the higher stated out-of-pocket maximum by $500 ($4,000 versus $3,500).
- The displayed $1,000 HSA amount may offset eligible healthcare costs over time, but its value depends on all four deposits being made and on eligibility continuing at each deposit date. It does not reduce paycheck deductions upfront and is not a guaranteed $1,000 available on day one.
- These stated figures do not establish which coverage is adequate or which plan has the lower total cost for Riley’s actual care.

Verification gaps to retain

Network and provider access
[ ] VERIFY final network files for both plans.
[ ] VERIFY the network names and whether Riley’s relevant doctors, clinics, hospitals, urgent-care facilities, laboratories, imaging providers, and other needed providers are in-network.
[ ] VERIFY any provider-specific tiering, referral, authorization, or network restrictions.
[ ] VERIFY out-of-network coverage and cost exposure.

Final documents and plan terms
[ ] VERIFY the final 2028 plan documents, not merely the preliminary preview.
[ ] VERIFY the final premiums, deductible definitions, coinsurance/copays, covered services, exclusions, and out-of-pocket maximum rules.
[ ] VERIFY whether medical and prescription cost-sharing limits are combined or separate, if applicable.
[ ] VERIFY the HDHP’s exact HSA eligibility requirements and the employer’s deposit conditions.
[ ] VERIFY the exact quarterly deposit dates and whether any proration, employment-status, or other conditions apply.

Election timing
[ ] VERIFY the 2028 election deadline; it has not been posted.
[ ] VERIFY the coverage effective date, enrollment process, and any correction or cancellation rules.

Current conclusion

No election is being made or recommended. The comparison remains informational and incomplete pending the final network files, final 2028 plan documents, exact HSA deposit terms and dates, and the posted 2028 election deadline.

arguments.hypothesis: Among the eight Helio Start workspaces with the highest post-admission support effort, separating customer-side authority or access blocks from product-guidance needs will explain meaningful differences in elapsed resolution time and repeat contacts; the mixed data-import case should be analyzed separately rather than forced into either mechanism.

arguments.body:
Purpose
Bounded diagnostic for the next review, not a broad onboarding rebuild. Test whether mechanism-level separation improves explanation of resolution time and repeat contacts in the eight highest-effort Helio Start workspaces.

Observed starting point (September 9 mechanism review)
- Eight high-effort workspaces; 472 post-admission product-support minutes total.
- Customer-side access or authority: 4 workspaces, 238 minutes.
- Product guidance: 3 workspaces, 174 minutes.
- Mixed data-import case: 1 workspace, 60 minutes.
- Preserve these classifications as the working mechanism labels; do not infer causality from minutes alone.

Scope and exclusions
- Anchor the interpretation to the accepted 52-workspace cohort and retain its accepted day-90 statuses: 39 paid-active, 7 canceled, 4 past due, and 2 billing hold.
- Analyze only post-admission product-support activity in the eight-workspace diagnostic subset for the mechanism test.
- Exclude pre-admission connector assistance and billing contacts from support minutes, elapsed-resolution measures, repeat-contact counts, and conclusions.
- Keep the mixed data-import workspace visible as its own category; do not recode it as customer-side authority or product guidance without evidence.

Review design
1. For each of the eight workspaces, preserve workspace-level mechanism, in-scope minutes, first in-scope contact timestamp, resolution timestamp, elapsed resolution time, and repeat-contact count.
2. Compare customer-side authority/access blocks with product-guidance needs on elapsed resolution time and repeat contacts.
3. Report the mixed data-import case separately, including its small-n limitation.
4. Check whether contact volume or elapsed time is being driven by one workspace; show workspace-level values alongside any summary.
5. Treat the result as descriptive/mechanism diagnostic unless the available data support a stronger design. Do not pool excluded activity into the comparison.
6. Reconcile the diagnostic readout with, but do not revise, the accepted 52-workspace cohort or its day-90 status table. Any later status changes must be reported as subsequent events rather than used to rewrite the accepted day-90 snapshot.

Decision questions for the next review
- Is the customer-side authority/access mechanism associated with longer elapsed resolution or more repeat contacts than product guidance in this small set?
- Does the mixed data-import case behave differently enough to warrant a separate workflow or follow-up investigation?
- What additional timestamp or contact-definition evidence is needed before treating the mechanism split as actionable?

Non-claims
This brief makes no staffing recommendation and no CAC, paid-channel, pipeline, or forecast claim. It is not an attribution analysis, a paid-growth assessment, or a commitment to change onboarding, staffing, plans, or operating targets.

Recommended diagnostic rule

Repeat contact should be measured at the workspace level using distinct human contact episodes, not raw messages or system events.

A qualifying contact episode is:

- A customer-initiated follow-up that adds a new question, request, evidence, or problem after the prior exchange.
- A substantive agent-initiated interaction that advances the case, requests customer action, provides a workaround, or communicates a material status or resolution.
- A call, meeting, or other documented human interaction that materially advances the case.

Do not count:

- Automated receipt or acknowledgement messages.
- Bot, routing, assignment, or status notifications.
- Duplicate messages generated by retries or workflow automation.
- Internal notes, QA events, or CSAT requests.
- Agent messages that merely repeat an automated acknowledgement.
- Multiple messages within the same unresolved exchange as separate contacts.

arguments.title: December 10 board operating segment — pre-read
arguments.body:
DECEMBER 10 BOARD OPERATING SEGMENT — PRE-READ
Due: December 5, 2025

PAGE 1 OF 6 — OPENING FRAME

Decision frame
Four certified lanes are ready for the December 10 operating-segment discussion. They answer different questions and must not be blended into one growth, revenue, acquisition, or causal number:

1. Helio Start: bounded organic pricing-page motion, with mature day-90 operating evidence.
2. Retained-mid Expansion Assist: bounded exploratory evidence; descriptive, not causal.
3. Pricing-page path quality: randomized path-quality evidence for the organic pricing-page experience.
4. System controls: certified October decision-state and communication controls.

Board takeaways
- Priya’s decision is to keep Helio Start organic-only through March 31, 2026.
- Pricing-page path quality supports the bounded rollout decision, narrowly: better funnel handling and fewer unsupported-condition route-outs. It is not a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or blended-growth result.
- Expansion Assist remains an observation read. Its exposure and outcome counts do not establish incremental expansion causality.
- October system controls show the governed-state and suppression boundaries held in production-shadow operation.

All denominators below are stated at the metric’s own level; observation windows and exclusions are part of the result.

PAGE 2 OF 6 — HELIO START

Decision
Keep Helio Start as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026. Do not reopen paid acquisition before that boundary.

Mature packet
Owen and Customer Success certified the mature packet on December 2, 2025: 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 observation windows. At the fixed day-90 checkpoint:
- 61 paid-active (61/82)
- 11 canceled before day 90 (11/82)
- 6 past due (6/82)
- 4 on billing hold (4/82)

Definition and operating load
Activation is paid-active workspaces at the fixed day-90 checkpoint divided by admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. The mature 82-workspace packet’s account-level support p90 was 70 minutes. The earlier Q4 packet was separately reported as 68 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, median support effort 21 minutes, p90 72 minutes, and six accounts above 90 support minutes; those figures are not substituted for the 82-workspace mature packet.

Reopening condition
A capped paid-acquisition proposal may be reopened only after two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes. Paid-acquisition cohorts must remain separately identified from organic cohorts. Any later paid-acquisition proposal must also pair mature retention evidence with refund-adjusted cash evidence; this pre-read does not make that proposal.

Limits
This packet supports early activation, day-90 status, and setup/support-load decisions. It does not support general availability, pricing-page performance, revenue, retention beyond the stated checkpoint, or paid-acquisition economics.

PAGE 3 OF 6 — RETAINED-MID EXPANSION ASSIST

Decision and evidence posture
Keep Expansion Assist bounded and observational. The certified extract covers two bounded pilots and 43 actual retained-mid account exposures. Both pilots had closed, complete 45-day outcome windows as of December 1, 2025.

Certified descriptive read
- Actual exposures: 43
- Exposures with help-or-options requests: 13/43
- Exposures producing expansions: 9/43

The counts are descriptive and are reported separately from eligibility, prompt exposure, and Customer Success handoff. They do not compare treated accounts with a valid randomized holdout in this board read and do not establish that a prompt caused a help request or expansion. Not-yet-activated treatment accounts are not a causal baseline.

Outcome window and exposure limits
A help request or expansion is in-window only when its source event occurs from 0 through 45 x 24 elapsed hours after exposure, inclusive. Events before exposure or more than 45 x 24 elapsed hours after exposure are outside the approved 45-day count, though later commercial outcomes may remain visible as later outcomes. Exposure is capped at the approved operational maximum of three accounts per week. Exposure closed at the approved maximum; no further prompts are sent.

Context and exclusions
The first bounded pilot had 30 exposures; 18/30 had ceiling events older than 14 days. Seven of the eight help-or-options requests in that 30-exposure subset came from the 12 accounts whose product-visible usage ceiling had been crossed within the preceding 14 days. These are descriptive sequence facts, not causal claims. Track eligibility, suppressed/not-exposed/failed states, help requests, Customer Success handoffs, ceiling crossings, opportunities, expansion type/amount or seats, dates, active workflows, and observation-window end separately.

PAGE 4 OF 6 — PRICING-PAGE PATH QUALITY

Decision
The certified Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test supports the bounded pricing-page rollout decision. Interpret it as funnel/path quality, not as revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or blended-growth evidence.

Window and denominator
The four-cohort test ran October 20 through November 16, 2025, with the UI/layout freeze held through the stabilization window. Total denominator: 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions, split 1,639 control and 1,647 treatment. Eligible-workspace admission and unsupported-condition route-outs use eligible-flow starts as their denominators.

Cohort read (control / treatment)
- Oct 20–26: 781 sessions (389/392); starts 82/86; unsupported route-outs 9/82 = 11.0% and 7/86 = 8.1%; admission 43.9%/44.2%; support p90 70/73 minutes.
- Oct 27–Nov 2: 832 sessions (414/418); starts 87/89; unsupported route-outs 10/87 = 11.5% and 6/89 = 6.7%; admission 43.7%/44.0%; support p90 72/75 minutes.
- Nov 3–9: 817 sessions (408/409); starts 86/88; unsupported route-outs 9/86 = 10.5% and 6/88 = 6.8%; admission 43.8%/44.2%; support p90 71/74 minutes.
- Nov 10–16 stabilization: 856 sessions (428/428); starts 89/89; unsupported route-outs 10/89 = 11.2% and 6/89 = 6.7%.

Aggregate path-quality result
Across 344 control starts, 38 routed out for an existing unsupported condition (11.0%). Across 352 treatment starts, 25 routed out (7.1%): a 35.7% relative reduction. Aggregate admission completion was 44.0% control and 44.1% treatment. Direction was favorable across all three weekly cohorts and the stabilization cohort, and the predeclared path-quality threshold passed.

Limits
No revenue, acquisition, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, eligibility-change, or blended-growth claim follows from this test. Preserve eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing boundaries.

PAGE 5 OF 6 — SYSTEM CONTROLS

Certified evidence
Owen certified the October 1–31, 2025 Customer Success auto-nudge packet on November 5, 2025.

Denominator and result
- 1,026 unique decisions in the packet.
- 41 visible field-specific holds.
- 985 proceeded or were suppressed on current state (985/1,026).

Control checks
- No governed-field disagreement.
- No customer correction.
- No adjacent eligibility-assuming lifecycle message was sent to held or suppressed records.
- No rollback.

Interpretation and limits
This is system-control evidence: state visibility, hold/suppression behavior, governed-field integrity, and message separation. A proceed result authorizes only the governed action it covers; it does not authorize a later lifecycle message. The packet does not establish customer, revenue, acquisition, or growth outcomes.

PAGE 6 OF 6 — CLAIMS-AND-EXCLUSIONS MATRIX

Lane: Helio Start
Claim supported: bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026; mature day-90 status and support-load evidence from 82 admitted workspaces with complete windows.
Exclude: general availability; pricing-page performance; revenue; paid-acquisition CAC; broad retention; any paid-acquisition reopening before the stated boundary or without two consecutive mature cohorts each below 5% above 90 support minutes.

Lane: Retained-mid Expansion Assist
Claim supported: descriptive counts from 43 actual exposures across two bounded pilots, with complete 45-day windows; 13 help-or-options requests and 9 expansions.
Exclude: causal uplift; incremental expansion; treatment-versus-holdout conclusions from not-yet-activated treatment accounts; outcomes outside 0–45 x 24 elapsed hours in the primary count; blending eligibility, exposure, handoff, and outcome denominators.

Lane: Pricing-page path quality
Claim supported: across 3,286 organic sessions (1,639 control; 1,647 treatment), treatment had 25/352 unsupported-condition route-outs versus control 38/344; funnel/path-quality threshold passed.
Exclude: revenue, acquisition, paid acquisition, pipeline, forecast, eligibility change, or blended-growth interpretation; any change to eligibility/refusal/connector/external-authority/lifecycle/instrumentation/support-routing boundaries.

Lane: System controls
Claim supported: October 1–31 auto-nudge packet covered 1,026 unique decisions, with 41 visible holds and 985 proceeded/suppressed on current state; no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, adjacent lifecycle message to held/suppressed records, or rollback.
Exclude: treating a proceed result as authorization for another action or later lifecycle message; customer, revenue, acquisition, or growth claims.

Cross-section rule
Do not sum these lanes into a single growth number. Keep decision rows at their own denominator, and retain warnings, holds, checks, and reevaluations as linked audit history rather than extra decision rows.

Purpose

This is a delivery aid derived only from the finalized six-page pre-read delivered Friday. It is not a replacement evidence source and does not change the pre-read’s four lanes, denominators, complete outcome windows, or claims-and-exclusions matrix.

5:15–6:15 — Lane 4: System controls

HELIO START AUTHORITY DIAGNOSTIC — 2024 HISTORICAL METHOD CARD

Purpose and status

This method card records the bounded 2024 Helio Start authority diagnostic. It is a historical method record, not a current operating authorization. Every population, date, classification, measure, exclusion, and decision boundary below belonged to that 2024 diagnostic.

1. Historical question

The diagnostic tested whether separating customer-side access or authority blockers from product-guidance needs explained differences in elapsed resolution time and substantive repeat contacts. It was deliberately a mechanism-level diagnostic, not a broad onboarding rebuild, root-cause proof, attribution analysis, or growth study.

The accepted 52-workspace Helio Start cohort and its accepted day-90 status table remained the surrounding cohort context: 39 paid-active, 7 canceled, 4 past due, and 2 on billing hold. The eight-case diagnostic subset was not used to rewrite that accepted snapshot. Any later status change was to be treated as a subsequent event rather than retroactively changing the historical day-90 table.

2. Historical enrollment setup and window

- Priya approved the narrow prospective authority diagnostic on October 1, 2024, instead of an onboarding rebuild.
- Enrollment was the first 60 qualifying workspaces admitted from October 1 through October 28, 2024.
- The enrollment target was reached when HST-1060 became the 60th qualifying workspace, admitted October 25, 2024 at 8:17 AM. HST-1061, admitted at 8:42 AM, remained outside the diagnostic; its live routing was unchanged.
- The enrollment milestone did not itself complete the diagnostic. The 60 enrolled workspaces still required complete prospective support windows.
- A December 12, 2024 close was available only if all 60 workspaces had been enrolled by October 28 and their required evidence was complete. Otherwise, closure waited until every enrolled workspace had a complete 45-day support window.
- The diagnostic preserved the live admission, pending-state, and assisted-routing rules. Enrollment and observation added measurement only; they did not alter production eligibility or routing.

3. Historical prospective classification

Each enrolled workspace was classified prospectively as exactly one of the following top-level diagnostic categories:

- External access or authority: setup depended on a customer-side administrator, owner, parent-company identity administrator, approval, permission, or other authority outside Helio’s product guidance.
- Product guidance: the required connector authority or access was available, but the customer needed help understanding, mapping, configuring, or completing setup in the product.
- Mixed: the workspace had both components. Sequential blockers were retained in order and recorded as separate intervals—for example, external approval pending, approval resolved, then product guidance required. A later guidance interval did not overwrite an earlier authority interval, and a successful admission was not recoded as an admission failure.

The mixed category remained visible as its own category rather than being forced into either mechanism without evidence.

4. Historical support outcomes and counting rules

For each enrolled workspace, the diagnostic tracked:

- Resolution time: elapsed time from the first in-scope post-admission support contact to resolution, with the applicable historical time unit and timestamps retained.
- Substantive repeat contacts: qualifying human contact episodes after the initial case entry.
- Support minutes: in-scope post-admission product-support minutes.
- Workspace-level mechanism, first in-scope contact timestamp, resolution timestamp, and any sequential blocker intervals.

The historical repeat-contact rule counted one episode for a contiguous human exchange. A repeat required a customer or agent to add a new substantive contact after the initial case entry—for example, a new question, request, evidence, problem, action-requiring follow-up, workaround, material status update, call, or meeting that advanced the case.

The historical rule excluded automated receipt or acknowledgment messages; bot, routing, assignment, and status notifications; retry-generated duplicates; internal notes; QA events; CSAT requests; agent messages that merely repeated an automated acknowledgment; and multiple messages within the same unresolved exchange. The two QA-flagged events in the original eight cases were automated acknowledgments and were therefore excluded.

Pre-admission connector assistance and billing contacts were outside the historical support-minute, resolution-time, and repeat-contact measures.

5. Historical starting evidence: the original eight cases

The original retrospective mechanism pass covered eight high-effort workspaces and 472 post-admission product-support minutes:

- External access or authority: 4 workspaces, 238 minutes, 4.0 business days median resolution, and 8 substantive repeat contacts.
- Product guidance: 3 workspaces, 174 minutes, 1.6 days median resolution, and 4 substantive repeat contacts.
- Mixed data import: 1 workspace, 60 minutes, 2.7 days resolution, and 3 substantive repeat contacts.

These figures were descriptive evidence for designing the prospective diagnostic. Minutes, resolution differences, and repeat-contact differences were not treated as proof of causality or as evidence that authority was the sole root cause.

6. Historical completion rule

The diagnostic was complete only after the enrolled population satisfied the approved enrollment condition and every enrolled workspace had a complete 45-day support window, with the agreed classifications and outcome fields available for review. The December 12, 2024 date was a conditional close date, not an unconditional deadline: it applied only when the cohort reached 60 by October 28 and the required observation evidence was complete. If that condition was not met, the close moved until all enrolled workspaces had complete 45-day windows.

Completion also required preserving workspace-level evidence, keeping the mixed cases separate, applying the finalized substantive-contact rule, and reporting the result as descriptive unless the available evidence supported a stronger design. The diagnostic did not permit excluded pre-admission or billing activity to be pooled into the comparison.

7. Historical operating implications

What the original eight cases did justify, within the 2024 diagnostic

- A bounded prospective authority diagnostic rather than an immediate broad onboarding rebuild.
- Prospective mechanism labels that separated external access or authority, product guidance, and mixed cases.
- Explicit tracking of resolution time, substantive repeat contacts, support minutes, and sequential blocker intervals.
- A standardized repeat-contact rule that excluded automated acknowledgments and other system-generated events.
- Retaining the accepted 52-workspace cohort and day-90 status table unchanged while testing the mechanism question in a separate eight-case subset.
- Keeping pre-admission connector assistance and billing contacts outside the historical support comparison.

What the original eight cases did not justify

- No causal claim that authority problems caused Helio Start onboarding to be slow.
- No conclusion that the 4.0-business-day authority median proved a dedicated-support or staffing requirement.
- No dedicated coverage, staffing increase, intake change, lifecycle-email change, routing change, admission-rule change, or pending-state change.
- No broad onboarding rebuild or product-wide operating change.
- No change to live assisted routing or production eligibility behavior.
- No CAC, paid-channel, pipeline, forecast, revenue, or growth claim.
- No recoding of mixed cases into a single mechanism merely to make the comparison cleaner.
- No replacement or revision of the accepted 52-workspace day-90 snapshot.

The historical operating conclusion was therefore narrow: the eight cases justified measuring the mechanisms prospectively and waiting for bounded evidence; they did not authorize changing intake, lifecycle, routing, staffing, admission, pending-state behavior, or broad onboarding operations.

8. Reuse guardrail

If this method card is reused, its 2024 population, dates, denominators, 45-day window, categories, exclusions, and operating limits must be treated as historical attributes of the original diagnostic—not as current defaults or standing authority. Any new study would require its own explicit approval, cohort definition, observation window, completion rule, and operating decision boundary.

arguments.body:
Helio Start bounded paid-search proposal — October 2027 working draft

COMPLETED PROPOSAL — DECISION AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARY

This document is the completed proposal for one bounded, high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch. It is submitted for separate decision; it is not approval. No budget, batch, paid traffic, production change, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or launch is authorized by this document. Paid traffic remains off unless and until the required decisions and launch checks are separately recorded.

1. Proposal objective and scope

Evaluate one high-intent paid-search batch under the fixed bounds, safeguards, staffing assumptions, measurement limits, and approval gates below. The proposal covers only the proposed batch. It authorizes no later or additional paid batch and does not change eligibility, routing, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, suppression, freshness, handoff, or owner-authority rules.

2. Certified evidence and claim boundary

Certified Q2 2027 mature descriptive evidence covers a fixed cohort of 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 2027, with complete day-90 windows:

- Customer Success certified 18 of 25 paid-active; 3 canceled; 2 past due; and 2 on billing hold.
- Owen certified $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Customer Success certified account-level support effort of 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; 5 of 25 workspaces exceeded 90 minutes.
- Daniela certified paid-source attribution for all 61 paid-source starts, with no unsupported applicant entering the admitted path, and certified the source as reliable.
- Ines certified that no lifecycle hold or suppression was bypassed.

This evidence is descriptive evidence from a fixed cohort. It supports reporting the observed cohort outcomes and an operational support signal. It does not establish causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue or forecast impact beyond the stated collected-cash record, or that an owner checklist causes improved support. The cohort had no randomized comparison.

The prior bounded execution record is distinct: its approved test budget cap was $8,000, certified final paid-search spend was $7,640, the vendor invoice was paid in full with zero balance and $0 taxes/fees, service ran April 12–May 17, 2027, and the fixed test cohort closed at 25 admitted workspaces across 61 starts (25 admitted, 18 assisted, 18 ineligible). Traffic is off and no later batch was authorized. The prior spend, cap, staffing reference, and this proposal do not create current authority.

3. Certified nonproduction preflight and staffed design

Daniela and Ines certified a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight consisting of 8 expected admissions, 8 expected assisted routes, and 8 expected fail-closed, held, or suppressed outcomes. Certification covered paid-source final-route attribution; governed-state meanings; lifecycle branches, holds, and suppression; setup-step exposure; coordination ownership and backup behavior; handoff; after-hours handling; and continuous account-level support-minute treatment. All expected routes, attribution, holds/suppressions, ownership, support clock, handoff, and support-minute behavior matched design.

This is nonproduction evidence. It does not authorize traffic, a batch, a budget, production connection, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, an eligibility/routing/ownership change, or a later launch. Any eventual run requires a fresh evaluation; prior preflight outcomes must not be reused as a substitute for current admission decisions.

Customer Success coordination assumptions for the proposed fixed cohort:

- Primary owner: Customer Success setup desk.
- Backup: on-duty Customer Success manager.
- Coverage: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central.
- After-hours cases queue to the named backup at the next service opening.
- Handoff begins when an admitted workspace needs owner action after admission.
- Handoff context includes connector, authority state, required action, route, first-contact time, and notes.
- Initial response target: within two business hours.
- Customer Success lead escalates if no owner accepts within the response window.
- Account-level support minutes continue from first contact; handoff and after-hours treatment do not reset the clock.

These assumptions describe coordination readiness only. They are not evidence of paid-growth capacity beyond the stated operating bound, causal lift, revenue, pipeline, or forecast impact.

4. Proposed budget, admission bound, and run-close rule

- Proposed budget ceiling: no more than $8,000 in paid-search spend, inclusive of applicable media costs and any directly attributable fees.
- Proposed admission bound: no more than 25 admitted workspaces.
- Run-close rule: close the batch at the earlier of the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces.
- The batch is one high-intent paid-search batch only; no automatic extension, replenishment, or second batch is included.
- Spend pacing, admission definition, and exception handling must be recorded by the acquisition/operating owner before launch. An admitted workspace is one that passes the current, fresh eligibility and routing evaluation and enters the admitted path; assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed routes are not silently counted as admissions.

These are proposed bounds for Priya’s decision, not approved budget or traffic authority.

5. Stop and pause conditions

Hard stop:

- If an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path, stop the batch immediately and keep paid traffic off pending incident review, correction, and an explicit restart decision.
- Close the batch when either the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces is reached, whichever occurs first.

Pause:

- Pause if paid-source reconciliation cannot be completed from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- After at least 10 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes.
- Pause for any material attribution discrepancy, lifecycle or suppression bypass, unresolved governed-state conflict, missing/stale required state, routing disagreement, or failure of the staffed handoff/support-clock design.

A pause keeps paid traffic off until the responsible owner documents the issue, correction, validation, and restart decision. A template-only override is not a correction. Restart requires fresh evaluation and explicit owner confirmation; prior preflight or shadow outcomes cannot substitute for current decisions.

6. Attribution, lifecycle, and operational safeguards

Any approved run must preserve all of the following:

- Reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- Evaluate every candidate from current authoritative state; do not reuse prior shadow or preflight outcomes.
- Keep existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules unchanged unless separately approved by the relevant owner.
- Keep governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, suppressions, routing, freshness, and handoff semantics unchanged.
- Hold missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state visibly and fail-closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.
- Suppress candidates with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- Do not create a production connection, customer-facing activation, or additional production consumer without separate release approval.
- Measure account-level support minutes continuously from first contact, including handoff and after-hours treatment.
- Hold affected records until authoritative correction is completed, validated, and documented.
- Give any unaffected audience its own complete preflight.
- Keep attribution, lifecycle, support, and outcome reporting separate from pipeline and forecast treatment unless Marcus Vail makes a separate explicit decision.

7. Measurement and claim limits

The operating record for this batch must include spend, admitted/assisted/ineligible/held/suppressed counts, paid-source reconciliation through final route, support minutes from first contact, stop/pause events, and owner-certified corrections. Paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort for the proposed fixed cohort are not mature claims until that cohort has complete day-90 windows.

Permitted current claims are limited to the certified historical evidence, the certified nonproduction preflight, and the stated Customer Success coordination design. Do not claim that the proposed batch or current evidence proves causal lift, scalable acquisition, mature customer outcomes, revenue, paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, pipeline, forecast impact, or general paid-growth capacity. Mature claims must wait for complete day-90 windows and owner certification. No randomized control exists for the cited historical cohort.

8. Decision owners and approvals

- Riley: final operating claims and claim boundaries; customer-action scope; bounded customer corrections; incident-stop decisions; disputed-semantics decisions; and board-readiness judgment.
- Priya: separate decision on whether to approve the proposed budget ceiling and one-batch operating bounds on October 16. The scheduled review is not advance approval.
- Daniela: source and release reliability; instrumentation and engineering-control evidence; separate production release and launch check; rollback approval and execution; and engineering incident-stop execution.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance authority for eligibility, routing, suppression, holds, freshness, and handoff semantics.
- Customer Success setup desk/on-duty manager: staffed coordination execution within the approved operating design, if a later run is separately approved.
- Marcus Vail: any pipeline treatment or forecast credit; none follows automatically from this proposal.
- Tomás: any final board-narrative treatment; no narrative expansion follows automatically.
- Owen: routine source-readiness/source-completeness lane only; source readiness is not claim approval, production approval, paid-traffic authorization, or forecast judgment.

9. Required decision record before any launch

Before any launch, the record must explicitly contain:

- Priya’s decision on the budget ceiling, one-batch scope, admission bound, and close rule.
- Riley’s approval of final operating claims and customer-action scope.
- Daniela’s separate launch check and, if applicable, production release and rollback approvals.
- Ines’s confirmation of final eligibility, routing, suppression, hold, freshness, and handoff semantics.
- Measurement-owner certification of the attribution, outcome metric, observation window, and reconciliation/reporting plan.
- Named acquisition/operating owner confirmation of pacing, admission definition, stop/pause authority, escalation, and restart rules.
- Any separate Marcus Vail decision on pipeline or forecast treatment; absent that decision, there is none.
- Any separate Tomás decision on board narrative; absent that decision, there is no narrative expansion.

No meeting invitation, evidence certification, staffing readiness, or source-readiness check silently transfers or expands authority.

10. Final recommendation

Recommendation for Priya’s October 16 review: consider approving, but do not assume approval of, one high-intent paid-search batch bounded at no more than $8,000 or 25 admitted workspaces, whichever comes first, with the hard stop, pause conditions, attribution reconciliation, fresh-evaluation, lifecycle, staffing, support-clock, measurement, and claim limits in this proposal.

Even if Priya approves the budget and batch bounds, paid traffic remains off until the required owner decisions are recorded and Daniela completes the separate launch check. No pipeline target or treatment, forecast credit, production change, customer-facing activation, or later paid batch is included. The proposal therefore recommends a conditional, separately gated decision—not immediate launch or implied approval.

NO-AUTHORIZATION STATEMENT

This completed proposal records a bounded request for decision. It authorizes no spend, paid traffic, batch, production change, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, or launch. Any execution requires the separate approvals and Daniela launch check stated above.

- Presentation-detail reconciliation: reconcile labels, links, counts, formatting, and source references against approved material; surface discrepancies rather than deciding disputed meaning.
- Administrative upkeep directly necessary to maintain these artifacts, provided it does not expand access, authority, or shared-state consumption.

Categorical exclusions
The contractor must not:
- Change, define, or reinterpret state meanings, reporting semantics, analytical conclusions, or governed fields.
- Resolve, adjudicate, or close disputed semantics or exceptions.
- Receive production-write, deployment, engineering release, rollback, or equivalent privileged access.
- Perform release work or change production behavior.
- Add a fifth shared-state consumer or create a parallel governed-state workflow.
- Replace Owen's reporting-semantics or analytical-conclusions lane; Ines's message-state-governance lane; Riley's exception or disputed-semantics authority; or Daniela's engineering release and rollback control.
- Conduct Helio Start paid acquisition or unrelated growth execution.
- Make customer-facing commitments, approve governed messaging, independently publish decisions, or sign off on governed reviews, decisions, exceptions, disputed semantics, or owner acceptance.
- Turn undocumented system knowledge into de facto ownership; all work remains reviewable, transferable, and bounded.

Finalist evidence from September 12 interviews
Candidate A
- Worked through a sample campaign export and found a duplicate inventory row, providing direct evidence of attention to inventory accuracy and discrepancy detection.
- Kept evidence preparation separate from owner approval, providing direct evidence of understanding the execution-versus-authority boundary.
- Described a credible first-month Customer.io learning plan, which is positive evidence of a structured approach to adapting to lifecycle tooling but is not yet evidence of demonstrated Customer.io execution.
- Remaining evidence gap: reference-confirmed ability to learn and use unfamiliar lifecycle tooling accurately, maintain durable documentation, escalate ambiguity, and sustain owner-review boundaries in live work.

Candidate C
- Correctly rebuilt a unique-decision denominator from a sample containing reevaluations, providing direct evidence of disciplined denominator treatment and distinction between decisions and linked reevaluations.
- Proposed a strong rework-tracking approach, providing direct evidence of measurement and correction discipline.
- Was less specific than A about adapting to lifecycle tooling, leaving an evidence gap on practical tool learning and campaign/message inventory execution.
- Remaining evidence gap: reference-confirmed ability to translate strong measurement/rework discipline into lifecycle-tool workflows while preserving the same boundary adherence and documentation quality.

Evidence-based reference-check priority
This is a reference-check sequence, not a hiring ranking or selection decision. Do not infer a final preference until references return and are reviewed.

1. Candidate A — first reference-check priority.
   Basis: A's interview evidence covers two immediate execution risks: detecting a concrete inventory defect and separating evidence preparation from owner approval. A also articulated a credible Customer.io learning plan. The highest-value unresolved question is whether that plan reflects demonstrated ability to learn and operate unfamiliar lifecycle tooling accurately and durably, rather than only a plausible plan. Check this first because it can validate or materially weaken A's strongest remaining uncertainty.

2. Candidate C — second reference-check priority.
   Basis: C has stronger direct interview evidence on unique-decision denominator handling and rework measurement, but less specific evidence on adapting to lifecycle tooling. The reference check should test whether C can carry that discipline into campaign/message inventory and routine tool operations without becoming an unauthorized owner. C remains fully active in the process; second priority does not mean lower selection status.

messages.content:
Ines — this is useful, especially the parts where we can reuse existing product-event email patterns. To keep the map moving without rewriting copy that may be excluded later, let’s triage the branches this way:

1. Safe to adapt now

Please continue adapting existing product-event emails when the message:

- Is triggered by a reliable product event we already use.
- Gives standard product guidance or a self-serve next step.
- Does not assume a particular account type, team structure, CSM assignment, or support entitlement.
- Does not imply a Helio Start launch date or broader availability.
- Can use the existing CTA pattern, such as connecting an integration, completing setup, or returning to the product.

For these, preserve the existing trigger and eligibility behavior where possible. We can refine wording later without reopening the operating model.

2. Depends on eligibility or support policy

Please leave the copy structure in place, but mark these branches as policy-dependent rather than rewriting them:

- Import stalled or failed.
- Billing mismatch or payment-related issues.
- Accounts that may or may not qualify for Helio Start.
- Whether a user has an assigned CSM, implementation lead, or other named contact.
- Whether single-team accounts should receive team-invite or multi-team messaging.
- Webinar, live onboarding, or other assisted-help CTAs.
- Any path where the action differs for sub-50-seat accounts versus other segments.

For each one, annotate the open decision we need: eligible population, support owner, allowed channel, response expectation, and fallback if the user is not eligible. The measurement table should state the eligibility and deployment shape explicitly, including the sub-50-seat threshold.

3. Do not touch until the boundaries are decided

Please do not finalize or adapt copy that creates a new support promise, including:

- “Offer live CS help.”
- “Reply to your CSM.”
- Promises of implementation or one-to-one onboarding.
- Any implied response-time or guaranteed human follow-up.
- Routing users to a named support role they may not have.
- Billing escalation language that assumes ownership or resolution authority.
- Any branch that requires a new support workflow, staffing commitment, or exception process.

For those, a placeholder such as “[support path pending policy]” is preferable to polished copy.

For the next pass, could you convert the map into the triage table with columns for trigger, eligibility, message/CTA, support implication, and open decision? That lets us keep the safe adaptations moving while making the unresolved boundaries visible, without spending time polishing branches we may remove.

Helio Start field-handling quick reference
Effective: 2028-01-01

Keep these readiness states separate

- External-authority readiness: the applicant or an available owner can perform the selected connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action.
  - Record: Daniela records this as a separate state.
  - Pending handling: Ines withholds setup prompts/messaging while this state is pending.
  - Reporting: Owen reports external-authority readiness and its support effects separately.

- Helio admin proof: evidence that the applicant satisfies the existing administrator-proof requirement.
  - Do not treat it as proof of external authority.

- Connector authentication: successful authentication/connection of the selected connector under the existing connector requirements.
  - Do not treat it as proof of external authority or admin proof.

Also preserve the existing entitlement, billing, and deployment requirements; none is interchangeable with the three states above.

Field handling

- Verified “yes” for external-authority readiness: continue through the existing admission flow, subject to all other current requirements.
- “No,” “not sure,” missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting external-authority state: route to Customer Success before admission, keep setup messaging withheld, and fail closed pending fresh authoritative confirmation.
- Do not manually release a setup prompt, apply a report-level/template override, or relabel a record to make the states agree.
- Once the authoritative state is corrected and validated, rerun the normal fresh eligibility and messaging checks. Do not rewrite existing admission measures.

Reporting rule

Report pending external-authority cases separately from admitted workspaces and separately from admin-proof or connector-authentication results. Keep the source state, downstream view, timestamps, route, and support effects visible.

arguments.body:
WORKING BRIEF

Purpose
Prepare a ten-minute operating case for Growth leadership, followed by ten minutes of questions. The case explains what the shared state contract solved, how its five governed fields work, and how the September 24 authority decision improved handoffs without expanding scope or release authority.

CORE THESIS
The problem was not simply whether a lifecycle action could be sent. The operating problem was that several systems and teams could hold different, incomplete, or differently interpreted views of whether the prerequisites for an action were satisfied. That made handoffs ambiguous and made it difficult to tell whether a blocked action reflected missing evidence, a stale record, an unresolved transition, a semantic disagreement, or an ownership question.

The shared state contract solved this by making the required state explicit, separately governed, and inspectable field by field. Each field has its own authority and status. If a required field is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting, the decision fails closed as a visible, field-specific hold—not as an invisible best effort and not as a blanket failure of delivery.

THE FIVE SEPARATELY GOVERNED FIELDS
1. External-system authority
   Is the relevant external system, account, or operator relationship authoritative for this decision? If authority is absent, stale, disputed, or not established, hold on this field.

2. Connector authentication
   Is the connector authenticated and usable for the relevant operation? Missing, expired, invalid, or unresolved authentication produces a connector-authentication hold.

3. Entitlement
   Is the customer or workspace entitled to the relevant capability or treatment? Missing, stale, transitional, or conflicting entitlement produces an entitlement hold.

4. Qualifying-human-admin status
   Is there a qualifying human administrator whose status satisfies the operating requirement? Missing, stale, unverified, or conflicting administrator state produces a qualifying-human-admin hold.

5. Active Customer Success adoption or renewal work
   Is there active CS adoption or renewal work that must be respected before the action proceeds? Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting work state produces an active-CS-work hold.

CONTROL BEHAVIOR
A required field does not silently default to proceed. A field-specific hold identifies the exact missing or disputed prerequisite and preserves the issue for review. Holds are visible controls: they prevent an action from crossing a known uncertainty boundary while keeping the decision auditable and actionable.

LOCKED Q3 PROOF POINTS
Use only these proof points in the presentation:
- 1,362 unique CS auto-nudge decisions.
- 57 field-specific holds.
- No governed-field disagreement.
- No customer correction.
- One bounded pre-breach intervention.

Evidence limits to say aloud: These points show that the contract and handoff model produced observable field-level decisions and holds in the measured Q3 set. They do not, by themselves, establish causality, broad operational impact, or mature reliability. The single pre-breach intervention is bounded evidence of one intervention, not a reliability-rate claim or proof that the contract caused the outcome. Do not add an implied denominator, uplift, avoided-loss estimate, or generalized customer result.

SEPTEMBER 24 AUTHORITY DECISION: HANDOFF IMPROVEMENT
The decision clarified who can close which class of work:
- Ines independently closes only routine Customer Success auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and owns related routine operator guidance.
- Owen retains routine operating explanation and the exception ledger.
- Riley retains disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing matters, ambiguous matters, exception-heavy matters, and executive claims.
- Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control.

What this improved: routine messaging-state review and operator guidance can close with a defined owner, while interpretation, exceptions, customer-impacting corrections, incident controls, executive claims, and engineering release decisions remain with the appropriate authority. The handoff is narrower and clearer—not a general delegation of the Lifecycle Systems operating surface.

NON-EXPANSION GUARDRAILS
The September 24 decision did not:
- grant Ines authority over Helio Start reporting;
- grant Ines authority over Expansion Assist selection;
- grant Ines authority over lifecycle preflight;
- change lifecycle-send release authority;
- broaden Lifecycle Systems beyond its four existing consumers.

TEN-MINUTE PRESENTATION RUN OF SHOW
0:00–1:00 — Opening and operating problem
State the problem as shared-state ambiguity across systems and teams, not as a messaging-volume problem. Explain that the question is whether the required prerequisites are known, current, and owned.

1:00–3:00 — What the shared state contract changed
Describe the contract as explicit, field-level prerequisites with visible fail-closed behavior. Contrast a visible field-specific hold with an implicit default or an undiagnosed handoff failure.

3:00–6:00 — Five governed fields
Spend roughly 20–25 seconds per field: authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin status, and active CS adoption or renewal work. For each, name the field owner/authority concept and the hold condition; do not collapse them into one generalized readiness flag.

6:00–7:30 — Q3 evidence, carefully bounded
Read the five locked proof points. Then state the evidence limit: these demonstrate observed control behavior in the measured set; they do not establish causality or mature reliability. Mention the one bounded pre-breach intervention only in that qualified way.

7:30–9:00 — September 24 handoff decision
Explain the four authority lanes: Ines for routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and routine operator guidance; Owen for routine operating explanation and the exception ledger; Riley for disputed, cross-surface, customer-correction, incident-stop, state-changing, ambiguous, exception-heavy, and executive-claim matters; Daniela for engineering release and rollback.

9:00–10:00 — Scope boundary and close
Say explicitly that the decision did not extend Ines's authority to Helio Start reporting, Expansion Assist selection, or lifecycle preflight; did not change lifecycle-send release authority; and did not expand Lifecycle Systems beyond its four existing consumers. Close with: clearer ownership makes routine handoffs faster without converting a proceed decision into blanket permission or moving authority across surfaces.

LIKELY QUESTIONS AND RESERVED ANSWERS
Q: Why are holds controls rather than delivery failures?
A: A hold is the intended fail-closed response when a required field is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting. It prevents an action from proceeding on an unverified prerequisite and exposes exactly what needs resolution. Calling it a delivery failure would confuse a deliberate safety boundary with an incident or a missed send. It may delay delivery, but its operating purpose is control integrity.

Q: Why does the September 24 decision not extend across all four consumers?
A: The decision assigned a narrow authority lane for routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and related routine operator guidance. The other consumers carry different reporting, selection, preflight, or release consequences. Extending the delegation would change semantics, cross-surface ownership, or release control, so it was intentionally out of scope. Lifecycle Systems remains bounded to its four existing consumers.

Q: Why is a proceed result not blanket contact permission?
A: Proceed means the required governed fields satisfied the contract for that specific decision and scope. It does not erase channel, audience, consent, suppression, timing, or other controls, and it does not grant authority to contact every customer or use every consumer. A proceed result is a bounded decision outcome, not a universal permission.

Q: Does zero governed-field disagreement prove the system is reliable?
A: No. It is a locked observation from the measured Q3 set. It supports that no disagreement was observed there; it does not establish mature reliability, causal impact, or performance outside that set.

Q: What does the one pre-breach intervention prove?
A: Only that one bounded intervention occurred before a breach in the observed evidence. It is not enough to estimate an intervention rate, prove prevention, or claim that the contract caused the result.

CLOSE
The operating case is disciplined delegation around explicit state: five separately governed fields, visible field-specific holds, a narrower and clearer September 24 handoff, and no expansion of consumer or release authority. The value is not a blanket proceed signal; it is a shared, auditable basis for deciding when to proceed and when to stop.

Measurement and evidence limits

Each scheduled decision appears once in the unique-decision denominator. Warnings, holds, fresh checks, interventions, corrections, and reevaluations remain linked history; they are not extra decision rows. A warning is not a hold unless a separate hold action occurred, and a scheduled decision is never counted both as an alert and as an additional hold or decision. The package does not establish causal lift, universal reliability, or that a source-age alert was deployed, live, delivered, evaluated, or effective. No governed-field disagreement or customer correction was identified in the locked readout. September 24 final authority decision

Q3 LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS — ROLE REFERENCE

Purpose
Compact operating reference for the Q3 Lifecycle Systems team. This is role clarity, not a new launch plan.

Current status
- CS auto-nudge migration: COMPLETE. The shared-state contract is the sole production path; the legacy path is engineering rollback-only.
- Helio Start: bounded GA already in place.
- Scope: FOUR production consumers. No new launch and no fifth-consumer proposal.

Ownership lanes

Owen — routine reporting, exception ledger, reporting semantics, and operating explanation
- Owns routine single-path reporting, denominator/ledger integrity, the routine exception ledger, and explanations of ordinary exceptions.
- Keeps reporting aligned to governed meanings without changing decision semantics.

Ines — routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state review and routine operator guidance
- Independently closes routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and owns routine operator guidance without Riley’s line-by-line approval.
- A review is routine only when all five governed fields retain their established meanings and current, consistent state, the messaging and nudge views agree, and there is no customer-correction, incident-stop, state-changing, ambiguous, exception-heavy, or disputed-semantics issue.
- Stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state creates a visible field-specific hold.
- Current active Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses the nudge under the shared contract; this is not discretionary closure by Ines.
- Escalates anything outside the routine criteria to Riley. Readiness or external-system authority is not blanket permission to contact.
- No engineering release-control access. No closure authority across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, or lifecycle preflight; no change to lifecycle-send release limits.

Daniela — transport, source reliability, release control, and rollback
- Owns transport health, source reliability, freshness/availability controls, production release and deployment/configuration control, and rollback readiness/execution.
- Maintains the boundary between the shared-state production path and the legacy engineering rollback path.

Riley — escalated interpretation and consequential decisions

- Decides when ambiguity, conflicting state, customer impact, or another excluded condition requires escalation or a stop.

Operating shorthand
- Suppressed = current active CS adoption or renewal work; no nudge under the shared contract.
- Held = missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state pauses the decision with a visible field-specific hold.
- Proceed = required state is current, consistent, and supported; it is not blanket permission for contact.
- Routine = all five governed fields preserve their meanings and current consistent state, messaging and nudge views agree, and no excluded condition is present.

The September 24 decision applies only to routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state review and guidance. It does not expand authority to Helio Start, Expansion Assist, or lifecycle preflight; change Ines’s lifecycle-send release limits; add a fifth consumer; expand the four-consumer scope; or change engineering release, stop, or rollback control. arguments.body:
Evidence bank — year-end first-draft expansion

The clearest evidence of my 2027 contribution is not a broad growth claim; it is the bounded Helio Start proposal and the claim discipline I owned around it. I translated the opportunity into a controlled paid-search batch with explicit attribution safeguards, pause and stop conditions, and staffing and support-clock requirements. I also set the evidence boundary before launch: operating activity could be reported descriptively, but the new batch could not support mature customer-outcome claims until the fixed cohort had complete day-90 observation windows. I did not treat launch authorization as proof of effectiveness, and I did not authorize an additional paid batch by implication.

I own the proposal, the operating limits, and the language of the claims. Priya deserves explicit credit for approving the batch and the high-intent paid-search traffic. Daniela deserves explicit credit for the final November 1 launch authorization and for verifying the live enable control. Those approvals were essential to execution, but they are distinct from my ownership of the bounded design, attribution guardrails, stop conditions, support coverage requirements, and evidence limits.

The current paid batch should be described as live operational work, not mature evidence. The November 10 support-monitor evaluation recorded 23 paid-source eligibility-flow starts; attribution reconciled for all 23, with 7 reaching the assisted route and 10 reaching the admitted route. These are useful operating observations about routing and instrumentation. They are not a mature outcome read, not a causal acquisition result, and not evidence of downstream retention, revenue, or scale. The fixed cohort still needs complete day-90 windows before those claims can be considered.

Four-lane year-end evidence framing

1. Helio Start customer outcomes. This lane covers the bounded proposal, admissions, activation and downstream outcome windows, with paid-source attribution kept separate from outcome interpretation. My exclusions are explicit: no mature outcome claim for the November batch before complete day-90 windows; no causal, revenue, pipeline, acquisition-efficiency, scale, or forecast claim from live-batch counts; and no assumption that admitted or assisted routing is equivalent to successful customer value.

2. Expansion Assist. This remains a distinct lane from Helio Start setup and lifecycle work. The framing is limited to the certified source, denominator, outcome-window, and operating evidence actually available. I exclude combining Expansion Assist with Helio Start to create a larger or cleaner-looking result, and I exclude unsupported causal or business-impact claims where the source only supports descriptive operating facts.

3. Pricing-page path quality. This lane is about path quality and unsupported-path starts, not a general conversion or growth claim. I exclude treating path-quality continuity as proof of incremental revenue, pipeline, acquisition performance, or causal lift. Any conclusion must preserve the applicable denominator, period, and the distinction between a cleaner route and a downstream customer outcome.

4. System controls and reliability. This lane covers governed-state consumption, send or suppress behavior, source integrity, release controls, rollback readiness, and exception handling. I exclude turning reliable control behavior into a claim of customer or financial impact without a separate outcome source. I also keep release readiness, operational safety, and message-state correctness visibly separate from the three customer or path-quality lanes.

This four-lane framing is also an exclusion mechanism: each lane keeps its own owner, denominator, source completeness, outcome window, reliability evidence, and unresolved gaps. I do not fill a missing field in one lane with a result from another, and I do not convert an operational checkpoint into a closed year-end conclusion.

Delegated evidence and operating leadership

Owen's work strengthened the measurement layer behind the claims. He owned the denominator and measurement work, normalized what counted in each read, checked source completeness, and reconciled exceptions rather than allowing them to disappear into an aggregate. His exception synthesis distinguishes missing required input from other exception categories, and routine source-completeness closure depends on the required named-owner certifications and the absence of a disputed semantic or cross-surface discrepancy. This is an important example of leadership through delegation: I retained the final claim and exclusion decisions while Owen made the underlying evidence more auditable and decision-ready.

Owen's October–December Q4 development focus remains open through the December cycle. The November synthesis is evidence of progress, not permission to mark the focus complete early. The remaining assessment should use the required December cycle and preserve the same standards for denominator clarity, source completeness, and exception classification.

Ines strengthened lifecycle governance and message-state consumption. Her lane covers state transitions, routine-send controls, governed lifecycle interpretation, and audits within the established operating ceiling. The operating rule is fail closed when required state is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting: a record is held rather than treated as queued delivery, and every possible display receives a fresh evaluation under the current governed state. This is the control logic that keeps a lifecycle message from outrunning the state it is supposed to represent.

The incomplete-setup reminder is the fifth production consumer of the shared-state feed, not a sixth consumer. In the November 1–7 operating read, the fully released reminder had 12,480 fresh evaluations, including 186 evaluations held because required state was missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting. Those figures are evidence of the control operating as designed, not a claim of customer impact. The reminder's behavior belongs in the shared-state and reliability framing: it consumes governed state, can be placed on hold, and must be re-evaluated after state changes. It should not be counted as an unrelated extra system or used to inflate a customer-outcome result.

Ines's October–December Q4 development focus also remains open through the December cycle. Her demonstrated lifecycle-risk explanations and state-governance work are meaningful progress, but they do not close the development focus before the required December review. I will keep that assessment open rather than turning partial-cycle evidence into a completion claim.

Daniela's evidence covers source reliability, engineering release control, source-integrity validation, production enablement, rollback readiness, and incident-stop execution. That work made the bounded launch operable and gave the team a safe way to stop or reverse it if the source, release, or operating conditions failed. Her November 1 authorization is therefore part of the launch record, while the resulting paid-batch activity remains operational evidence pending the outcome window. I credit her for the reliability, release, and rollback work without attributing those engineering controls to mature customer or business results.

Year-end claim discipline

My role this year was to connect growth proposals to an evidence system without letting urgency erase the boundaries. The strongest version of the self-review should say that I created a bounded path to learn, secured the necessary approvals, and kept the language proportional to what the data can currently support. It should credit Priya, Daniela, Owen, and Ines for their distinct contributions; preserve the four lanes and their exclusions; call the paid batch live operational work rather than mature evidence; and leave Owen's and Ines's Q4 development focuses open through the December cycle.

SEPTEMBER 2027 LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS OPERATING PRIORITIES
For Priya’s September 2 staff review

Decision frame
September is a control-and-evidence month, not a paid-growth expansion month. Keep paid traffic off. No second Q3 Helio Start batch is authorized. The audited descriptive claim remains limited to 25 paid customers acquired April 12–May 17 and $27,860 in revenue; do not say the paid motion proved to scale. 1. Helio Start
Scope: paid-source and operating-control evidence for Helio Start, kept descriptive and separate from lifecycle-governance decisions.
- Riley: final operating claim, claim boundaries, correction decisions, disputed-semantics decisions, and board-readiness decisions.
- Owen: routine monthly source-readiness and source-cycle work; named owners, certified-through dates, certification ETAs, freshness limits, visible incompleteness when certification is missing, and fail-closed handling.

- Riley: final operating claim and reconciliation of separate views and denominators.
- Owen: certified evidence extract, cohort dates, coverage/window metadata, and routine completeness review.

- Daniela: source and release-reliability evidence.

4. CS auto-nudge system controls
Scope: system-control performance, coverage, reliability, and governed execution—not customer response or causal lift.
- Riley: final operating claim; keep control performance separate from customer-outcome evidence.
- Daniela: control coverage, source/release reliability, engineering release and rollback control, cross-surface reliability gaps, and incident-stop execution.
- Engineering / control source owner: control logs, population and coverage basis, exact coverage dates, source freshness, exception treatment, and named-owner confirmation where not assigned.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance limits when control behavior touches eligibility, suppression, routing, or handoff.

OPERATING BOUNDARIES

1. Preserve the routine source-cycle lane
Owen continues the monthly source-readiness and source-cycle process in his routine lane. Riley does not take over routine closure, and Owen’s packet closure is not claim approval, board-readiness approval, causal/revenue/forecast judgment, or authorization for paid traffic or another batch.

2. Growth reminder: nonproduction only
Treat the incomplete-setup reminder as nonproduction work only. Historical replay and any bounded shadow must use replayed/offline data, remain isolated from production and live state, and create no customer exposure, display/send, dispatch, routing, recommendation, write, or other production-side effect.

3. Keep Customer Success coordination design separate from the later 24-case preflight
The Customer Success coordination design is a staffing and handoff design: named staffed owner, rotating backup, service hours and time zone, capacity assumptions, admission-to-handoff trigger, transferred context, response target, after-hours queue treatment, escalation, and preservation of account support minutes from first contact. The later 24-case preflight is a separate future nonproduction workstream. EXPLICIT NO-AUTHORIZATION STATEMENT
Nothing in this September brief—or in the source cycle, Growth reminder replay/shadow, Customer Success coordination design, or later 24-case preflight—authorizes paid traffic, a second Q3 batch, budget, production connection, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, a new consumer, a release, a semantic change, or any transfer or expansion of authority. arguments.body:
Purpose
Run and evaluate the approved Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test without changing scope or existing operating rules, then use the certified path-quality result to make an organic pricing-page rollout decision.

Status
Experiment decision complete as of November 25, 2025. Priya approved the tested path-separated design as the default organic pricing-page experience and authorized Daniela to move treatment to 100% on November 26, 2025. This authorization is not evidence that rollout has already occurred: Daniela must perform tomorrow’s rollout before the treatment becomes the default experience. Until that rollout is performed, treatment remains non-default.

Design
- Audience: organic pricing-page sessions only.
- Allocation during the test: 50/50 control and treatment from October 20 through November 16, 2025.
- Treatment: separate the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path from the assisted path.
- Control: existing pricing-page path.

Certified result — November 19, 2025
Owen certified the completed four-cohort read across 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions: 1,639 control and 1,647 treatment. Among Helio Start eligibility-flow starts, 38 of 344 control starts (11.0%) versus 25 of 352 treatment starts (7.1%) routed out for an existing unsupported condition, a 35.7% relative reduction. Eligible-workspace admission completion was 43.8% in control and 44.1% in treatment. Account-level support time at the 90th percentile was 71 minutes in control and 74 minutes in treatment. The favorable direction held in all three weekly cohorts and the November 10–16 stabilization cohort, with no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change.

The predeclared path-quality threshold and both guardrails passed. The measured gain is fewer unsupported self-serve starts and funnel-quality evidence. It is not a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim.

Decision and rollout authorization — November 25, 2025
At the scheduled result decision, Priya approved the tested path-separated design as the default organic pricing-page experience and authorized Daniela to move treatment to 100% on November 26, 2025. Marcus Vail and Tomás accepted the framing that the measured gain is fewer unsupported self-serve starts and funnel-quality evidence, not a revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim.

The experiment decision is complete, but the treatment does not become default until Daniela performs the November 26 rollout. No claim of completed rollout or default treatment is made in this update.

Unchanged operating rules and boundaries
All existing boundaries remain intact, including eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules. Paid-acquisition boundaries remain unchanged: this evidence and authorization concern organic pricing-page traffic only; paid acquisition is excluded. Pipeline targets and forecast credit remain excluded. No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change was part of the test or result.

Decision criteria
- Primary threshold: at least a 25% relative reduction in eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition.
- Guardrail: eligible-workspace admission completion may decline by no more than 1.5 percentage points.
- Guardrail: account-level support time at the 90th percentile may increase by no more than 10 minutes.

Interpretation limits
This result supports fewer unsupported self-serve starts, funnel-quality evidence, and the organic pricing-page rollout decision only. It does not establish revenue lift, acquisition impact, pipeline impact, or forecast credit, and it does not change any eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, support-routing, paid-acquisition, pipeline, or forecast boundary.

Next action
Daniela is authorized to move treatment to 100% on November 26, 2025. Verify the rollout separately; until Daniela performs it, the tested treatment remains non-default.

Purpose
Run the approved Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test without changing scope or existing operating rules.

Status
Approved and in progress. The test remains LIVE. Treatment remains non-default; no default-experience change has been made or authorized.

Design
- Audience: organic pricing-page sessions only.
- Allocation: 50/50 control and treatment from October 20 through November 16, 2025.
- Treatment: separate the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path from the assisted path.
- Control: existing pricing-page path.

Unchanged operating rules and boundaries
All existing operating rules remain unchanged, including eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules. Paid traffic, pipeline targets, and forecast credit are excluded. Pricing-page layout and UI are frozen through November 16, including the November 10–16 stabilization cohort; no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change is permitted during this period.

Decision criteria
- Primary threshold: at least a 25% relative reduction in eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition.
- Guardrail: eligible-workspace admission completion may decline by no more than 1.5 percentage points.
- Guardrail: account-level support time at the 90th percentile may increase by no more than 10 minutes.

Interim checkpoint — November 10, 2025
The third complete weekly cohort, covering November 3–9, again points in the favorable direction on unsupported-condition route-outs. In that cohort, unsupported-condition routing was 9/86 (10.5%) in control and 6/88 (6.8%) in treatment. Both guardrails remained inside their limits: eligible-workspace admission completion was 43.8% control versus 44.2% treatment, and account-level support time at P90 was 71 minutes control versus 74 minutes treatment.

This is explicitly an interim checkpoint only. The November 10–16 stabilization cohort has only begun, so the evidence is incomplete and no result, rollout, default-experience, revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim is made. The checkpoint does not change the test status, treatment assignment, decision criteria, or operating boundaries.

Readout and decision
Owen will read three complete weekly cohorts plus the November 10–16 stabilization cohort. The stabilization cohort is required before the result is interpreted. Result-decision date: November 25, 2025. Until then, keep the test live, keep treatment non-default, and maintain the pricing-page layout/UI freeze through November 16.
