arguments.body:
# Helio Start connector-access investigation

## Live design (2024-04-23)

The reviewed connector-access change is live in the Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page. Applicants answer a connector-specific question for the selected supported connector:

- Yes — the applicant expects to be able to authenticate that connector account during the first week.
- No — the applicant cannot currently authenticate it.
- Not sure — the applicant's access is unresolved.

The connector-authentication answer is collected and stored separately from Helio workspace-administrator proof. The existing eligibility checks otherwise remain unchanged. Applicants must not enter passwords, tokens, or other secrets in this intake answer.

## Routing and lifecycle behavior

A definite Yes continues through the otherwise unchanged eligibility checks. It is not a replacement for, or evidence of, Helio administrator proof.

No and Not sure remain pending before workspace admission and route to assistance. Customer Success has added this pending case to its routing instructions so the applicant can receive help resolving connector access or clarifying the appropriate owner.

While connector-access proof is pending, Ines prevents connection prompts. This avoids asking an applicant to connect before the access question is resolved. After assistance resolves the case and the applicant satisfies the existing admission checks, the normal admission and connection lifecycle can proceed. The pending state itself does not admit a workspace and does not grant connector access.

## Operating owners

- Daniela: stores the connector-authentication answer as a distinct intake field from Helio admin proof.
- Ines: suppresses connection prompts while connector-access proof is pending and allows the normal prompt lifecycle after the pending condition is cleared.
- Customer Success: routes applicants with No or Not sure to assistance and follows the pending-case routing instructions.
- Owen: evaluates the post-cutover cohort descriptively, including answer distribution, assisted resolution, subsequent admission, and supported integration by day seven.

## Unchanged boundaries

This change does not alter the existing eligibility or refusal boundaries. Agencies, unresolved ownership, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, and all other existing route-out conditions remain unchanged. The connector-access answer cannot override those conditions, substitute for Helio administrator proof, or authorize unsupported permissions. A Yes answer only continues through the existing checks; it does not guarantee admission or successful integration.

## Owen's evaluation plan

Owen's readout is noncausal and descriptive. He will not claim that the question or routing caused any change, and there is no randomized treatment/control interpretation. For the post-cutover public-pricing cohort, he will examine:

1. Distribution of Yes, No, and Not sure answers, overall and by selected supported connector.
2. The share of No and Not sure cases receiving assistance and the assisted-resolution outcome.
3. Subsequent workspace admission after assistance or clarification, while retaining the existing route-out conditions in the denominator and reporting exclusions explicitly.
4. Supported integration by day seven among admitted applicants, with the day-7 window defined from the applicable admission/start point.
5. Operational follow-up for pending duration and connection-prompt suppression, to confirm that applicants are not prompted before proof is resolved.

Results should be segmented by answer and route, accompanied by cohort counts and denominators, and interpreted as monitoring evidence rather than causal impact. Existing eligibility and route-out categories must not be weakened or reclassified to improve the reported metrics.

arguments.title: Helio Start bounded GA — March 18 operating plan
arguments.body:
Helio Start bounded GA — March 18 operating plan

Decision and operating intent

The March 4 decision approves a bounded public self-serve launch for March 18, 2024. This is an operating model layered onto existing ownership and reporting—not a new team, reorganization, or open-ended expansion of scope. The launch makes Helio Start available only within the eligibility, refusal, routing, instrumentation, and risk controls below.

Operating principles

- Keep the public offer bounded and legible: admit eligible use cases, refuse or route cases the product cannot safely support, and preserve a clear record of each outcome.
- Treat activation and support load as co-equal operating signals. A launch that activates users but creates unmanaged support load is not healthy.
- Keep accepted self-serve exposure distinct from mature measurement windows and from accounts routed before setup. Do not collapse still-observing workspaces into “not activated,” “non-converting,” or “unsupported.”
- Use existing functional owners and existing decision forums; this plan coordinates work across functions rather than creating a new team.

1. Public eligibility and refusal rules

Public eligibility

Helio Start is available through the public self-serve path when the applicant:

- fits the published Helio Start use case and operating envelope;
- can complete setup with the supported integration and has the required administrative authority;
- can attest to the required admin proof during setup; and
- meets the published account, usage, and support expectations for the bounded beta/GA population and remaining capacity.

The public path must not imply that every applicant is entitled to self-serve access. Capacity remains bounded and the public entry point is an eligibility screen, not a promise of admission.

Refusal and routing

- Refuse or do not admit applicants who are outside the supported use case, lack the required administrative authority, cannot provide the required admin proof, or require unsupported permissions, environments, integrations, or service levels.
- Viewer/API-key cases that require administrative permissions are treated as PERMISSIONS_ADMIN_ROLE; they do not pass as ordinary self-serve setup merely because an API key is present.
- If the applicant is unsure about readiness, permissions, or setup ownership, route to Customer Success before setup rather than allowing an ambiguous self-serve outcome.
- Do not silently convert an ineligible or refused applicant into an accepted self-serve workspace. Record the disposition—accepted self-serve, routed before setup, or refused—and count each workspace once in the appropriate view.
- Route capacity-constrained or high-touch cases through the existing Customer Success path; do not create an exception queue that functions as an unbounded second product.

The public copy and intake experience must explain what is supported, what evidence is required, and what happens when the criteria are not met. Refusal is a controlled product boundary, not a support failure.

2. Owen — activation and support-load reporting

Owen owns separate Helio Start reporting from retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist reporting. The reporting lane will:

- report total accepted self-serve invited workspaces as total exposure;
- show seven-day-window-complete workspaces separately from still-observing workspaces;
- report activation only on the mature, seven-day-window-complete denominator;
- report support load as a first-class metric alongside activation, including support contacts/cases and the relevant incidence rate on the appropriate mature denominator;
- preserve routed-before-setup and refused outcomes as separate dispositions rather than mixing them into self-serve activation or support rates; and
- reconcile workspace-level counts so that a workspace is counted once in its applicable disposition and cohort view.

Every readout should make the denominator and maturity state explicit. Do not publish one current activation rate or support rate over all invited workspaces when the observation window is incomplete. Still-observing workspaces remain exposure and are labeled as observing.

Owen’s reporting is an operating signal for the existing cross-functional decision lane. It is not a new reporting organization and does not replace the source-of-truth instrumentation owned by Daniela.

3. Daniela — entitlement and support-state instrumentation checks

Daniela owns the entitlement and support-state instrumentation needed to make the public self-serve model auditable. Before March 18 and during launch monitoring, verify that:

- the accepted-self-serve, routed-before-setup, and refused dispositions are recorded distinctly;
- entitlement state is singular and current for each workspace, with no duplicate or contradictory active entitlement;
- support state is singular and current, including the distinction between self-serve, routed/assisted, and refused or otherwise ineligible states;
- admin proof is captured as admin_proof_attested, and the event/state is tied to the correct workspace and lifecycle stage;
- permission failures are represented as PERMISSIONS_ADMIN_ROLE where applicable rather than misclassified as generic setup friction;
- unsure applicants are observable as assisted-setup routing, not lost in an unclassified funnel step; and
- dashboard tracking reconciles to backend/source events for entitlement, support state, routing, and activation.

Instrumentation checks must include a pre-launch validation, a launch-day smoke check, and a post-launch reconciliation. Any discrepancy that could change an activation or support-load denominator is raised in the existing cross-functional decision lane before the metric is used for a decision.

4. Ines — lifecycle copy and risk controls

Ines owns lifecycle copy and risk controls for the public self-serve model. The copy must:

- state the supported use case and the bounded nature of access;
- make the admin-proof and permissions requirement clear before setup;
- explain the difference between self-serve eligibility and Customer Success routing;
- avoid promising unsupported service levels, universal admission, or outcomes that the product cannot yet substantiate; and
- tell refused or routed applicants what the next valid path is without disguising a refusal as activation.

Risk controls

- Keep the public eligibility/refusal rules consistent across the pricing page, signup, setup, lifecycle messages, and support macros.
- Ensure lifecycle audiences respect entitlement and support state; do not send self-serve activation messaging to refused or pre-setup-routed cases.
- Gate or pause messaging if instrumentation shows duplicate entitlements, incorrect support states, missing admin proof, or a material mismatch between dashboard and backend state.
- Use the existing review and escalation path for copy or risk changes; do not broaden eligibility through ad hoc messaging.

5. Customer Success — routed-before-setup path

Customer Success owns the path for accounts routed before setup. The path begins when an applicant is unsure about readiness, administrative authority, permissions, or fit, or when the account falls into a high-touch/capacity-constrained case.

Customer Success will:

- receive the routed case before setup;
- confirm fit, administrative authority, permissions, and the appropriate entitlement/support state;
- either return an eligible account to the supported self-serve path, continue an assisted setup, or close the case as refused/ineligible;
- keep the workspace’s disposition singular and current so it is not counted both as accepted self-serve and as an accepted self-serve outcome after routing; and
- report routed volume and contacts separately from self-serve activation and support-load denominators.

The March 18 plan explicitly excludes:

- paid acquisition or paid campaigns during the launch week;

arguments.body:
LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS Q2 KICKOFF — MARCH 18 OPEN QUESTIONS
Working record | prepared March 8, 2027

Purpose
Keep the March 18 kickoff compact, evidence-led, and lane-specific. The four operating lanes remain separate; this meeting is for open questions, owner inputs, and boundary confirmation—not for expanding the decision surface.

FOUR EXISTING OPERATING LANES

1. Helio Start
Scope: paid-source and operating-control evidence for Helio Start, kept descriptive and separate from lifecycle-governance decisions.
Current owner responsibilities:
- Riley: final operating claim, claim boundaries, and board-readiness decisions.
- Owen: source completeness, denominator/window documentation, coverage and measurement limits; escalate missing fields or disputed semantics.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance limits, including eligibility, routing, suppression, and handoff semantics.
- Daniela: source and release reliability, instrumentation, and engineering-control evidence where applicable.
- Marcus Vail: forecast ownership remains separate; no forecast treatment follows from this lane without an explicit decision.
- Tomás: final board narrative; no narrative expansion is implied by the kickoff.

2. Expansion Assist
Scope: descriptive qualifying-admin, usage, assistance, and expansion evidence; do not combine it with Helio Start or customer-outcome claims.
Current owner responsibilities:
- Riley: final operating claim and reconciliation of separate views and denominators.
- Owen: certified evidence extract, cohort dates, coverage/window metadata, and routine completeness review.
- Ines: operating rules and lifecycle limits, including eligibility, pacing, suppression, and handoff semantics.
- Marcus Vail: forecast treatment remains his separate responsibility and is not inferred from descriptive activity.
- Customer Success / renewal owner: provide the status and outcome of any renewal work or planned exposure without converting it into a causal or revenue claim.

3. Pricing-page path quality
Scope: path definitions, progression, and post-rollout continuity signals—not pricing-driven revenue or conversion attribution.
Current owner responsibilities:
- Riley: operating evidence coordination and final bounded claim.
- Analytics / operating source owner: path definitions, event-taxonomy checks, snapshots, denominators, and coverage dates; named-owner confirmation is still an input where not assigned.
- Daniela: source and release-reliability evidence.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance review if path behavior touches eligibility, routing, suppression, or handoff.

4. CS auto-nudge system controls
Scope: system-control performance, coverage, reliability, and governed execution—not customer response or causal lift.
Current owner responsibilities:
- Riley: final operating claim; keep control performance separate from customer-outcome evidence.
- Daniela: control coverage, source/release reliability, engineering release and rollback control, and cross-surface reliability gaps.
- Engineering / control source owner: control logs, population and coverage basis, exact coverage dates, source freshness, and exception treatment; named-owner confirmation is still an input where not assigned.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance limits when control behavior touches eligibility, suppression, routing, or handoff.
- Owen: routine source-completeness review only when required fields are present, definitions are unchanged, named owners have certified their sections, and no cross-surface discrepancy exists.

SHARED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY
Riley retains final operating claims and board-readiness decisions. Ines retains lifecycle-governance limits. Daniela retains source-reliability and engineering release/rollback control. Owen has only the bounded routine source-completeness closure authority described above. Marcus Vail retains forecast ownership. Tomás retains the final board narrative. No owner’s role is broadened by this kickoff.

DECISIONS OUTSIDE THE MARCH 18 KICKOFF
The kickoff does not approve:
- a Helio Start paid proposal;
- a Helio Start budget;
- Helio Start paid traffic;
- Helio Start pipeline treatment;
- Helio Start forecast credit;
- a fifth shared-state consumer;
- any change to existing eligibility boundaries; or
- any change to existing lifecycle boundaries, including routing, suppression, pacing, or handoff semantics.

It also does not approve a second paid batch, scale or acquisition claims, causal or revenue treatment, new customer-outcome interpretation, a new pricing experiment, or a change to CS auto-nudge behavior. Paid traffic remains off; any later commercial proposal requires its own explicit review and approval. Descriptive, continuity, and system-control evidence must not be combined into a growth number or forecast input by implication.

SHORT INPUT-NEEDED LIST
1. Helio Start: mature authority-checklist cohort support input, staffed CS admission-cap input, and a clear statement of what remains unavailable for any paid proposal; confirm that no paid traffic or second batch has started.
2. Expansion Assist: current status and source-backed outcome of the renewal work / planned exposure, with the exact as-of time and unchanged eligibility interpretation.
3. Pricing-page path quality: named source owner, event/path definitions, taxonomy checks, denominator, coverage dates, and continuity snapshot.
4. CS auto-nudge: named control source owner, latest control log and coverage basis, source-age/reliability status, and any release, rollback, disagreement, correction, or exception record.
5. All lanes: owner certifications, definitions, exclusions, and cross-surface discrepancy check before any completeness closure.

KICKOFF OUTPUT
A compact list of answered questions, unresolved inputs with owners and dates, and confirmed boundaries. No lane is merged with another, and no decision outside the stated kickoff scope is implied by attendance or discussion.

arguments.title: Helio Start bounded GA — March 18 operating plan
arguments.body:
Helio Start bounded GA — March 18 operating plan

Decision and operating intent

The March 4 decision approves a bounded public self-serve launch for March 18, 2024. This is an operating model layered onto existing ownership and reporting—not a new team, reorganization, or open-ended expansion of scope. The launch makes Helio Start available only within the eligibility, refusal, routing, instrumentation, and risk controls below.

Operating principles

- Keep the public offer bounded and legible: admit eligible use cases, refuse or route cases the product cannot safely support, and preserve a clear record of each outcome.
- Treat activation and support load as co-equal operating signals. A launch that activates users but creates unmanaged support load is not healthy.
- Keep accepted self-serve exposure distinct from mature measurement windows and from accounts routed before setup. Do not collapse still-observing workspaces into “not activated,” “non-converting,” or “unsupported.”
- Use existing functional owners and existing decision forums; this plan coordinates work across functions rather than creating a new team.

1. Public eligibility and refusal rules

Public eligibility

Helio Start is available through the public self-serve path when the applicant:

- fits the published Helio Start use case and operating envelope;
- can complete setup with the supported integration and has the required administrative authority;
- can attest to the required admin proof during setup; and
- meets the published account, usage, and support expectations for the bounded beta/GA population and remaining capacity.

The public path must not imply that every applicant is entitled to self-serve access. Capacity remains bounded and the public entry point is an eligibility screen, not a promise of admission.

Refusal and routing

- Refuse or do not admit applicants who are outside the supported use case, lack the required administrative authority, cannot provide the required admin proof, or require unsupported permissions, environments, integrations, or service levels.
- Viewer/API-key cases that require administrative permissions are treated as PERMISSIONS_ADMIN_ROLE; they do not pass as ordinary self-serve setup merely because an API key is present.
- If the applicant is unsure about readiness, permissions, or setup ownership, route to Customer Success before setup rather than allowing an ambiguous self-serve outcome.
- Do not silently convert an ineligible or refused applicant into an accepted self-serve workspace. Record the disposition—accepted self-serve, routed before setup, or refused—and count each workspace once in the appropriate view.
- Route capacity-constrained or high-touch cases through the existing Customer Success path; do not create an exception queue that functions as an unbounded second product.

The public copy and intake experience must explain what is supported, what evidence is required, and what happens when the criteria are not met. Refusal is a controlled product boundary, not a support failure.

2. Owen — activation and support-load reporting

Owen owns separate Helio Start reporting from retained mid-segment and Expansion Assist reporting. The reporting lane will:

- report total accepted self-serve invited workspaces as total exposure;
- show seven-day-window-complete workspaces separately from still-observing workspaces;
- report activation only on the mature, seven-day-window-complete denominator;
- report support load as a first-class metric alongside activation, including support contacts/cases and the relevant incidence rate on the appropriate mature denominator;
- preserve routed-before-setup and refused outcomes as separate dispositions rather than mixing them into self-serve activation or support rates; and
- reconcile workspace-level counts so that a workspace is counted once in its applicable disposition and cohort view.

Every readout should make the denominator and maturity state explicit. Do not publish one current activation rate or support rate over all invited workspaces when the observation window is incomplete. Still-observing workspaces remain exposure and are labeled as observing.

Owen’s reporting is an operating signal for the existing cross-functional decision lane. It is not a new reporting organization and does not replace the source-of-truth instrumentation owned by Daniela.

3. Daniela — entitlement and support-state instrumentation checks

Daniela owns the entitlement and support-state instrumentation needed to make the public self-serve model auditable. Before March 18 and during launch monitoring, verify that:

- the accepted-self-serve, routed-before-setup, and refused dispositions are recorded distinctly;
- entitlement state is singular and current for each workspace, with no duplicate or contradictory active entitlement;
- support state is singular and current, including the distinction between self-serve, routed/assisted, and refused or otherwise ineligible states;
- admin proof is captured as admin_proof_attested, and the event/state is tied to the correct workspace and lifecycle stage;
- permission failures are represented as PERMISSIONS_ADMIN_ROLE where applicable rather than misclassified as generic setup friction;
- unsure applicants are observable as assisted-setup routing, not lost in an unclassified funnel step; and
- dashboard tracking reconciles to backend/source events for entitlement, support state, routing, and activation.

Instrumentation checks must include a pre-launch validation, a launch-day smoke check, and a post-launch reconciliation. Any discrepancy that could change an activation or support-load denominator is raised in the existing cross-functional decision lane before the metric is used for a decision.

4. Ines — lifecycle copy and risk controls

Ines owns lifecycle copy and risk controls for the public self-serve model. The copy must:

- state the supported use case and the bounded nature of access;
- make the admin-proof and permissions requirement clear before setup;
- explain the difference between self-serve eligibility and Customer Success routing;
- avoid promising unsupported service levels, universal admission, or outcomes that the product cannot yet substantiate; and
- tell refused or routed applicants what the next valid path is without disguising a refusal as activation.

Risk controls

- Keep the public eligibility/refusal rules consistent across the pricing page, signup, setup, lifecycle messages, and support macros.
- Ensure lifecycle audiences respect entitlement and support state; do not send self-serve activation messaging to refused or pre-setup-routed cases.
- Gate or pause messaging if instrumentation shows duplicate entitlements, incorrect support states, missing admin proof, or a material mismatch between dashboard and backend state.
- Use the existing review and escalation path for copy or risk changes; do not broaden eligibility through ad hoc messaging.

5. Customer Success — routed-before-setup path

Customer Success owns the path for accounts routed before setup. The path begins when an applicant is unsure about readiness, administrative authority, permissions, or fit, or when the account falls into a high-touch/capacity-constrained case.

Customer Success will:

- receive the routed case before setup;
- confirm fit, administrative authority, permissions, and the appropriate entitlement/support state;
- either return an eligible account to the supported self-serve path, continue an assisted setup, or close the case as refused/ineligible;
- keep the workspace’s disposition singular and current so it is not counted both as accepted self-serve and as an accepted self-serve outcome after routing; and
- report routed volume and contacts separately from self-serve activation and support-load denominators.

Routing is an existing operating path owned by Customer Success, not a new team or a backdoor to unrestricted admission. Support should use neutral, consistent language: the account is being routed for fit/setup confirmation, not labeled as failed or unsupported while it is still being assessed.

6. Executive-language and cross-functional decision lane

The executive description is: “On March 18, Helio Start will enter a bounded public self-serve model with explicit eligibility and refusal rules, existing-function ownership, and activation plus support-load monitoring.”

Use “bounded public self-serve launch” or “bounded GA” where appropriate. Do not describe this as a new team, a broad commercial expansion, universal self-serve access, or a forecast commitment.

The cross-functional decision lane uses the existing owners:

- Owen: activation and support-load reporting;
- Daniela: entitlement and support-state instrumentation;
- Ines: lifecycle copy and risk controls; and
- Customer Success: routed-before-setup support path.

The executive decision lane reviews the combined readout—exposure, maturity, activation, support load, routing, refusals, entitlement/support-state integrity, and copy/risk exceptions—and decides whether to maintain the bounded model, adjust controls, pause an element, or bring a separately approved scope change for decision. No single metric or immature cohort view is sufficient on its own.

7. Explicit exclusions and guardrails

The March 18 plan explicitly excludes:

- paid acquisition or paid campaigns during the launch week;
- forecastable pipeline language, including a “$300K Q2 pipeline target” or any equivalent forecast claim in the launch or sales brief;
- treating the bounded self-serve launch as a commitment to a forecastable pipeline outcome;
- creating a new Helio Start team or separate standing organization; and
- expanding eligibility, service levels, or go-to-market scope through copy, routing, or reporting changes without a new decision.

The launch is therefore a bounded operating model: a public entry point with explicit boundaries, coordinated execution through existing functions, and a decision loop grounded in mature activation, support load, and state integrity.

arguments.title: Final Helio Start Authority-Diagnostic Closeout
arguments.body:
Final Helio Start Authority-Diagnostic Closeout

Closeout date
December 12, 2024

Scope and completion
The final Helio Start diagnostic window is closed. All 60 enrolled workspaces completed their full 45-day post-admission support windows.

Complete results

• 17 of 60 workspaces contacted support during the window.
• Those workspaces generated 486 post-admission human support minutes.
• 7 contacts were authority cases involving owner-level permission, network allowlisting, or another external-authority dependency.
  • 301 post-admission human minutes.
  • 3.6-business-day median resolution time.
  • 12 substantive repeat contacts.
• 10 contacts were product-guidance cases.
  • 185 post-admission human minutes.
  • 1.4-day median resolution time.
  • 6 substantive repeat contacts.

The categories reconcile to the full observed support population: 7 authority cases plus 10 product-guidance cases equals 17 contacted workspaces, and 301 plus 185 equals 486 human minutes.

Supported interpretation
The diagnostic supports treating external-system authority as a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication.

Every authority case had already passed the Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication checks. The subsequent owner-level permission, network-allowlist, or other external-authority dependency therefore represents a distinct dependency outside those Helio checks—not evidence that the Helio admission checks were ineffective or that the workspace failed Helio authentication.

The result is a bounded readiness interpretation: Helio admission evidence can establish Helio administrator authority and connector authentication, while readiness may still depend on authority held in an external system. Both inputs matter, and they should not be collapsed into one check.

Operating boundaries remain unchanged

• Existing Helio Start admission rules remain unchanged. No new admission gate or revised eligibility threshold is established by this closeout.
• Existing routing rules remain unchanged. Authority cases continue to be handled through the existing external-authority/owner or network-allowlist path; product-guidance cases continue through the existing product-guidance path.
• External-system authority remains a separately classified dependency. It is not reclassified as a Helio admin-proof or connector-authentication failure.
• The diagnostic results do not authorize automatic changes to onboarding, support routing, or operating scope.
• The results must not be generalized into a claim that onboarding or support demand as a whole is broken. The observed population includes seven authority cases and ten product-guidance cases, with distinct causes and resolution patterns.

Closeout conclusion
The 45-day diagnostic is complete for all 60 enrolled workspaces. It establishes a clear, limited finding: external-system authority created a meaningful but separately bounded source of post-admission work even after Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication checks passed. The existing admission and routing rules, classifications, and operating boundaries remain in force.

Ines owns routine, non-state-changing sends within her authority and routine preflights. Daniela retains engineering release controls, and Ines does not have engineering release-control access. This clarified operational ownership without weakening the safety boundary.

• I handled the stale-retry-manifest correction without overstating its cause. I focused on correcting the operational issue and kept the explanation within what the evidence supported.

• I repeatedly corrected metric definitions before unsupported claims reached leadership. This included checking what each measure actually counted and separating supported conclusions from interpretations that the underlying data could not establish.

Improvement area

I need to reduce late-stage manual interpretation by specifying ownership and evidence boundaries earlier. In practice, that means defining who can decide, what evidence is required, and what remains out of scope before work reaches final review or release. This should make corrections less dependent on my intervention late in the process.

Overall reflection

My strongest contribution this year was making operational decisions more precise: narrowing claims to the evidence, separating readiness inputs, and delegating routine work while preserving explicit controls for higher-risk actions. The next step is to make those boundaries legible earlier so the system and team carry more of that precision without late-stage manual interpretation.

arguments.body:
Q3 LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS PRIORITIES
Decision memo for Priya’s review

Date: June 17, 2025

Decision summary

Treat the CS auto-nudge migration as complete in the Q3 Lifecycle Systems outline. It is not a pending gate for Q3 work. The shared-state contract is the single production path for CS auto-nudge decisions; the legacy nightly decision path has been disabled and retained only for engineering rollback. Q3 priorities should therefore focus on making the operating model routine, observable, and well-governed—not on re-opening the migration decision.

Q3 operating priorities

1. Routine single-path operating explanation — Owen

- Make the single production path easy to explain and operate in ordinary weekly workflows.
- Document the normal decision flow, operator responsibilities, freshness expectations, and the conditions under which an incident rollback or customer correction is appropriate.
- Keep the explanation operational and concise: the migration is complete, the shared-state contract is authoritative, and the legacy path is rollback-only.

2. Messaging consumption and lifecycle governance — Ines

- Own how downstream messaging consumes governed shared-state outputs.
- Maintain lifecycle governance for field meanings, eligibility and suppression behavior, freshness limits, review points, and changes to consuming workflows.
- Preserve the distinction between a governed readiness signal and authorization for automated contact.
- Ensure consumer changes are reviewed against the existing contract rather than creating parallel decision logic.

3. Transport and source reliability — Daniela

- Own connector, transport, source-system, and shared-state reliability.
- Maintain the health checks, failure handling, observability, and incident procedures needed to keep the single path dependable.
- Retain rollback capability for engineering incidents without treating the legacy path as a second production evaluator or release path.

4. High-stakes decisions — Riley

- Reserve high-stakes customer, safety, incident-stop, and material operating decisions for Riley’s explicit judgment.
- Do not convert a governed readiness or review signal into blanket authorization for contact or action.
- Restoration of the legacy path remains limited to Daniela’s incident rollback or Riley’s customer-correction or incident-stop decision.

Current operating state to preserve

- The CS auto-nudge migration is complete as of June 17, 2025.
- The shared-state contract is the single production path.
- The five governed field meanings remain unchanged.
- The external-system authority meaning is verified readiness for the connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; it is not permission for automated contact.
- The legacy nightly decision path is disabled and retained only for engineering rollback.
- CS review is not blanket authorization; renewal-risk handling continues to require mapping, owner review, freshness limits, an operator view, and rollback rehearsal.

Helio Start scope clarification

Helio Start is already a bounded-GA self-serve product and is already represented on the public pricing page. Q3 planning should treat that status as existing operating context. This memo does not propose a new beta, a launch decision, or a pricing-page decision.

Helio Start reporting is one of the existing shared-state consumers. It should be governed and supported within the existing consumer model. It does not constitute a fifth consumer, and Q3 planning should not introduce or imply an additional consumer count.

Q3 non-goals

- Re-litigating or gating Q3 on the completed CS auto-nudge migration.
- Creating a new CS auto-nudge beta or launch phase.
- Making a new Helio Start launch or pricing-page decision.
- Treating Helio Start reporting as a fifth shared-state consumer.
- Reintroducing the legacy nightly path as a parallel production path.
- Expanding operational signals into automatic-contact authorization.

Review decision requested from Priya

Approve the Q3 Lifecycle Systems outline with the following framing:

- Migration complete; no pending migration gate.
- Owen: routine single-path operating explanation.
- Ines: messaging consumption and lifecycle governance.
- Daniela: transport and source reliability.
- Riley: high-stakes decisions and explicit exception authority.
- Helio Start: bounded-GA self-serve product already on the public pricing page; reporting remains an existing shared-state consumer, not a fifth consumer.

Success measures for Q3

- Operators can explain and execute the normal single-path workflow without referring to the legacy path as active production logic.
- Consumer changes remain within the governed shared-state contract.
- Transport and source failures are observable, owned, and recoverable through documented procedures.
- High-stakes exceptions have explicit human decision ownership.
- Q3 planning materials contain no new beta, launch, pricing-page, or fifth-consumer implication.

arguments.title: Helio Start internal triage FAQ
arguments.body:
Helio Start internal triage FAQ

Purpose
Apply the established eligibility, pending-state, assistance, and refusal rules consistently. Do not infer permission, eligibility, or authority from a nearby signal.

What are the three checks?

1. Helio admin proof
This is the required evidence that the person meets the Helio admin-proof requirement for the relevant eligibility decision. It is an eligibility input, not a substitute for connector authentication or verified authority in an external system.

2. Connector authentication
This is the authentication/setup state for connecting to the relevant external system. Successful authentication means the connector can authenticate; it does not by itself establish Helio eligibility, admin proof, or authority to act in that external system.

3. External-system authority
This is the verified authority state in the external system needed for connector readiness. It is connector-readiness state only—not permission for automated contact, other outreach, or any action outside the established product flow.

What is the ordinary product-guidance path?
Use the docs-first path for ordinary, supported product guidance: point to the applicable documentation and provide guidance within the documented self-serve flow. Do not use assistance to bypass an unmet eligibility requirement, pending state, refusal, or an unresolved authority question.

How do we handle assistance?

• Pending assistance before admission: Keep the account pending when a required field is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting. Preserve the reason at the field level. Provide only the permitted docs-first/product guidance; do not treat assistance or a Proceed signal as admission or as blanket permission to contact the account.

• Supported admission: Admit only when the established eligibility requirements are satisfied and the required state is verified and current. Then provide supported product guidance within the documented path. Connector readiness still does not authorize automated contact or other outreach.

• Routing outside self-serve: If the request is not ordinary supported guidance, cannot be resolved through the docs-first path, or requires authority or handling not available in self-serve, route it through the established non-self-serve path. Do not improvise a workaround or override a refusal.

Fail-closed rules
Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state remains fail-closed. Keep the corresponding field pending, retain its specific pending reason, and do not manually release it based on adjacent evidence. A verified external authority signal does not change this rule and does not grant outreach permission.

Refusal boundary
Refuse requests that would bypass eligibility, pending-state, assistance, or refusal rules; expose or act on authority that has not been verified; or initiate automated contact or other outreach merely because connector readiness is present.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start connector-access investigation

## Live design (2024-04-23)

The reviewed connector-access change is live in the Helio Start intake reached from the public pricing page. Applicants answer a connector-specific question for the selected supported connector:

- Yes — the applicant expects to be able to authenticate that connector account during the first week.
- No — the applicant cannot currently authenticate it.
- Not sure — the applicant's access is unresolved.

The connector-authentication answer is collected and stored separately from Helio workspace-administrator proof. The existing eligibility checks otherwise remain unchanged. Applicants must not enter passwords, tokens, or other secrets in this intake answer.

## Routing and lifecycle behavior

A definite Yes continues through the otherwise unchanged eligibility checks. It is not a replacement for, or evidence of, Helio administrator proof.

No and Not sure remain pending before workspace admission and route to assistance. Customer Success has added this pending case to its routing instructions so the applicant can receive help resolving connector access or clarifying the appropriate owner.

While connector-access proof is pending, Ines prevents connection prompts. This avoids asking an applicant to connect before the access question is resolved. After assistance resolves the case and the applicant satisfies the existing admission checks, the normal admission and connection lifecycle can proceed. The pending state itself does not admit a workspace and does not grant connector access.

## Operating owners

- Daniela: stores the connector-authentication answer as a distinct intake field from Helio admin proof.
- Ines: suppresses connection prompts while connector-access proof is pending and allows the normal prompt lifecycle after the pending condition is cleared.
- Customer Success: routes applicants with No or Not sure to assistance and follows the pending-case routing instructions.
- Owen: evaluates the post-cutover cohort descriptively, including answer distribution, assisted resolution, subsequent admission, and supported integration by day seven.

## Unchanged boundaries

This change does not alter the existing eligibility or refusal boundaries. Agencies, unresolved ownership, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, and all other existing route-out conditions remain unchanged. The connector-access answer cannot override those conditions, substitute for Helio administrator proof, or authorize unsupported permissions. A Yes answer only continues through the existing checks; it does not guarantee admission or successful integration.

## Owen's evaluation plan

Owen's readout is noncausal and descriptive. He will not claim that the question or routing caused any change, and there is no randomized treatment/control interpretation. For the post-cutover public-pricing cohort, he will examine:

1. Distribution of Yes, No, and Not sure answers, overall and by selected supported connector.
2. The share of No and Not sure cases receiving assistance and the assisted-resolution outcome.
3. Subsequent workspace admission after assistance or clarification, while retaining the existing route-out conditions in the denominator and reporting exclusions explicitly.
4. Supported integration by day seven among admitted applicants, with the day-7 window defined from the applicable admission/start point.
5. Operational follow-up for pending duration and connection-prompt suppression, to confirm that applicants are not prompted before proof is resolved.

Results should be segmented by answer and route, accompanied by cohort counts and denominators, and interpreted as monitoring evidence rather than causal impact. Existing eligibility and route-out categories must not be weakened or reclassified to improve the reported metrics.

arguments.body:
Diagnostic question
Among recent Helio Start applicants who expressed connector-access uncertainty, which uncertainty concerns:
1. control of existing credentials,
2. supported-connector availability,
3. security approval timing, or
4. an expectation of same-day setup?

Purpose and sponsor boundary
Priya approved this narrow diagnostic question in the Monday one-on-one. The output is a coded descriptive read only—not a recommendation to change admission, product scope, or applicant handling.

Eight-interaction sample
Review eight recent, de-identified applicant interactions meeting the cohort scope. Hold the sample as eight interaction records labeled Interaction 1 through Interaction 8 (or equivalent de-identified IDs). Preserve only the evidence needed for coding; exclude names, company identifiers, contact details, and other direct identifiers.

Coding dimensions
Code each interaction for evidence of one or more of the following dimensions; multi-coding is allowed:
- Credential control: uncertainty about who controls, can authorize, or can provide access to existing credentials.
- Supported-connector availability: uncertainty about whether the needed connector/integration is supported or available.
- Security approval timing: uncertainty about the time required for security, IT, procurement, or related approval.
- Same-day setup expectation: uncertainty arising from an expectation that setup or access should be completed the same day.

For each interaction, record the de-identified interaction ID, concise evidence excerpt or paraphrase, dimension code(s), and a short rationale. Summarize counts by dimension and note overlap; do not infer prevalence beyond this eight-interaction descriptive sample. If an interaction does not fit, use an explicit other/uncodable note rather than forcing a code.

Exclusions
- Do not reopen, revise, or evaluate the Helio Start admission rule.
- Do not label uncertainty itself as a product defect.
- Do not recommend a change to admission, eligibility, or routing based on this read.
- Do not pull Owen back into weekly signoff.
- Do not convert the descriptive counts into a causal claim, forecast, or general population estimate.
- Do not identify applicants or include unnecessary sensitive or proprietary details.

Unchanged-admission decision boundary
The current Helio Start admission decision remains unchanged throughout this work. This is an observational coding exercise about the character of connector-access uncertainty among eight recent interactions. Any future policy or admission discussion would require a separate decision and approval path; it is outside this brief.

Among recent Helio Start applicants who expressed connector-access uncertainty, which uncertainty concerns:
1. control of existing credentials,
2. supported-connector availability,
3. security approval timing, or
4. an expectation of same-day setup?

Purpose and sponsor boundary
Priya approved this narrow diagnostic question in the Monday one-on-one. The output is a coded descriptive read only—not a recommendation to change admission, product scope, or applicant handling.

Eight-interaction sample
Review eight recent, de-identified applicant interactions meeting the cohort scope. Hold the sample as eight interaction records labeled Interaction 1 through Interaction 8 (or equivalent de-identified IDs). Preserve only the evidence needed for coding; exclude names, company identifiers, contact details, and other direct identifiers.

Coded table
Dimension | Count of 8 excerpts | Descriptive coding note
Credential control / usable-credential ownership | 4 | Uncertainty about who controls the usable credentials or can authorize/provide access.
Security approval timing | 2 | Unresolved timing for security approval.
Supported-connector availability | 1 | Question about an unsupported in-house connector.
Same-day setup expectation | 1 | Expectation of same-day workspace and connector setup.

Coding interpretation and limitation
The counts are descriptive for this eight-excerpt sample only. Coding dimensions overlap only where an excerpt explicitly supports both issues; the counts do not measure prevalence, support a population estimate, establish causality, or establish a product defect. The table should therefore be read as a small-sample diagnostic of the character of the reviewed interactions, not as evidence that any issue is widespread or that the admission flow is defective.

1. Is clearer pre-application ownership language worth testing?
2. Is supported-connector language sufficiently visible?
3. Do same-day expectations arise from copy outside the admission flow?

- Credential control: uncertainty about who controls, can authorize, or can provide access to existing credentials.

- Security approval timing: uncertainty about the time required for security, IT, procurement, or related approval.
- Same-day setup expectation: uncertainty arising from an expectation that setup or access should be completed the same day.

arguments.body:
# Helio Start continuation-gate evidence brief

## Purpose and decision context
This brief records the evidence and decision state for the May 24 review and subsequent operating decision. It is not a launch announcement and does not broaden Helio Start eligibility.

## Validated evidence through the fifth cohort
Across five non-overlapping cohorts:

- 274 admitted accounts have complete day-7 observation windows.
- 210 accounts received supported first integrations.
- The five cohorts are the defined evidence set for the May 24 review.

## Validated six-cohort evidence
- 334 admitted accounts have complete day-7 observation windows.
- 256 accounts received supported first integrations (76.6% validated cumulative activation).
- In the validated sixth cohort, 46 supported integrations were recorded among 60 admitted accounts with complete day-7 windows (76.7%).
- Two integrations were removed from the preliminary totals because a local-calendar-date query counted them after the accounts’ exact day-7 timestamp cutoffs. This was an activation-window query correction, not a routing or entitlement-integrity problem.

These figures are cohort evidence only. They must not be described as mature retention, paid conversion, forecastable revenue, or a revenue claim.

## Latest-cohort support-contact accounting
- Post-admission support: 17 contacts across 12 workspaces. These contacts are outside the admitted-account activation denominator; they are not additional failures or additional accounts.
- Intake support: 8 pre-admission connector-assistance contacts across 5 applicants. This is a separate intake-support line and must not be mixed with post-admission workspace contacts.

## Data-quality checks
- Entitlement-state check: clean; no duplicate or blank current entitlement state.
- Lifecycle-branch check: clean; no unsupported lifecycle branch.

These checks establish evidence quality and support-contact context; they do not establish mature retention, paid conversion, or revenue.

## Separate connector-access check
This evidence remains separate from the validated six-cohort totals. No non-overlap relationship between this evidence and those six cohorts has been established, so these figures must not be folded into, added to, or used to revise the six-cohort totals.

### Intake and routing
- 92 completed applications were reviewed.
- Applications were assigned to three routing groups.

### Admitted-workspace operating outcomes
- 59 integrations were recorded among 68 admitted workspaces.
- Three admitted workspaces were nonactivators attributed to credential-related issues.
- For comparison, the prior admitted population had 18 credential-related stalls among 147 admitted workspaces.
- Customer Success recorded 11 support contacts across eight admitted workspaces.

This is operating evidence about connector access, admission readiness, activation friction, credential-related stalls, and support context. It does not establish mature retention, paid conversion, or revenue.

## Completed day-90 status table
All 52 day-90 windows are mature. The statuses are mutually exclusive and exhaustive:

| Day-90 status | Accounts | Share of 52 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Paid and active | 39 | 75.0% |
| Canceled before day 90 | 7 | 13.5% |
| Past due at day 90 | 4 | 7.7% |
| Billing hold at day 90 | 2 | 3.8% |
| Total | 52 | 100.0% |

The completed table remains separate from the validated 41-of-52 day-30 settled-cash measure and from later-refund observations. The 39 paid-active result is a day-90 retention observation for this bounded organic cohort; it is not, by itself, evidence of paid-acquisition economics, pipeline, or forecastable revenue.

## Decision state — unchanged boundary through Q3
Continue bounded organic availability through Q3 within the current scope. This remains a bounded continuation of the organic pricing-page path, not broader eligibility, a self-serve approval for all applicants, a paid-acquisition authorization, a Q3 pipeline commitment, or a revenue forecast.

Paid acquisition was declined. A Q3 pipeline target was declined. No paid test, pipeline target, or forecast claim has been approved under this decision.

## Existing refusal rules and connector-access check
Keep the refusal and routing rules in force:

- The pricing page may say: “Fast path for eligible teams.”
- It must say: “Check your fit and connector access to start self-serve if eligible; applicants who need assistance or fall outside the criteria will be routed accordingly.”
- Self-serve is available only when the applicant meets the current fit criteria and passes the connector-access check. Refuse or route away from self-serve when the applicant needs assistance, lacks supported connector access, or falls outside the criteria.
- Manual-invoiced annual agreements and custom payment terms are outside self-serve billing; route otherwise-fit applicants to assisted handling without implying that assisted handling is self-serve approval or setup fit.

Do not broaden eligibility, convert observed activation into a revenue claim, or weaken these refusal rules during Q3.

## Reconsideration evidence gate
Any later paid-acquisition proposal must present the combined evidence owned jointly by Owen and Customer Success:

1. Mature retention status, including the complete day-90 table.
2. Refund-adjusted cash.
3. Account-level support effort.

These measures must remain separate at the account level; they must not be collapsed into a single blended measure or substituted with first-paid, activation, or paid-active status alone. No later paid-acquisition proposal is approved merely because the day-90 table is complete. Until a separate decision approves otherwise, the boundary remains bounded organic continuation through Q3, with no paid test, pipeline target, or forecast claim approved.

arguments.message:
Implementation handoff — approved Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test

Test window: October 20–November 16. Organic pricing-page sessions split 50/50 between control and treatment.

Treatment: separate the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start entry from the assisted path. No changes to eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or support-routing rules.

Primary threshold: at least a 25% relative reduction in Helio Start eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition.

Guardrails:
• Eligible-workspace admission completion declines by no more than 1.5 percentage points.
• Account-level support time at the 90th percentile increases by no more than 10 minutes.

Measurement and decision:
• Owen will provide three complete weekly cohorts plus the November 10–16 stabilization cohort.
• Priya will make the result decision on November 25.

Exclusions during the test: paid traffic, pipeline targets, forecast credit, and unrelated pricing-page layout or UI changes.

Purpose
Run the approved Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test as a controlled live test without changing scope or existing operating rules.

Status and launch
LIVE as of October 20, 2025. Daniela launched the test at a 50/50 split for organic pricing-page sessions after the audience, path-selection, admission, and support-routing events passed validation. This is a live experiment, not a default rollout: treatment is not the default experience, and launch does not imply a result before the stabilized read.

Design
- Audience: organic pricing-page sessions only.
- Allocation: 50/50 control and treatment.
- Treatment: separate the bounded under-50, simple-deployment Helio Start path from the assisted path.
- Control: existing pricing-page path.
- Customer Success retains the existing assisted routes.

Passed validations and unchanged boundaries
Audience, path-selection, admission, and support-routing events passed validation. Ines confirmed that treatment introduces no new lifecycle branch. Admission, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, assisted support-routing, and acquisition boundaries are unchanged.

Clean-attribution freeze and exclusions
Unrelated pricing-page layout and UI work is frozen through the November 16 stabilization cohort. Paid traffic, pipeline targets, and forecast credit remain excluded.

Decision criteria
- Primary threshold: at least a 25% relative reduction in eligibility-flow starts that later route out for an existing unsupported condition.
- Guardrail: eligible-workspace admission completion may decline by no more than 1.5 percentage points.
- Guardrail: account-level support time at the 90th percentile may increase by no more than 10 minutes.

Readout and decision
Owen will read three complete weekly cohorts plus the November 10–16 stabilization cohort. The stabilization cohort is required before the result is interpreted. Result-decision date: November 25, 2025. The live test neither makes treatment the default experience nor implies a result before the stabilized read.

input.body:
Helio Start intake regression lineage — 2024-04-23

Historical baseline card

Purpose
Regression-lineage fixture for the approved public-path admission checklist as of 2024-04-23, with the later connector-access input added at that cutover. Historical baseline only; this card does not change live eligibility, routing, lifecycle, or admission behavior.

Inputs

The baseline has seven independent admission inputs:

1. Account is under 50 seats.
2. Helio admin proof is present.
3. Deployment is simple.
4. First-week integration fit is present.
5. Entitlement state is current.
6. Billing is supported.
7. Connector access is definite Yes for the selected supported connector: the applicant expects to be able to authenticate that connector account during the first week.

Connector-access lineage

The connector-access answer is stored separately from Helio admin proof. A definite Yes continues through the otherwise unchanged checks. No and Not sure remain pending and route to assistance before workspace admission; the pending state does not admit a workspace or grant connector access. Connection prompts remain suppressed while connector-access proof is pending. No passwords, tokens, API keys, secrets, or another person’s credentials belong in the intake answer.

Regression cases

Case A — admitted baseline

All seven inputs present:
- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: ADMITTED through the public self-serve path.

Case B — non-admitted: account-size input missing

- Under 50 seats: missing
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; route out of the public self-serve path under the existing account-boundary rule.

Case C — non-admitted: Helio admin-proof input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: missing
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; required admin proof is absent.

Case D — non-admitted: deployment-simplicity input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: missing / complex
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; route out rather than entering the bounded self-serve path.

Case E — non-admitted: first-week integration-fit input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: missing
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; required first-week integration fit is absent.

Case F — non-admitted: current-entitlement input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: missing / stale
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; current entitlement is required.

Case G — non-admitted: supported-billing input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: missing / unsupported
- Connector access: definite Yes

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED; route to the applicable assisted path rather than self-serve.

Case H — non-admitted: connector-access input missing

- Under 50 seats: present
- Helio admin proof: present
- Simple deployment: present
- First-week integration fit: present
- Current entitlement: present
- Supported billing: present
- Connector access: missing / unresolved (No or Not sure)

Expected outcome: NOT ADMITTED before workspace admission; keep pending and route to assistance. Do not issue connection prompts while connector-access proof is unresolved.

Lineage and interpretation controls

- Case A is the sole admitted fixture.
- Cases B–H each omit exactly one input; no case combines two missing inputs.
- Every non-target input is held present in Cases B–H so failures remain attributable to one input.
- This is a regression baseline, not causal evidence and not a claim that any single input alone causes admission.
- Existing route-out conditions remain unchanged, including agencies, unresolved ownership, manual billing, imports, migrations, unsupported permissions, and other unsupported cases.
- A connector-access Yes answer does not replace Helio admin proof, establish external-system authority, override route-out conditions, or guarantee successful integration.
- Historical reference: connector-access change live in the public-pricing-page intake on 2024-04-23; the evaluation boundary is descriptive and noncausal.

requirement.criterion:
The document clearly presents the matrix as the live Helio Start intake baseline on April 23, 2024, and explicitly avoids presenting it as the later or current intake path.

The document contains a compact acceptance-test matrix that (1) has a positive case where every required input is satisfied and the expected result is admitted, and (2) has a separate negative case for each of these high-level inputs: account is under 50, admin proof is present, deployment is simple, first-week integration fit is present, a current entitlement state is present, and billing is supported. Each negative case must show that the applicant is not admitted when that input is absent or unsatisfied. The first-week integration-fit case must reflect the April 23 connector-access design: the applicant must definitely be able to authenticate the selected supported connector; a No or Not sure answer remains pending and routes to assistance before admission. Connector access must not be conflated with Helio admin proof. Equivalent concise labels for non-admission, pending, assisted routing, or ineligibility are acceptable where they preserve these outcomes.

arguments.title: December 10 board operating segment — evidence scaffold
arguments.body:
December 5 board pre-read format
December 10 board operating segment — evidence scaffold

PAGE 1 OF 6 — OPENING FRAME

Purpose
This pre-read is an evidence scaffold, not a combined growth narrative. It presents four separate lanes with separate denominators, outcome windows, evidence standards, and certification states.

Reading rule
Only the system-controls lane contains certified October evidence. Helio Start and retained-mid Expansion Assist remain unfinished evidence placeholders. Pricing-page path quality remains explicitly pending the stabilized Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test read.

Boundary
Do not combine the lanes into one growth number or infer revenue, acquisition, pipeline, customer-outcome, or forecast impact where the relevant evidence is not complete and certified. Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not causal.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 2 OF 6 — HELIO START

Status: UNFINISHED EVIDENCE PLACEHOLDER

Board question
What mature Helio Start status and operating performance can be supported once the evidence package is complete?

Required evidence before a claim
- Verified population definition, inclusion/exclusion rules, denominator, source, and extraction date: [pending]
- Complete outcome window, maturity/follow-up rule, and completeness check: [pending]
- Mature-status result: [pending certification]
- Refund-adjusted cash definition, reconciliation, and result: [pending certification]
- Account-level support-effort definition, attribution rule, coverage, and result: [pending certification]
- Unresolved records, exclusions, and limitations: [pending]

Permitted framing
Describe mature status only where maturity is verified, paired with refund-adjusted cash and account-level support effort.

Explicit limits
Do not present unadjusted bookings, gross revenue, incomplete support signals, acquisition implications, pipeline implications, or forecast implications as certified outcomes. No board-facing claim until the denominator, complete outcome window, limits, and certification are recorded.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 3 OF 6 — RETAINED-MID EXPANSION ASSIST

Status: UNFINISHED EVIDENCE PLACEHOLDER

Board question
What retained-mid Expansion Assist activity and observed outcomes can be described from a complete, verified window?

Required evidence before a claim
- Retained-mid population and Expansion Assist exposure/observation definitions: [pending]
- Verified denominator, source, and extraction date: [pending]
- Complete outcome window and retention/observation maturity rule: [pending]
- Descriptive result and outcome-window result: [pending certification]
- Selection effects, exposure differences, missingness, concurrent interventions, and other caveats: [pending]

Permitted framing
Report who or what was observed, when, and which outcomes were recorded.

Explicit limits
Do not claim that Expansion Assist caused expansion, retention, or any other outcome. Causal analysis is not established. Do not combine this lane with Helio Start, pricing-page path quality, or system controls, and do not infer revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast impact.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 4 OF 6 — PRICING-PAGE PATH QUALITY

Status: PENDING STABILIZED TEST READ

Board question
What does the stabilized Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test show about pricing-page path quality?

Current state
The test read is not yet stabilized for board use. Preserve this lane as a placeholder; do not substitute interim observations for the stabilized read.

Required evidence before a claim
- Final test assignment, eligibility, exclusions, path definition, and verified denominator: [pending stabilized read]
- Complete test outcome window and maturity/completeness check: [pending stabilized read]
- Instrumentation checks and analysis plan: [pending]
- Certified pricing-page path-quality result and interpretation: [pending completion and certification]

Explicit limits
No interim path-quality result, uplift claim, acquisition conclusion, revenue conclusion, pipeline conclusion, or forecast conclusion is certified. Do not merge this lane with the other three lanes.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 5 OF 6 — SYSTEM CONTROLS

Status: CERTIFIED OCTOBER CS AUTO-NUDGE EVIDENCE

Board question
Did the CS auto-nudge control account for and handle scheduled decisions under the recorded state during the certified window?

Dated evidence
- Evidence packet: October 1–31, 2025
- Certification: Owen, November 5, 2025
- Decision unit: each scheduled decision appears once with one disposition; warnings, holds, checks, and reevaluations remain linked audit history and are not additional denominator rows
- Verified denominator: 1,026 unique decisions

Certified outcomes
- 41 visible field-specific holds
- 985 decisions proceeded or were suppressed on current state
- No governed-field disagreement identified
- No customer correction identified
- No adjacent eligibility-assuming lifecycle message sent to held or suppressed records
- No rollback occurred

Evidence boundary
This supports system-control performance only: decision accounting, state-based handling, holds, suppressions, message exclusion, and the recorded audit outcomes for this population and window. It does not establish revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, customer-outcome lift, or causal impact. The absence of an observed disagreement, correction, adjacent message, or rollback is limited to the certified population and window; it is not a claim that such events cannot occur outside it.

Certification record
Owen / November 5, 2025 / October CS auto-nudge packet. No broader failure-rate or business-performance claim is supported by this packet.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 6 OF 6 — CLAIMS-AND-EXCLUSIONS MATRIX

Lane | Board-usable claim now | Required evidence / status | Exclusions

Helio Start | None beyond a clearly labeled placeholder; eventual claim must pair verified mature status with refund-adjusted cash and account-level support effort. | Denominator, complete outcome window, definitions, reconciliation, support coverage, and certification pending. | Unadjusted bookings, gross revenue, incomplete support signals, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, and causal claims.

Retained-mid Expansion Assist | None beyond a clearly labeled descriptive placeholder. | Denominator, exposure definition, complete observation window, descriptive results, and caveats pending. | Causal expansion/retention claims; revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or blended-growth claims.

Pricing-page path quality | None until the stabilized Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test read is complete and certified. | Final assignment/eligibility/exclusions, denominator, complete window, instrumentation checks, analysis, and certification pending. | Interim result, uplift, acquisition, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claims.

System controls / CS auto-nudge | For October 1–31, 2025: 1,026 unique decisions; 41 visible field-specific holds; 985 proceeded or were suppressed on current state; no observed governed-field disagreement, customer correction, adjacent message to held/suppressed records, or rollback. | Certified by Owen on November 5, 2025; limited to the named packet, population, and window. | Revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, customer-outcome lift, causal impact, broader failure-rate, or aggregate-growth claims.

Cross-lane control
- Keep all four lanes visibly separate, with separate denominators and outcome windows.
- Do not create a blended score, aggregate performance claim, or single growth number.
- Every board-facing number must name its denominator, outcome window, source, exclusions, and certification status.
- Claims not supported by a completed, certified lane remain exclusions—not placeholders to be filled with interpretation.
- Final cross-lane reviewer/sign-off: [pending].

arguments.title: December 10 board operating segment — 8-minute talk track
arguments.body:
DECEMBER 10 BOARD OPERATING SEGMENT — 8-MINUTE TALK TRACK

Purpose

This is a delivery aid derived only from the finalized six-page pre-read delivered Friday. It is not a replacement evidence source and does not change the pre-read’s four lanes, denominators, complete outcome windows, or claims-and-exclusions matrix.

Target timing: about 8 minutes of prepared remarks, leaving about 12 minutes for questions in the 10:10–10:30am segment.

Delivery rule

Keep the four lanes visibly separate. Name the denominator and outcome window for each lane. Do not read every supporting detail aloud; direct questions to the corresponding page of the finalized pre-read. Do not create a combined growth, revenue, acquisition, or causal number.

0:00–0:45 — Opening frame

“Today’s read has four certified lanes, each answering a different question: Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and system controls. I’ll keep their denominators, outcome windows, and evidence limits separate. The claims-and-exclusions matrix on page 6 remains the governing boundary; this is not a blended growth read.”

“The short version is: Helio Start remains bounded organic through March 31, 2026; Expansion Assist is descriptive rather than causal; pricing-page evidence is about funnel and path quality rather than revenue or acquisition; and the October system-control packet shows the recorded hold, suppression, and message-separation controls.”

0:45–2:15 — Lane 1: Helio Start

“Helio Start remains a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026. Paid acquisition does not reopen before that boundary.”

“The evidence unit is 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 observation windows. At the fixed day-90 checkpoint, 61 were paid-active, 11 had canceled before day 90, six were past due, and four were on billing hold. Activation here means paid-active at that fixed checkpoint divided by the admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. The mature packet’s account-level support p90 was 70 minutes.”

“The reopening condition is explicit: a capped paid-acquisition proposal may be reopened only after two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes. Paid-acquisition cohorts must remain separate from organic cohorts, and any later proposal would also need mature retention evidence and refund-adjusted cash evidence.”

“This lane supports early activation, day-90 status, and setup/support-load decisions within the stated window. It does not support general availability, pricing-page performance, revenue, retention beyond the checkpoint, or paid-acquisition economics.”

2:15–3:30 — Lane 2: Retained-mid Expansion Assist

“Expansion Assist remains bounded and observational. The certified extract covers two bounded pilots and 43 actual retained-mid account exposures. Both pilots had closed, complete 45-day outcome windows as of December 1.”

“Within those approved windows, 13 of 43 exposures had help-or-options requests and nine of 43 produced expansions. Those are descriptive counts. This board read does not compare treated accounts with a valid randomized holdout, and it does not establish that a prompt caused a request or an expansion.”
