arguments.title: December 10 board operating segment — evidence scaffold
arguments.body:
December 5 board pre-read format
December 10 board operating segment — evidence scaffold

PAGE 1 OF 6 — OPENING FRAME

Purpose
This pre-read is an evidence scaffold, not a combined growth narrative. It presents four separate lanes with separate denominators, outcome windows, evidence standards, and certification states.

Reading rule
The Helio Start, system-controls, and retained-mid Expansion Assist lanes contain certified evidence within their stated windows and limits. Pricing-page path quality is implemented for the default organic experience, but its evidence remains limited to the certified stabilized test read and the narrow path-quality interpretation recorded on page 4.

Boundary
Do not combine the lanes into one growth number or infer revenue, acquisition, pipeline, customer-outcome, or forecast impact where the relevant evidence is not complete and certified. Expansion Assist remains descriptive, not causal. The certified Helio Start mature-cohort evidence and Priya’s final December 3 Q1 gate decision are recorded on page 2; the decision does not reduce the gate to a single conversion number.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 2 OF 6 — HELIO START

Status: CERTIFIED MATURE-COHORT EVIDENCE; Q1 GATE DECIDED

Board question
What mature Helio Start status and operating performance are supported by the completed mature-cohort packet, and what Q1 exposure decision follows from it?

Certification and scope
- Owen and Customer Success provided the completed mature Helio Start packet on December 2, 2025, after the Tuesday 1:1.
- Decision unit / denominator: 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows.
- Mature cohort status: 61 paid-active, 11 canceled, six past due, and four on billing hold.
- The status counts cover all 82 admitted workspaces.

Certified cash evidence
- Gross billed cash: $95,420.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash: $89,110.
- Use the refund-adjusted collected-cash figure for the collected-cash result; do not substitute gross billed cash for it.

Certified support-effort evidence
- Account-level support effort: 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile.
- Seven accounts exceeded 90 minutes of support effort. State this high-support tail plainly: all seven involved external-authority or ownership assistance.

Admitted-path exclusions
- No manual-billing case entered the admitted path.
- No import case entered the admitted path.
- No migration case entered the admitted path.
- No agency case entered the admitted path.

Priya’s final Q1 gate decision — December 3, 2025
- After reviewing the mature Helio Start packet, Priya decided that Helio Start will remain a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026.
- There will be no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit during this bounded period.
- The high-support tail remains above 5%: seven of the 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows exceeded 90 support minutes.
- A capped paid-acquisition proposal can be reopened only after two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes and no unsupported case enters the admitted path.
- Any reopened capped paid-acquisition proposal would still require separate budget approval.
- The gate remains multi-dimensional: continue to pair day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort; do not reduce the decision to one conversion number.

Permitted framing
Among 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, the certified mature cohort contained 61 paid-active workspaces, 11 canceled workspaces, six past-due workspaces, and four workspaces on billing hold. The cohort produced $95,420 in gross billed cash and $89,110 in refund-adjusted collected cash. Account-level support effort was 20 minutes at the median and 70 minutes at the 90th percentile; seven accounts exceeded 90 minutes, and all seven involved external-authority or ownership assistance. Priya’s final Q1 decision keeps Helio Start as a bounded organic pricing-page channel through March 31, 2026, with no paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit. The decision gate continues to pair day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort rather than relying on a single conversion number.

Evidence limits and decision boundary
- This is certified cohort-status, cash, and support-effort evidence for the named admitted population and complete day-90 windows. It does not establish causality or generalize beyond the stated population and window.
- The absence of manual-billing, import, migration, or agency cases in the admitted path is a scope/exclusion statement, not evidence about those cases outside the admitted path.
- The bounded organic pricing-page channel ends at the stated March 31, 2026 boundary unless a separately approved decision changes it.
- No paid-acquisition test, pipeline target, or forecast credit is authorized by this decision.
- Reopening is not permitted unless two consecutive mature cohorts each have fewer than 5% of accounts exceeding 90 support minutes and no unsupported case enters the admitted path; a capped paid-acquisition proposal would still need separate budget approval.
- Do not infer revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast impact beyond the certified cash measures, stated cohort evidence, and explicit decision boundaries.

Certification record
Owen and Customer Success / December 2, 2025 / completed mature Helio Start packet covering 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows. Priya / December 3, 2025 / final Q1 gate decision after review of the mature packet.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 3 OF 6 — RETAINED-MID EXPANSION ASSIST

Status: CERTIFIED DESCRIPTIVE RESULT — TWO BOUNDED PILOTS

Board question
What retained-mid Expansion Assist activity and observed outcomes were recorded across the two bounded pilots’ complete outcome windows?

Certified denominator and scope
- Certification: Owen and Ines delivered the certified Expansion Assist extract on December 1, 2025.
- Scope: two bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows.
- Decision unit / denominator: 43 actual Expansion Assist exposures across the two pilots.
- Pilot composition: the first pilot contributed 30 exposures; the second cohort contributed the remaining 13 exposures.
- The product-visible usage-ceiling requirement was newly crossed within the prior 14 days only for the second cohort.
- Of the first pilot’s 30 exposures, 18 had an older usage-ceiling event; they remain included in the certified actual-exposure denominator because the newer-crossing requirement did not apply to that cohort.

Complete outcome window
- Outcome windows: both bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows.
- Window maturity rule: report outcomes observed through the full 45-day window for each pilot.
- Window completeness check: complete for both certified pilot windows.
- Certified descriptive outcomes within those windows: 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions.

Standing-lane operating rule
- The current standing lane remains narrow, behavior-based, and state-specific.
- An active Customer Success adoption or renewal work state suppresses a commercial prompt.
- The lane is not a general commercial or lifecycle rollout; the certified extract does not override those suppression rules.

Permitted framing
Across the two bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows, 43 actual exposures were associated with 13 help-or-options requests and nine expansions. This is descriptive evidence about recorded exposures and observed outcomes.

Evidence limits
- There was no randomized control; the evidence is descriptive rather than causal.
- Do not claim that Expansion Assist caused expansion, retention, help-seeking, or any other outcome.
- Do not treat the first pilot’s 18 older usage-ceiling events as newly crossed within 14 days; that requirement applied only to the second cohort.
- Selection effects, exposure differences, the cohort-specific ceiling-event rule, missingness, concurrent interventions, and state-based suppression limit interpretation.
- The lane remains outside pipeline, revenue commitments, and forecast credit.
- Do not combine this lane with Helio Start, pricing-page path quality, or system controls, and do not infer revenue, acquisition, pipeline, or forecast impact from these descriptive observations.

Certification record
Owen and Ines / December 1, 2025 / certified Expansion Assist extract covering the two bounded pilots’ closed, complete 45-day windows.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 4 OF 6 — PRICING-PAGE PATH QUALITY

Status: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — DEFAULT ORGANIC EXPERIENCE

Board question
What does the certified Q4 Pricing Path Clarity Test show about pricing-page path quality, and what was implemented?

Certified test evidence
- Test window: October 20–November 16, 2025; four-cohort read certified by Owen on November 19, 2025.
- Denominator: 3,286 organic pricing-page sessions; 1,639 control and 1,647 treatment.
- Helio Start eligibility-flow starts routing out for an existing unsupported condition: 38/344 control (11.0%) versus 25/352 treatment (7.1%), a 35.7% relative reduction.
- Eligible-workspace admission completion: 43.8% control versus 44.1% treatment.
- Account-level support time at P90: 71 minutes control versus 74 minutes treatment.
- Favorable direction held across all three weekly cohorts and the November 10–16 stabilization cohort.
- Attribution check: no unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change occurred during the test.
- The predeclared path-quality threshold and both guardrails passed.

Implementation state — November 26, 2025
Priya approved the tested path-separated design as the default organic pricing-page experience on November 25 and authorized Daniela to move it to 100% on November 26. Daniela completed that rollout on November 26: the path-separated treatment is now 100% of organic pricing-page traffic and the control is retired. Post-rollout checks show that the existing path-selection, eligibility, admission, and support-routing events continue to populate without a taxonomy change.

Narrow interpretation
The default organic experience now gives bounded Helio Start and assisted needs separate entry paths. The evidence supports fewer unsupported self-serve starts and funnel-quality evidence only. It is not revenue, paid-acquisition, pipeline, forecast, or eligibility evidence, and the implementation does not change the existing operating boundaries.

Unchanged boundaries
Eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules remain unchanged. Paid-acquisition boundaries remain unchanged because this evidence and rollout concern organic pricing-page traffic only. Pipeline targets and forecast credit remain excluded. No unrelated pricing-page layout or UI change was introduced.

Explicit limits
Do not turn the path-quality result or rollout into a revenue, acquisition, paid-acquisition, pipeline, or forecast claim. Do not infer a change to eligibility or refusal rules, connector access, external-authority handling, lifecycle behavior, instrumentation taxonomy, or support routing. Keep this lane separate from Helio Start, retained-mid Expansion Assist, and system controls.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 5 OF 6 — SYSTEM CONTROLS

Status: CERTIFIED OCTOBER CS AUTO-NUDGE EVIDENCE

Board question
Did the CS auto-nudge control account for and handle scheduled decisions under the recorded state during the certified window?

Dated evidence
- Evidence packet: October 1–31, 2025
- Certification: Owen, November 5, 2025
- Decision unit: each scheduled decision appears once with one disposition; warnings, holds, checks, and reevaluations remain linked audit history and are not additional denominator rows
- Verified denominator: 1,026 unique decisions

Certified outcomes
- 41 visible field-specific holds
- 985 decisions proceeded or were suppressed on current state
- No governed-field disagreement identified
- No customer correction identified
- No adjacent eligibility-assuming lifecycle message sent to held or suppressed records
- No rollback occurred

Evidence boundary
This supports system-control performance only: decision accounting, state-based handling, holds, suppressions, message exclusion, and the recorded audit outcomes for this population and window. It does not establish revenue, acquisition, pipeline, forecast, customer-outcome lift, or causal impact. The absence of an observed disagreement, correction, adjacent message, or rollback is limited to the certified population and window; it is not a claim that such events cannot occur outside it.

Certification record
Owen / November 5, 2025 / October CS auto-nudge packet. No broader failure-rate or business-performance claim is supported by this packet.

--- PAGE BREAK ---

PAGE 6 OF 6 — CLAIMS-AND-EXCLUSIONS MATRIX

Lane | Board-usable claim now | Required evidence / status | Exclusions

Helio Start | Among 82 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, 61 were paid-active, 11 canceled, six were past due, and four were on billing hold. arguments.title: Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine
arguments.body:
Helio Start pre-discovery readout — measurement spine

Purpose
This pre-read frames the baseline for Monday discussion. The goal is to define and validate an initial eligibility model, not to declare a universal under-50-seat segment, a final eligibility threshold, or a pricing boundary.

1) Helio Start is a working name, not a launch promise

“Helio Start” is a working name for pre-discovery and eligibility-model work. It is not a launch commitment, product announcement, or promise that every under-50-seat account will qualify.

The baseline is directional: it identifies onboarding conditions that may predict activation and administrative burden. It does not prove that seat count is irrelevant, that all under-50-seat accounts are good candidates, or that the observed activation pattern will generalize across every acquisition source, deployment model, or future cohort.

2) Measurement method

Use activation definition v3 for the primary outcome. Before interpreting any rate, label the relevant month explicitly as signup month, first-integration month, activation-completion month, or report-extraction month; do not leave the month label implicit.

Keep the current 75–200-seat mid-segment v2 band separate from the Helio Start view. Show the 50–75-seat band separately as its own comparison column or cut rather than folding it into either population.

Lead with onboarding conditions, with seat band as a secondary breakdown. The initial cuts should distinguish:

- Simple versus complex deployment shape.
- First integration completed in week one versus not completed in week one.
- Administrative dependencies: permissions required, import help required, billing exception required, and migration support required.

Report activation deltas, support load, and gross retention by seat band where available. Treat the baseline as an eligibility and onboarding-complexity signal, not as evidence that administrative complexity causes the activation gap.

3) Baseline finding

Simple under-50-seat deployments with a first-week first integration behave near the target range. By contrast, deployments involving permissions, import, billing, or migration complexity lag by more than 15 points.

The practical read is that under-50-seat accounts are not a uniform activation population. Onboarding conditions and early integration readiness appear more informative for initial eligibility than seat count alone. This remains a baseline finding to validate, not a final segmentation rule.

4) Eligibility and refusal-rule implications

The first eligibility model should prioritize simple deployment and early integration readiness, then test how reliably those signals predict activation without administrative intervention.

Potential positive eligibility signals:

- A simple deployment shape.
- A first integration completed in week one, or a credible path to completing it without intervention.
- No material administrative dependency at intake.

Potential refusal or escalation rules:

- Permissions required before the account can make progress.
- Import help required.
- Billing exception required.
- Migration support required.
- A complex deployment shape or a missed first-week integration that requires manual recovery.

These should be treated as operational rules to test and refine, not as permanent exclusions. A refusal rule should route the account to the appropriate assisted path or a later review, with an explicit reason recorded. The model should be evaluated for false refusals, false acceptances, activation, support burden, and retention; it should not be reduced to “under 50 is fine” or “under 50 is bad.”

5) Open questions for Monday

Lifecycle
- Which lifecycle touchpoints can reinforce first-week integration without implying a launch promise?
- What intervention, if any, should be offered when a deployment misses the first-week integration signal?
- How should holdouts and administrative intervention be handled so that lifecycle lift is not confused with eligibility quality?

Instrumentation
- Are deployment shape, seat band, first integration timing, and each administrative-dependency flag captured consistently at intake and in the warehouse?
- Which event should be the canonical first-integration event, and how will we preserve the activation definition v3 versioning?
- What cohort and month labels will be used in the Monday readout and subsequent tracking?
- How will we separate the 75–200-seat mid-segment v2 band and the 50–75-seat band in dashboards and analyses?

Support
- What support load is associated with each dependency flag and with manual intervention versus refusal/escalation?
- What assisted path should receive accounts that fail a refusal rule?
- Can support reliably identify the dependency before intervention changes the observed activation outcome?

Engineering sizing
- What is required to capture or validate deployment shape and dependency flags at intake?
- What work is needed to make first-week integration status and activation definition v3 reliable in reporting?
- What dashboard, routing, audit-log, and experiment support is needed for a scoped eligibility test?
- What engineering capacity and timeline are required before this can move beyond pre-discovery?

Decision needed Monday
Agree on the measurement spine and the first eligibility-model validation plan, including the separate 75–200-seat v2 and 50–75-seat views, the initial refusal-rule candidates, and owners for the lifecycle, instrumentation, support, and engineering questions.

arguments.body:
Monday pre-read revisions — opener and risk labels

Opener
Helio Start is an assessment of whether a safe, self-serve setup path could serve an eligible subset of sub-50-seat customers. The refusal rules are customer-protection rules: they keep accounts that need permissions help, import help, billing exceptions, or migration support from being placed into a self-serve setup that is likely to fail them. This is an assessment, not a launch commitment or a promise of a cheap plan.

Baseline caveat
The baseline is descriptive, not causal. It shows how first-week integration and activation appear together in the observed data; it does not establish that completing an integration in the first week causes activation. Any relationship should be treated as a signal for further investigation and measurement, not as a causal claim.

Risk labels
- Needs guided setup — permissions, import help, billing exceptions, or migration support are required; exclude from the initial self-serve eligible population.
- Self-serve setup risk — the account may be placed into a setup path that cannot adequately support its requirements; apply the refusal rule to protect the customer from a failed setup.
- Eligible for self-serve assessment — no identified guided-support requirement under the current rules; this label does not imply fit, readiness, causality, launch approval, or a Q3 commitment.

arguments.title: Riley Tanaka — 2027 year-end self-review working draft
arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2027 year-end self-review working draft

Working draft for Priya’s 2027 year-end self-review window. First draft requested by November 19, 2027.

Operating-model decisions and claim discipline

I personally owned two things this year. First, I set the bounded operating frame for the November Helio Start paid batch: paid traffic stayed gated until the required paid-source trace, rollback control, staffed Customer Success coverage, and approved traffic conditions were confirmed. Priya approved the bounded batch, and Daniela authorized the November 1 launch once the operating gates were met. I maintained the approval boundary and treated the launch as live operational work, not as evidence of a mature acquisition outcome.

Second, I set the four-lane claim limits for the work. My lane was the operating decision and the explicit boundary around what could be claimed. Owen owned measurement, denominators, reporting semantics, source completeness, and exception reporting. Ines owned lifecycle governance, owner-state certification, and message-state work. Daniela owned source reliability, engineering release, rollback control, and reliability authority. I kept those lanes distinct rather than blending their evidence into a single project claim. Their contributions are material: Owen made the operating read measurable and auditable; Ines kept lifecycle and message-state decisions governed; and Daniela made the live enablement and rollback boundary reliable.

The four lanes also defined what I deliberately kept out of the self-review claims: pipeline and forecast treatment; early mature claims for the live cohort; and automatic expansion beyond the fifth consumer. I did not convert a small live-batch read into claims about acquisition efficiency, retention, or scale, and I did not treat the fifth-consumer reminder as a reason to expand the shared-state model automatically. December development outcomes also remain open; October and November evidence is progress, not completion of the required October–December cycle.

For the November paid batch, I made the operating decision and maintained the approval boundary; I did not claim ownership of the supporting measurement, lifecycle-state certification, source reliability, release, or rollback work. That separation is an operating-model result in itself: each decision was supported by the appropriate owner evidence rather than by a blended claim.

I also made the operating-model decision to keep the incomplete-setup reminder as Lifecycle Systems’ fifth production consumer, not a sixth consumer. The model required a fresh evaluation for every possible display, with current setup, qualifying-human-admin status, active Customer Success work, and required state determining display, suppression, or hold. A held record was not treated as a queued delivery. These choices kept the reminder within the existing shared-state model and preserved the existing owner lanes. I did not authorize automatic expansion beyond that fifth consumer, and I do not claim ownership of the reminder’s implementation or day-to-day execution.

Evidence and bounded outcomes

I have been deliberate about distinguishing what was decided, what was observed, and what remains unproven. The November 1–7 reminder operation had 12,480 fresh evaluations. Of those, 1,615 displayed, 520 were suppressed because current Customer Success work was active, 186 were held because required state was missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting, and 10,159 did not display because current setup or qualifying-human-admin conditions were not met. These are operating counts, not claims of customer impact, durable behavior change, or mature performance.

The paid-batch evidence is similarly bounded. By Owen’s November 5 operating snapshot, 12 paid-source eligibility-flow starts had reached final states: five admitted, four assisted, and three ineligible, with $1,580 in spend. Paid-source attribution reconciled through every final route, and no unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. This is a live operational-status read, not a mature-outcome read for the live cohort. The formal support-pause monitor had not begun because the admission count was still below its threshold. I will continue to avoid converting early routing and control evidence into claims about acquisition efficiency, retention, or scale.

The evidence boundary also requires acknowledging what did not occur during the November 1–7 reminder interval: no reusable audience was created, no failed rollback occurred, no incident stop was triggered, and no customer correction was recorded. Those facts demonstrate the bounded state of the operation; they do not prove that the system is broadly mature or that future intervals will behave the same way.

Team development

My leadership goal has been to make ownership legible and to develop independent operating judgment without absorbing other people’s lanes. Owen’s measurement and exception-reporting work includes definitions, denominators, bounded operating snapshots, source-completeness checks, and exception synthesis. Ines’s work includes lifecycle governance, owner-state certification, lifecycle-risk explanation, and message-state transitions and controls. Daniela’s work includes source-integrity and reliability checks, production enablement, engineering release control, and rollback readiness.

The Q4 development focuses for Owen and Ines remain open through the required December cycle. October and November submissions are evidence of progress, not completion of the October–December focus. Owen’s November operating read and Ines’s November lifecycle-risk explanation should be credited to their respective lanes, while each focus remains open until the required December cycle is completed and reviewed. I am preserving that status rather than prematurely marking either development focus complete. Daniela’s engineering authority likewise remains intact rather than being treated as a substitute for my operating decisions.

System reliability

My contribution to reliability was to make the operating boundaries explicit: approval gates, fresh state evaluation, held-versus-queued semantics, active-work suppression, staffed backup handling, and a clear stop/correction boundary. The November paid batch launched only after the control evidence was available. Daniela verified the live enable and rollback controls and retained engineering authority. Ines maintained the lifecycle and message-state boundary. Owen provided the bounded measurement and exception read. The reminder operation’s agreed reporting, lifecycle, and reminder outcomes show that the five-consumer operation remained coherent during the observed interval; they do not make me the owner of the underlying implementation or execution.

I do not interpret the absence of a failed rollback, incident stop, or customer correction as proof that reliability work is finished. The right claim is narrower: the controls were exercised in a bounded live interval without those recorded events, and the owner lanes and escalation boundaries held. Continued operation and the required December cycle are still needed before making broader claims.

Next-cycle focus

In the next cycle, I will continue to make explicit, reversible operating decisions with approval gates and evidence boundaries visible in the working record. I want to improve the handoff from live operating status to a genuinely mature outcome read: clear thresholds, complete observation windows, denominator discipline, and an explicit decision about when evidence is sufficient for expansion, continuation, or pause.

I will keep the five-consumer reminder operation within its current shared-state contract while reviewing held, suppressed, and displayed paths for operational clarity rather than optimizing display volume. I will also preserve the distinction between my decision lane and the owner lanes: Owen’s measurement and exception synthesis, Ines’s lifecycle governance and message-state work, and Daniela’s source reliability, engineering release, and rollback control. Finally, I will keep Owen’s and Ines’s Q4 development focuses open until the required December cycle is complete, then use the owner-reviewed evidence to decide what should carry forward into 2028.

Priya’s November 15 review comment has been incorporated: the draft now leads with Riley’s ownership of the bounded paid-batch operating frame and four-lane claim limits; Owen, Ines, and Daniela are credited explicitly without attributing their execution to Riley; the exclusions cover pipeline and forecast treatment, early mature claims for the live cohort, and automatic expansion beyond the fifth consumer; and December development outcomes remain open.

Evidence bank — year-end first-draft expansion

The clearest evidence of my 2027 contribution is not a broad growth claim; it is the bounded Helio Start proposal and the claim discipline I owned around it. I translated the opportunity into a controlled paid-search batch with explicit attribution safeguards, pause and stop conditions, and staffing and support-clock requirements. I also set the evidence boundary before launch: operating activity could be reported descriptively, but the new batch could not support mature customer-outcome claims until the fixed cohort had complete day-90 observation windows. I did not treat launch authorization as proof of effectiveness, and I did not authorize an additional paid batch by implication.

I own the proposal, the operating limits, and the language of the claims. Priya deserves explicit credit for approving the batch and the high-intent paid-search traffic. Daniela deserves explicit credit for the final November 1 launch authorization and for verifying the live enable control. Those approvals were essential to execution, but they are distinct from my ownership of the bounded design, attribution guardrails, stop conditions, support coverage requirements, and evidence limits.

The current paid batch should be described as live operational work, not mature evidence. The November 10 support-monitor evaluation recorded 23 paid-source eligibility-flow starts; attribution reconciled for all 23, with 7 reaching the assisted route and 10 reaching the admitted route. These are useful operating observations about routing and instrumentation. They are not a mature outcome read, not a causal acquisition result, and not evidence of downstream retention, revenue, or scale. The fixed cohort still needs complete day-90 windows before those claims can be considered.

Four-lane year-end evidence framing

1. Helio Start customer outcomes. This lane covers the bounded proposal, admissions, activation and downstream outcome windows, with paid-source attribution kept separate from outcome interpretation. My exclusions are explicit: no mature outcome claim for the November batch before complete day-90 windows; no causal, revenue, pipeline, acquisition-efficiency, scale, or forecast claim from live-batch counts; and no assumption that admitted or assisted routing is equivalent to successful customer value.

2. Expansion Assist. This remains a distinct lane from Helio Start setup and lifecycle work. The framing is limited to the certified source, denominator, outcome-window, and operating evidence actually available. I exclude combining Expansion Assist with Helio Start to create a larger or cleaner-looking result, and I exclude unsupported causal or business-impact claims where the source only supports descriptive operating facts.

3. Pricing-page path quality. This lane is about path quality and unsupported-path starts, not a general conversion or growth claim. I exclude treating path-quality continuity as proof of incremental revenue, pipeline, acquisition performance, or causal lift. Any conclusion must preserve the applicable denominator, period, and the distinction between a cleaner route and a downstream customer outcome.

4. System controls and reliability. This lane covers governed-state consumption, send or suppress behavior, source integrity, release controls, rollback readiness, and exception handling. I exclude turning reliable control behavior into a claim of customer or financial impact without a separate outcome source. I also keep release readiness, operational safety, and message-state correctness visibly separate from the three customer or path-quality lanes.

This four-lane framing is also an exclusion mechanism: each lane keeps its own owner, denominator, source completeness, outcome window, reliability evidence, and unresolved gaps. arguments.body:
Riley Tanaka — 2027 year-end self-review working draft

Working draft for Priya’s 2027 year-end self-review window. First draft requested by November 19, 2027.

Operating-model decisions

My contribution this year was to make bounded operating-model decisions, preserve explicit approval gates, and keep decisions separate from measurement, lifecycle-state governance, and engineering control. I set the decision frame and operating boundaries for the November Helio Start paid batch: paid traffic stayed gated until the required paid-source trace, rollback control, staffed Customer Success coverage, and approved traffic conditions were confirmed. I then supported the controlled November 1 launch rather than treating the launch gate as evidence of a mature acquisition outcome. I retained the decision rights for customer correction and incident-stop decisions in the Growth reminder lane.

I also helped establish the incomplete-setup reminder as Lifecycle Systems’ fifth production consumer, not a sixth consumer. The operating model required a fresh evaluation for every possible display, with current setup, qualifying-human-admin status, active Customer Success work, and required state determining display, suppression, or hold. A held record was not treated as a queued delivery. These choices kept the reminder within the existing shared-state model and preserved the existing owner lanes.

For the November paid batch, I made the operating decision and maintained the approval boundary; I did not claim ownership of the supporting measurement, lifecycle-state certification, source reliability, release, or rollback work. Owen Pham owned measurement, reporting semantics, and exception reporting. Ines Kovac owned lifecycle governance and message-state work. Daniela owned source reliability, engineering release, and rollback control. That separation is an operating-model result in itself: each decision was supported by the appropriate owner evidence rather than by a blended claim.

Evidence and claim discipline

I have been deliberate about distinguishing what was decided, what was observed, and what remains unproven. The November 1–7 reminder operation had 12,480 fresh evaluations. Of those, 1,615 displayed, 520 were suppressed because current Customer Success work was active, 186 were held because required state was missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting, and 10,159 did not display because current setup or qualifying-human-admin conditions were not met. These are operating counts, not claims of customer impact, durable behavior change, or mature performance.

The paid-batch evidence is similarly bounded. By Owen’s November 5 operating snapshot, 12 paid-source eligibility-flow starts had reached final states: five admitted, four assisted, and three ineligible, with $1,580 in spend. Paid-source attribution reconciled through every final route, and no unsupported applicant entered the admitted path. This is a live operating-status read, not a mature-outcome read. The formal support-pause monitor had not begun because the admission count was still below its threshold. I will continue to avoid converting early routing and control evidence into claims about acquisition efficiency, retention, or scale.

The evidence boundary also requires acknowledging what did not occur during the November 1–7 reminder interval: no reusable audience was created, no failed rollback occurred, no incident stop was triggered, and no customer correction was recorded. Those facts demonstrate the bounded state of the operation; they do not prove that the system is broadly mature or that future intervals will behave the same way.

Team development

My leadership goal has been to make ownership legible and to develop independent operating judgment without absorbing other people’s lanes. Owen’s measurement and exception-reporting work includes definitions, denominators, bounded operating snapshots, and exception synthesis. Ines’s work includes lifecycle governance, owner-state certification, lifecycle-risk explanation, and message-state transitions and controls. Daniela’s work includes source-integrity and reliability checks, production enablement, engineering release control, and rollback readiness.

The Q4 development focuses for Owen and Ines remain open through the required December cycle. October and November submissions are evidence of progress, not completion of the October–December focus. Owen’s November operating read and Ines’s November lifecycle-risk explanation should be credited to their respective lanes, while the focus remains open until the required December cycle is completed and reviewed. I am preserving that status rather than prematurely marking either development focus complete. I likewise continue to keep Daniela’s engineering authority intact rather than treating my operating decisions as a substitute for release or rollback ownership.

System reliability

The reliability improvement I helped drive was procedural as much as technical: explicit gates, fresh state evaluation, held-versus-queued semantics, active-work suppression, staffed backup handling, and a clear stop/correction boundary. The November paid batch launched only after the control evidence was available. Daniela verified the live enable and rollback controls and retained engineering authority. Ines maintained the lifecycle and message-state boundary. Owen provided the bounded measurement and exception read. The reminder operation’s agreed reporting, lifecycle, and reminder outcomes show that the five-consumer operation remained coherent during the observed interval.

I do not interpret the absence of a failed rollback, incident stop, or customer correction as proof that reliability work is finished. The right claim is narrower: the controls were exercised in a bounded live interval without those recorded events, and the owner lanes and escalation boundaries held. Continued operation and the required December cycle are still needed before making broader claims.

Next-cycle focus

In the next cycle, I will continue to make explicit, reversible operating decisions with approval gates and evidence boundaries visible in the working record. I want to improve the handoff from live operating status to a genuinely mature outcome read: clear thresholds, complete observation windows, denominator discipline, and an explicit decision about when evidence is sufficient for expansion, continuation, or pause.

I will keep the five-consumer reminder operation within its current shared-state contract while reviewing held, suppressed, and displayed paths for operational clarity rather than optimizing display volume. I will also preserve the distinction between my decision lane and the owner lanes: Owen’s measurement and exception synthesis, Ines’s lifecycle governance and message-state work, and Daniela’s source reliability, engineering release, and rollback control. Finally, I will keep Owen’s and Ines’s Q4 development focuses open until the required December cycle is complete, then use the owner-reviewed evidence to decide what should carry forward into 2028.

arguments.body:
Helio Start November 1 final-launch checklist

STATUS

SHIPPED — November 1, 2027 launch gate passed. Daniela confirmed the three required launch-day proofs and gave final authorization. The approved high-intent paid-search traffic is enabled within the boundaries below.

LAUNCH-DAY PROOFS — COMPLETE

[x] Current paid-source trace through admitted, assisted, and ineligible final routes, with held and suppressed outcomes remaining visible and not silently admitted.

[x] Live enable and rollback verification, including the ability to disable the paid source and prevent further entry while an incident, discrepancy, correction, validation, or restart decision is pending.

[x] Same-day confirmation that the Customer Success owner and named backup are staffed.

DANIELA FINAL AUTHORIZATION — COMPLETE

[x] Daniela confirmed the release and rollback controls, current paid-source trace through the final routes, and the staffed Customer Success owner-and-backup coverage, and authorized the bounded live run.

CERTIFIED Q2 EVIDENCE — HISTORICAL DESCRIPTIVE EVIDENCE ONLY

The certified Q2 evidence remains retained and separate from the new live cohort: 18 of 25 workspaces were paid-active; refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860; median support time was 33 minutes; support time at the 90th percentile was 116 minutes; and 5 of 25 workspaces were above 90 minutes. This historical evidence does not create a pipeline target, treatment, forecast credit, or mature claim for the new cohort.

OPERATING BOUNDARIES

1. Bounded batch and close rule

- Exactly one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch is in scope.
- The maximum paid-search spend is $8,000, inclusive of applicable media costs and directly attributable fees.
- The admission bound is no more than 25 admitted workspaces.
- The batch closes at the earlier of $8,000 in spend or 25 admitted workspaces.
- There is no automatic extension, replenishment, exception, or additional paid batch.
- An admitted workspace must pass the current, fresh eligibility and routing evaluation and enter the admitted path. Assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed routes are not silently counted as admissions.

2. Attribution and final-route boundary

- Paid-source reconciliation runs continuously for every paid-source eligibility-flow start from the beginning of the flow through the final terminal route.
- The final routes that must remain visible are admitted, assisted, and ineligible; held and suppressed outcomes also remain visible and must not become untracked or silently admitted endpoints.
- The operating record retains source, route, timestamps, reconciliation status, discrepancies, delayed or missing events, and owner-certified corrections.
- Prior shadow, preflight, or historical results cannot substitute for a current authoritative evaluation.

3. Eligibility, refusal, state, and routing boundaries

- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, governed-state, suppression, hold, freshness, routing, handoff, instrumentation, and assisted-routing rules remain unchanged.
- Applicants who need assistance or fall outside the criteria continue to receive the appropriate assisted or ineligible outcome.
- Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state remains visible, held, and fail-closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.
- Candidates with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work remain suppressed from the candidate path.
- No production connection, customer-facing activation, or additional production consumer is created without separate release approval.
- Affected records remain held until authoritative correction is completed, validated, and documented; a template-only override is not a correction.

4. Customer Success operating boundary

- Coverage is Monday through Friday, 8:00am–6:00pm Central, with a primary setup-desk owner and a named on-duty backup for every covered period.
- After-hours cases are handled by the named Customer Success backup at the next service opening; after-hours handling creates no unowned route and does not reset the support clock.
- Handoff begins when an admitted workspace needs owner action and carries connector, authority state, required action, route, first-contact time, and notes.
- The initial-response target is within two business hours, with Customer Success lead escalation if no owner accepts within that window.
- Account-level support minutes run continuously from first contact, including pre-admission contact where applicable, admission, handoff, and after-hours handling; handoff and after-hours treatment do not reset the clock.

5. Hard stops and pause conditions

- An unsupported applicant entering the admitted path is an immediate hard stop. Paid traffic stops pending incident review, correction, validation, and an explicit restart decision.
- The batch closes at the earlier of $8,000 in spend or 25 admitted workspaces; no further workspace may be admitted after the applicable cap is reached.
- Paid traffic pauses if paid source cannot reconcile continuously through the final route, including any material attribution discrepancy, lifecycle or suppression bypass, unresolved governed-state conflict, missing/stale/unresolved/conflicting required state, routing disagreement, staffed-handoff or continuous-support-clock failure, or routing/instrumentation failure that blocks reconciliation.
- After at least 10 admissions, traffic pauses if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes.
- The technical stop disables the paid source and prevents further entry while a hard-stop or pause condition is investigated. Restart requires documented correction, validation, fresh evaluation, and explicit owner confirmation.

6. Measurement, commercial, and claim boundaries

- The run record keeps spend; admitted, assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed counts; final-route reconciliation; continuous support minutes from first contact; stop/pause events; and owner-certified corrections.
- Attribution, lifecycle, support, and outcome reporting remain separate from pipeline and forecast treatment.
- This bounded approval creates no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. None follows automatically from spend, admissions, assisted routes, support evidence, or operating results.
- No additional paid batch is authorized.
- Results from this new cohort are not mature claims until every admitted workspace has a complete day-90 window and the applicable certifications. Paid-active status, collected cash, support outcomes, causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast impact, and general paid-growth capacity remain unavailable as mature claims before then.
- The certified Q2 evidence above remains historical descriptive evidence and must not be blended with the new cohort or used to make mature claims for it.
- No board or narrative expansion, meeting attendance, evidence certification, source-readiness check, staffing-readiness check, or operational attendance silently transfers or expands authority.

LIVE-GATE RECORD

- Priya-approved scope: one bounded high-intent paid-search batch.
- Daniela: launch-day proofs complete; live enable and rollback verified; final authorization complete.
- Customer Success: Monday–Friday, 8:00am–6:00pm Central staffed owner and named backup; after-hours cases handled at the next service opening.
- Live status: enabled only within the boundaries in this checklist; stop/pause rules remain active and controlling.
- November 1, 2027 is the live start date for this bounded run, not authority to expand scope, change rules, add a batch, assign pipeline treatment, grant forecast credit, or make mature claims before the complete day-90 windows.

The remaining assessment should use the required December cycle and preserve the same standards for denominator clarity, source completeness, and exception classification.

Ines strengthened lifecycle governance and message-state consumption. Her lane covers state transitions, routine-send controls, governed lifecycle interpretation, and audits within the established operating ceiling. The operating rule is fail closed when required state is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting: a record is held rather than treated as queued delivery, and every possible display receives a fresh evaluation under the current governed state. This is the control logic that keeps a lifecycle message from outrunning the state it is supposed to represent.

The incomplete-setup reminder is the fifth production consumer of the shared-state feed, not a sixth consumer. In the November 1–7 operating read, the fully released reminder had 12,480 fresh evaluations, including 186 evaluations held because required state was missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting. Those figures are evidence of the control operating as designed, not a claim of customer impact. The reminder's behavior belongs in the shared-state and reliability framing: it consumes governed state, can be placed on hold, and must be re-evaluated after state changes. It should not be counted as an unrelated extra system or used to inflate a customer-outcome result.

Ines's October–December Q4 development focus also remains open through the December cycle. Her demonstrated lifecycle-risk explanations and state-governance work are meaningful progress, but they do not close the development focus before the required December review. I will keep that assessment open rather than turning partial-cycle evidence into a completion claim.

Daniela's evidence covers source reliability, engineering release control, source-integrity validation, production enablement, rollback readiness, and incident-stop execution. That work made the bounded launch operable and gave the team a safe way to stop or reverse it if the source, release, or operating conditions failed. Her November 1 authorization is therefore part of the launch record, while the resulting paid-batch activity remains operational evidence pending the outcome window. I credit her for the reliability, release, and rollback work without attributing those engineering controls to mature customer or business results.

Year-end claim discipline

My role this year was to connect growth proposals to an evidence system without letting urgency erase the boundaries. The strongest version of the self-review should say that I created a bounded path to learn, secured the necessary approvals, and kept the language proportional to what the data can currently support. It should credit Priya, Daniela, Owen, and Ines for their distinct contributions; preserve the four lanes and their exclusions; call the paid batch live operational work rather than mature evidence; and leave Owen's and Ines's Q4 development focuses open through the December cycle.

arguments.body:
Helio Start bounded paid-search proposal — October 2027 working draft

APPROVED BOUNDED DECISION — AUTHORITY AND LAUNCH BOUNDARY

Priya approved one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch after reviewing this completed proposal and its certified Q2 2027 mature evidence. The approval is strictly bounded and conditional. It authorizes one batch only within the limits and gates below; it does not mean that paid traffic is live or authorize immediate launch.

Paid traffic remains off. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start date. Before any start, Daniela must confirm the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and the staffed owner-and-backup rota. All other required owner decisions, current-state checks, and launch controls remain in force.

1. Certified Q2 2027 evidence and claim boundary

Certified Q2 2027 mature descriptive evidence covers a fixed cohort of 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 2027, with complete day-90 windows:

- Customer Success certified 18 of 25 paid-active; 3 canceled; 2 past due; and 2 on billing hold.
- Owen certified $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Customer Success certified account-level support effort of 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; 5 of 25 workspaces exceeded 90 minutes.
- Daniela certified paid-source attribution for all 61 paid-source starts, with no unsupported applicant entering the admitted path, and certified the source as reliable.
- Ines certified that no lifecycle hold or suppression was bypassed.

This evidence is descriptive evidence from the fixed Q2 2027 cohort. It supports reporting the observed historical cohort outcomes and an operational support signal. It does not establish causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue or forecast impact beyond the stated collected-cash record, or that an owner checklist causes improved support. The cohort had no randomized comparison.

The prior bounded execution record is distinct: its approved test budget cap was $8,000, certified final paid-search spend was $7,640, the vendor invoice was paid in full with zero balance and $0 taxes/fees, service ran April 12–May 17, 2027, and the fixed test cohort closed at 25 admitted workspaces across 61 starts (25 admitted, 18 assisted, 18 ineligible). Traffic is off and no later batch was authorized before this decision. The prior spend, cap, staffing reference, and this approval do not create authority beyond the single batch and boundaries recorded here.

2. Certified nonproduction preflight and staffed design

Daniela and Ines certified a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight consisting of 8 expected admissions, 8 expected assisted routes, and 8 expected fail-closed, held, or suppressed outcomes. Certification covered paid-source final-route attribution; governed-state meanings; lifecycle branches, holds, and suppression; setup-step exposure; coordination ownership and backup behavior; handoff; after-hours handling; and continuous account-level support-minute treatment. All expected routes, attribution, holds/suppressions, ownership, support clock, handoff, and support-minute behavior matched design.

This is nonproduction evidence. It does not authorize traffic, a production connection, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, an eligibility/routing/ownership change, or a later launch. Any run requires a fresh evaluation; prior preflight outcomes must not be reused as a substitute for current admission decisions.

Customer Success coordination assumptions for the fixed cohort:

- Primary owner: Customer Success setup desk.
- Backup: on-duty Customer Success manager.
- Coverage: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central.
- After-hours cases queue to the named backup at the next service opening.
- Handoff begins when an admitted workspace needs owner action after admission.
- Handoff context includes connector, authority state, required action, route, first-contact time, and notes.
- Initial response target: within two business hours.
- Customer Success lead escalates if no owner accepts within the response window.
- Account-level support minutes continue from first contact; handoff and after-hours treatment do not reset the clock.

These assumptions describe coordination readiness only. Daniela's pre-start confirmation of the current staffed owner-and-backup rota is still required. The assumptions are not evidence of paid-growth capacity beyond the approved operating bound, causal lift, revenue, pipeline, or forecast impact.

3. Approved budget, admission bound, and run-close rule

- Approval owner: Priya.
- Approved scope: one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch only.
- Spend ceiling: no more than $8,000 in paid-search spend, inclusive of applicable media costs and any directly attributable fees.
- Admission bound: no more than 25 admitted workspaces.
- Run-close rule: close the batch at the earlier of the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces.
- November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start; it is not a launch date or traffic authorization.
- No automatic extension, replenishment, or second/additional paid batch is authorized.
- Spend pacing, admission definition, and exception handling must be recorded by the acquisition/operating owner before launch. An admitted workspace is one that passes the current, fresh eligibility and routing evaluation and enters the admitted path; assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed routes are not silently counted as admissions.

4. Stop, pause, staffing, and support-clock conditions

Hard stop:

- If an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path, stop the batch immediately and keep paid traffic off pending incident review, correction, and an explicit restart decision.
- Close the batch when either the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces is reached, whichever occurs first.

Pause:

- Pause if paid-source reconciliation cannot be completed from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- After at least 10 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes.
- Pause for any material attribution discrepancy, lifecycle or suppression bypass, unresolved governed-state conflict, missing/stale required state, routing disagreement, or failure of the staffed handoff/support-clock design.

A pause keeps paid traffic off until the responsible owner documents the issue, correction, validation, and restart decision. A template-only override is not a correction. Restart requires fresh evaluation and explicit owner confirmation; prior preflight or shadow outcomes cannot substitute for current decisions.

The staffed operating design remains intact: Customer Success setup desk primary owner; on-duty Customer Success manager backup; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central coverage; next-opening queue for after-hours cases; two-business-hour initial response target; escalation if no owner accepts; and continuous account-level support minutes from first contact without a clock reset at handoff or after hours. Daniela must confirm the staffed owner-and-backup rota before any start.

5. Attribution, lifecycle, eligibility, and operational safeguards

Any run under this approval must preserve all of the following:

- Reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- Daniela must confirm the current attribution endpoints before any start.
- Evaluate every candidate from current authoritative state; do not reuse prior shadow or preflight outcomes.
- Keep eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, suppression, freshness, handoff, and assisted-routing rules unchanged unless separately approved by the relevant owner.
- Keep governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, suppressions, routing, freshness, and handoff semantics unchanged.
- Hold missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state visibly and fail-closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.
- Refuse or fail closed any candidate that does not satisfy the current authorized eligibility and routing conditions.
- Suppress candidates with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- Do not create a production connection, customer-facing activation, or additional production consumer without separate release approval.
- Daniela must confirm the current release and rollback controls before any start; rollback approval and execution remain with Daniela.
- Measure account-level support minutes continuously from first contact, including handoff and after-hours treatment.
- Hold affected records until authoritative correction is completed, validated, and documented.
- Give any unaffected audience its own complete preflight.
- Keep attribution, lifecycle, support, and outcome reporting separate from pipeline and forecast treatment unless Marcus Vail makes a separate explicit decision.

6. Measurement and claim limits

The operating record for this batch must include spend, admitted/assisted/ineligible/held/suppressed counts, paid-source reconciliation through final route, support minutes from first contact, stop/pause events, and owner-certified corrections.

The operating results of this newly approved batch are unavailable for mature claims until its fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows. Do not report its paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, support outcomes, causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast impact, or general paid-growth capacity as mature before those windows are complete and the applicable owners certify the results.

Permitted current claims are limited to the certified historical Q2 2027 evidence, the certified nonproduction preflight, the stated Customer Success coordination design, and the fact of Priya's bounded conditional approval. No randomized control exists for the cited historical cohort. The new batch's results must remain distinct from the certified Q2 2027 historical outcomes.

7. Decision owners and remaining launch gates

- Priya: approval owner for the one new batch, the $8,000 spend ceiling, the 25-workspace admission bound, and the earlier-cap close rule.
- Riley: final operating claims and claim boundaries; customer-action scope; bounded customer corrections; incident-stop decisions; disputed-semantics decisions; and board-readiness judgment.
- Daniela: current attribution endpoints; source and release reliability; instrumentation and engineering-control evidence; separate production release and launch check; current release and rollback controls; rollback approval and execution; and engineering incident-stop execution. Daniela must confirm the staffed owner-and-backup rota before any start.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance authority for eligibility, routing, suppression, holds, freshness, and handoff semantics.
- Customer Success setup desk/on-duty manager: staffed coordination execution within the approved operating design, if the conditional run starts.
- Marcus Vail: any pipeline treatment or forecast credit; none follows automatically from this approval.
- Tomás: any final board-narrative treatment; no narrative expansion follows automatically.
- Owen: routine source-readiness/source-completeness lane only; source readiness is not claim approval, production approval, paid-traffic authorization, or forecast judgment.

Before any start, the record must explicitly contain Priya's approval; Daniela's confirmation of the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and staffed owner-and-backup rota; Riley's approval of final operating claims and customer-action scope; Ines's confirmation of final eligibility, routing, suppression, hold, freshness, and handoff semantics; measurement-owner certification of the attribution, outcome metric, observation window, and reconciliation/reporting plan; and named acquisition/operating owner confirmation of pacing, admission definition, stop/pause authority, escalation, and restart rules. Any separate Marcus Vail decision on pipeline or forecast treatment is absent unless explicitly recorded; therefore there is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. No meeting invitation, evidence certification, staffing readiness, or source-readiness check silently transfers or expands authority.

8. Approved decision and final boundary

Priya approved exactly one new high-intent paid-search batch bounded at no more than $8,000 or 25 admitted workspaces, whichever comes first, with all proposed stop, pause, staffing, attribution, lifecycle, support-clock, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, instrumentation, and assisted-routing conditions intact.

This approval is not immediate launch authority. Paid traffic remains off. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start, and the batch cannot start until Daniela confirms the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and staffed owner-and-backup rota, together with the other required launch gates and current-state checks. No additional paid batch is authorized. There is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. The operating results of this batch remain unavailable for mature claims until its fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows.

NO-AUTHORIZATION BEYOND THE BOUNDED DECISION

This document records Priya's bounded conditional approval of one batch only. It authorizes no live traffic at this time, no immediate launch, no additional paid batch, no production change beyond separately approved release controls, no customer-facing activation, no pipeline target or treatment, and no forecast credit. Any start remains separately gated by the recorded owner confirmations and Daniela's launch check.

arguments.body:
AUGUST 3, 2026 — LIFECYCLE SYSTEMS PRIORITIES REFRESH

Purpose and current operating scope

Keep the established Lifecycle Systems operating model in force while the Helio Start paid-search cohort reaches its mature evidence window. The shared-state contract remains the operating basis across four existing production consumers. Helio Start remains the bounded-GA self-serve product already in operation; this refresh is not a new launch, beta, pricing-page decision, or fifth-consumer proposal.

Current owner lanes

- Owen: routine single-path reporting, reporting semantics and definitions, the routine exception ledger, and explanation of ordinary exceptions.
- Ines: lifecycle governance, governed message-state meanings, and how messaging consumes governed states; readiness remains distinct from blanket authorization to contact.
- Daniela: transport, source reliability and freshness/availability controls, engineering release control, production-path discipline, and rollback readiness/execution.
- Riley: disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident-stop decisions, and executive claims; consequential interpretation stays escalated here.

Helio Start fixed-cohort evidence

The paid-search pilot is a fixed 50-workspace cohort with $14,420 in spend. Attribution is complete, no unsupported admission entered the cohort, 39/50 reached first integration by day 7, and 4/50 exceeded 90 account-level support minutes. These are bounded operating facts and the 39/50 result is the predeclared leading operating read only. They are not mature acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast, or scale evidence.

Timing and review gates

- August 16: the last complete day-90 window closes for the fixed 50-workspace cohort.
- August 17: Owen and Customer Success can assemble the mature source packet and conduct source certification if the final records reconcile. Certification should cover mutually exclusive day-90 statuses, gross billed cash, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort, paid-source reconciliation, unsupported-admission checks, and the certified 39/50 day-7 first-integration result.

Evidence boundaries

Source completeness or source certification is not the same as final-claims approval. A complete, reconciled packet establishes that the required inputs are available for review; it does not by itself establish a mature outcome, close the claim, authorize a second paid batch, or grant pipeline or forecast credit. Final claims require a separate reviewed decision after the complete day-90 outcomes are examined.

Until all 50 workspaces have complete day-90 windows for paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort, no mature Helio Start conclusion is supported. Even after those windows close, the resulting review does not pre-approve another batch. Do not make acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast, or scale claims, and do not treat the August 17 source-certification review as authorization for a second batch or as forecast treatment.

August priority

Maintain the four-consumer operating model and named ownership; finish and certify the fixed-cohort source packet; preserve the separation between source completeness, final claims, and any later growth decision; and keep Helio Start evidence decision-gated until the day-90 review is complete.

Owen Pham — H1 2026 calibration note

H1 calibration summary
Owen has consistently strengthened the reliability and usability of shared operating evidence. He is effective at setting explicit denominators, cutoffs, and coverage boundaries, and at keeping conclusions appropriately bounded when the evidence is not yet mature.

Strengths

• Helio Start paid-search pilot: Independently certified the fixed day-7 result—39 of 50 admitted workspaces reached first integration—while preserving the essential distinction between a leading operating read and mature acquisition/scale evidence. He did not turn the result into an unsupported acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast, or scale claim.

• Expansion Assist: Delivered the denominator and cutoff, together with the pricing-page coverage fields, by May 29. This gave the work a defined measurement boundary rather than leaving key completeness decisions implicit.

• CS auto-nudge: Co-certified the coverage and reliability evidence by June 5, supporting the Mar 1–May 31 review with explicit evidence for the governed decisions and source freshness.

• Renewal prioritization: Responded with bounded aggregate sizing rather than creating an unapproved fifth shared-state consumer or an account-level feed. This showed good judgment about scope, governance, and the risks of expanding a shared-state surface without authorization.

Forward-looking growth focus

Make source completeness and measurement limits legible in the first pass, without requiring line-by-line review. The aim is for initial drafts to state what is covered, what is excluded, which denominators and cutoffs apply, how fresh the sources are, and whether a result is leading or mature evidence. Escalation should remain reserved for disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, or decisions about executive language—not for avoidable ambiguity that can be resolved in the first-pass evidence framing.

Overall calibration

Strong H1 performance in evidence definition, certification, and bounded decision support. The next step is to make that judgment visible earlier and more independently in the initial work product.

messages.content:
Recommendation: keep Helio Start as a bounded organic pricing-page channel for Q4. Do not take Priya a recommendation to authorize even a small paid-acquisition test yet.

What the mature evidence supports:

- Retention/status: Of 68 admitted workspaces with complete day-90 windows, 49 were paid-active. The remaining 19 were canceled, past due, or on billing hold. That is meaningful evidence that the organic motion can produce durable paid accounts, but it is not uniformly successful.
- Cash: The cohort generated $76,940 gross billed and $71,820 in refund-adjusted collected cash. This confirms realized cash, not merely first-paid or booked revenue. It does not establish acquisition economics, contribution margin, payback, or what paid traffic would add.
- Support: The median effort was 21 minutes, but the 90th percentile was 72 minutes, and six accounts exceeded 90 minutes. Every one of those high-effort cases involved external-authority or ownership assistance. The absence of manual-billing, import, migration, and agency cases in the admitted self-serve path is reassuring, but it does not eliminate the support-risk tail for a broader or differently sourced audience.

The combined read is: Helio Start is a credible, bounded organic motion with collected cash and manageable typical support effort, but it has a material assistance tail. Paid acquisition could change the mix of entrants and expose more of that tail; this cohort does not tell us whether that would happen, nor does it provide CAC, incrementality, or payback evidence. A small cap limits exposure, but it does not resolve those missing measurements.

The bounded case to Priya should therefore be an evidence-gated continuation, not a paid test:

- Keep the existing organic pricing-page boundary and eligibility/refusal/routing rules.
- Do not assign pipeline or forecast credit.
- If paid acquisition is revisited, require source-tagged admissions and account-level tracking of day-90 status, refund-adjusted collected cash, support minutes, and external-authority/ownership assistance.
- Define the spend cap, cohort limit, stop conditions, and review date before any future authorization.
- Treat high-effort external-authority cases as a first-class guardrail, rather than averaging them away with the 21-minute median.

In short: the evidence is strong enough to keep operating the organic channel, but not strong enough to justify buying more traffic.
