arguments.title: Source-age alert — August 6 release brief
arguments.hypothesis: A governed source-age alert can surface lateness early enough for owners to investigate and correct freshness issues before the actual freshness limit, while preserving the existing field-specific hold when the limit is crossed and without deciding customer action.
arguments.metric_of_record: Source-age alert readiness: all five governed fields exercised across all four production consumers, with warning behavior in the final 60 minutes before each freshness limit and visible field-specific holds retained at the actual limit.
arguments.cohort_scope: Five governed fields across four production consumers; staging and production evidence tracked separately.

arguments.body:
Status and release boundary
- Scheduled release date: August 6, 2025.
- Explicit status: the August 6 release is scheduled but not live. No production behavior should be represented as released until Daniela confirms the production release has occurred.
- Scope is credential-only/operational alerting as approved; meanings, freshness limits, fail-closed behavior, and the four production consumers remain unchanged.

Objective and guardrails
- Exercise the source-age alert across all five governed fields and all four production consumers.
- In the final 60 minutes before each freshness limit, warn with: consumer, record count, Daniela as engineering owner, and the responsible source owner.
- At the actual freshness-limit crossing, retain the visible field-specific hold. The warning must not decide customer action.
- Any disputed meaning, correction, exception, or incident stop routes to the user; do not infer or change semantics in the release.

Pre-release checks — completion/evidence placeholders
1. [ ] Confirm the release artifact/configuration is the intended August 6 version. Evidence: [STAGING — attach artifact/version/checksum here].
2. [ ] Exercise each of the five governed fields in staging. Evidence: [STAGING — field-by-field test results here].
3. [ ] Exercise each staging representation of the four production consumers. Evidence: [STAGING — consumer-by-consumer results here].
4. [ ] Verify warning timing in the final 60 minutes before each freshness limit. Evidence: [STAGING — timestamps, field, consumer, record count, Daniela, and source owner here].
5. [ ] Verify actual-limit crossing preserves the visible field-specific hold and fail-closed behavior. Evidence: [STAGING — hold screenshots/logs and expected-vs-observed behavior here].
6. [ ] Verify warning content identifies consumer, record count, Daniela, and source owner without prescribing customer action. Evidence: [STAGING — sample alert payloads here].
7. [ ] Confirm all four consumers continue to use the unchanged field meanings and freshness limits. Evidence: [STAGING — contract/consumer check results here].
8. [ ] Confirm production release window, contacts, and stop criteria with Daniela. Evidence: [STAGING — release checklist/sign-off here].

Owner responsibilities
- Daniela: owns engineering release, production monitoring, rollback decision/execution, and certificate rotation if applicable; confirms release/rollback status and controls the release boundary.
- User: owns exceptions, disputed meanings, corrections, and incident stops; decides whether a case requires semantic or customer-action review. The alert does not make customer decisions.
- Source owner: owns source correction and confirms source-side freshness/recovery for each affected field. Name/contact: [PRODUCTION — fill in].
- Consumer owners: validate their consumer behavior and acknowledge alerts/holds. Names/contacts: [PRODUCTION — fill in per consumer].

Rollback verification
- [ ] Define rollback trigger thresholds and stop conditions before release. Evidence: [STAGING — approved thresholds/stop criteria here].
- [ ] Verify rollback restores the prior alert configuration/version. Evidence: [STAGING — rollback test output/version here].
- [ ] Verify rollback preserves the prior visible field-specific hold and fail-closed behavior at the actual freshness limit. Evidence: [STAGING — rollback hold test here].
- [ ] Verify all four consumers after rollback and record any consumer-specific impact. Evidence: [STAGING — post-rollback matrix here].
- [ ] Confirm Daniela can execute and communicate rollback, and identify the restoration checkpoint. Evidence: [STAGING — runbook/drill acknowledgment here].
- Production rollback evidence: [PRODUCTION — leave blank until the scheduled release is live; attach timestamp, version restored, consumers checked, and Daniela’s confirmation here].

Dry-run evidence
STAGING ONLY
- Dry-run date/time: [STAGING — fill in].
- Fields exercised: [STAGING — list all five and pass/fail].
- Consumers exercised: [STAGING — list all four and pass/fail].
- Warning-window observations: [STAGING — timestamps and alert samples].
- Actual-limit/hold observations: [STAGING — field-specific hold evidence].
- Exceptions, disputed meanings, or incident stops encountered: [STAGING — record here].
- Dry-run owner/sign-off: [STAGING — Daniela / reviewers / date].

PRODUCTION ONLY — DO NOT COMPLETE BEFORE RELEASE

- Production fields/consumers exercised: [PRODUCTION — placeholder].
- Production warning evidence: [PRODUCTION — placeholder].
- Production hold evidence at actual limit: [PRODUCTION — placeholder].

Release decision record

messages.content: [2024-03-19T09:18:00-05:00] Owen's first live export has a reporting overlap I need cleaned up before it gets repeated. We have 64 completed eligibility submissions with final states of 34 admitted, 18 assisted, and 12 ineligible, but the dashboard is currently showing 38 eligible starts because four of the assisted cases emitted a provisional eligibility event before their final route-out event. The raw records still have both timestamps, and no unsupported workspace was actually admitted. I need the corrected mutually exclusive reporting structure for the 64 submissions, a way to retain those four provisional events for instrumentation review without inflating the admitted denominator, and the exact caveat Owen should use while the seven-day activation window is still immature. We should not publish an activation rate from this export.

Corrected mutually exclusive reporting for the 64 completed submissions:

  Final state       Count
  Admitted             34
  Assisted             18
  Ineligible           12
  Total                64

The dashboard’s 38 eligible starts is overstated by four. It is counting four provisional eligibility events from submissions whose final state was assisted. The corrected admitted/eligible-start count is 34.

Retention approach:

1. Maintain a submission-level reporting table with exactly one record per submission, keyed by submission ID.
2. Assign the final state as the authoritative disposition:
   - admitted
   - assisted
   - ineligible
3. Keep the raw event stream separately, including both timestamps and event types.
4. Mark the four provisional eligibility events as non-terminal or superseded by final route-out. Retain them for instrumentation review, but exclude them from all final-state and admitted counts.
5. Deduplicate reporting by submission ID, with the final route-out event taking precedence over any earlier provisional eligibility event.

For Owen, use this exact caveat:

“ This export contains 64 completed eligibility submissions: 34 final admitted, 18 final assisted, and 12 final ineligible. Four assisted submissions emitted provisional eligibility events before their final route-out; those events are retained for instrumentation review but are excluded from the admitted and eligible-start counts. No unsupported workspace was admitted. The seven-day activation window is still immature, so activation outcomes are incomplete and no activation rate should be calculated or published from this export.”

results.title: Define live-evidence review boundary
results.snippet: [2025-03-10T13:10:00-05:00] After the >>>first live<<< operating pass, Priya told me that Owen should own the routine three-week exception readout rather than sending every row back for my shadow signoff. I should join when...

messages.content: [2025-03-10T13:10:00-05:00] After the first live operating pass, Priya told me that Owen should own the routine three-week exception readout rather than sending every row back for my shadow signoff. I should join when an exception changes a cross-surface decision, reveals an owner or semantics conflict, or affects executive language. I agree with that direction, but want to preserve my accountability without recreating line-by-line approval. Recommend a concrete review boundary between Owen's routine exception ownership and my high-stakes intervention points for the live-evidence period.

Recommend a “routine by default, escalate by trigger” boundary for the three-week live-evidence period.

Owen owns the routine exception readout when all of the following are true:

- The exception is confined to one surface or feed.
- The owner, definition, unit, and treatment are already established.
- The record can be resolved by applying an existing rule, or held without changing a decision.
- It does not alter authority, entitlement, active-admin status, CS-work status, launch eligibility, or rollback posture.
- It does not require changing executive, board, or other high-stakes language.
- The resolution is reversible and does not create a precedent beyond the existing rule.

For those rows, Owen should classify the exception, apply the established treatment, record the evidence and disposition, and report it in the routine readout. His readout should include counts by disposition, aging, repeated exceptions, unresolved holds, and any exceptions closed without escalation. That makes him accountable for the operating process without requiring your approval of every row.

You should intervene before disposition when any of these triggers occur:

1. Cross-surface decision
   The exception changes a conclusion that depends on two or more surfaces, such as combining lifecycle evidence with entitlement, authority, admin, or CS-work data.

2. Owner or semantics conflict

arguments.body:
Purpose and decision boundary

Assemble the September 19 Q3 evidence lock continuously rather than reconstructing it at the deadline. This is a working evidence template, not an approval of new authority, a new reliability control, a new shared-state consumer, or a change to release, stop, hold, or rollback boundaries.

September 24 decision scope — preserve exactly

The quarter-close decision is limited to whether routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and operator guidance remain in Ines’s independently owned lane without Riley’s line-by-line approval. This template does not imply that that authority has already been approved. The September 24 review decides that question using the September 19 evidence lock.

Existing boundaries remain unchanged

- Riley: exception authority, disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer-correction decisions, incident-stop decisions, and executive claims.
- Owen: routine operating reporting, reconciliation, denominator integrity, and exception explanation within the existing contract; he owns the unique-decision denominator and hold-disposition evidence for this template.
- Ines: lifecycle governance and messaging-state alignment within the existing operating lane; she owns evidence of operator-guidance interventions. No broader independent routine-review or review-closure authority is granted by this template.
- Daniela: engineering release, deployment/configuration, source-reliability evidence, and rollback control; she owns source-reliability and rollback evidence. Credential meanings, freshness requirements, fail-closed behavior, governed-field holds, four-consumer scope, and release/rollback control are unchanged.
- Higher-risk, stop, release, and rollback boundaries remain as previously defined. Escalate exceptions, disputed semantics, cross-consumer conflicts, proposed reliability controls, and any higher-risk or stop condition to Riley and/or Daniela under the existing boundary; do not resolve them in the ledger by inference.

Evidence model and row discipline

Primary decision table: exactly one row per scheduled decision. A primary row is immutable as an identity record and carries:

- decision_id (stable; never reused)
- scheduled_at and decision window
- workspace/customer reference, governed field(s), and intended message/state
- source snapshot/version and source timestamps available at decision time
- decision state: proceeded, suppressed, held, or not-run
- current disposition, disposition owner, and disposition timestamp
- evidence status: complete, partial, or blocked
- links to all related history records

Unique-decision and warning-history measurement rule

Count each scheduled decision exactly once in the unique-decision denominator, using the stable decision_id and scheduled decision window as the exactly-once key. A source-age or reliability alert/warning is linked audit history for that same primary decision; it is not a second decision, a second denominator unit, or an additional hold row merely because the alert occurred.

If the same scheduled decision is alerted, held, fresh-checked, corrected, or reevaluated, retain one primary decision row and append linked warning, hold, fresh_check, correction, or reevaluation history. Do not count one scheduled decision both as an alert and as an additional hold or decision. Do not count a warning as a hold unless a separate, explicitly recorded hold action occurred; if it did, link that hold to the same decision_id rather than adding a denominator row. Preserve distinct event timestamps and states in the linked history so measurement does not erase the operational sequence.

This is a measurement and row-accounting rule only. It does not assume that the source-age alert exists, is live, is firing correctly, is effective, or has changed eligibility, disposition, release authority, or any operating boundary. Record alert deployment, delivery, evaluation, and effectiveness separately and only when supported by evidence. An absent, unverified, or ineffective alert remains an evidence gap; it must not be represented as a functioning control by this counting rule.

Do not create a second primary row when a decision is held, checked again, warned on, corrected, or reevaluated. Add linked history records instead, preserving the original decision_id and timestamp.

Linked history types (append-only)

- hold: governed field, hold reason, trigger time, source owner, last-known update, disposition, and who/when resolved or left open. A hold is a linked event/disposition, not an additional scheduled decision.
- fresh_check: fields checked, source snapshot/version, checked_at, result, and evidence link.
- warning: source-age or reliability warning, threshold/window, detected_at, affected field/consumer, owner, and action; warning is linked audit history, not a release or a final disposition, and not an additional denominator unit.
- reevaluation: prior state, new evidence/check links, reevaluated_at, evaluator, resulting state, and reason; never overwrite prior history.
- intervention: operator-guidance action, trigger/context, guidance shown or changed, population, date, owner, and observed follow-up; do not call an intervention an outcome without evidence.
- correction/escalation: customer correction, semantic dispute, cross-surface conflict, stop condition, or authority escalation, with explicit owner and decision.

Required owner sections

1. Owen — unique-decision denominator and hold dispositions

Maintain the reconciliation ledger and prove completeness:
- scheduled count, unique decision count, duplicate candidates, missing/not-run decisions, and reconciliation method.
- exactly-once key and deduplication evidence; do not silently merge records with different governed fields or decision windows.
- reconcile alert/warning events, holds, and final dispositions back to decision_id; report event counts separately from unique-decision counts.
- apply the explicit guard: one scheduled decision cannot be counted both as an alert and as an additional hold or decision. A warning without a separate hold action remains warning history only; a separate hold action remains linked to the same primary decision.
- hold counts by governed field, reason, age, source owner, and current disposition.
- separate holds from final outcomes; record open, resolved, superseded, and escalated dispositions without double-counting.
- preserve denominator changes as linked reconciliation history with reason, timestamp, and approver/owner.
- evidence-limit prompt: What does this denominator exclude (e.g., not-run decisions, unavailable source snapshots, late-arriving records, or unobserved channels), and what claim must not be made from it?
- evidence-limit prompt: Can every total be traced to one primary decision row and its linked records, with alerts/warnings, holds, and final dispositions reported as distinct event/state measures?

2. Ines — operator-guidance interventions

Maintain the intervention register:
- trigger and intended operator behavior.
- exact guidance/version, surface, audience/population, exposure or delivery evidence, and dates.
- observed operator response, exceptions, reversals, and follow-up evidence; distinguish exposure from adoption and adoption from outcome.
- record whether guidance stayed within the existing lifecycle-governance and messaging-state alignment lane.
- evidence-limit prompt: Does this show guidance was delivered, followed, or effective? Record only the level supported.
- evidence-limit prompt: Are routine review and operator guidance being documented as operating evidence rather than treated as already-approved independent authority?

Independently authored intervention — Ines, August 13, 2025

Record this as an operator-guidance intervention authored independently by Ines, not as an authority approval or a new control:
- Trigger/context: Ines corrected the interpretation of the external-system-authority state for CS operations.
- Guidance/version: external-system authority means readiness for the connector’s required owner-level action; it does not mean blanket permission to contact the person or account.
- Intended operator behavior: apply the applicable messaging rules and the current governed state before outreach; do not infer contact permission from external-system authority alone.
- Owner/author: Ines. This is evidence of authored guidance within the existing lifecycle-governance and messaging-state alignment lane.
- Surface, audience/population, delivery or exposure evidence, observed response, exceptions, reversals, and effectiveness: record only when supported by linked evidence; they are not established by this entry.
- Boundary note: the intervention does not grant broader independent routine-review, review-closure, customer-correction, exception, disputed-semantics, cross-surface, stop, release, or rollback authority. Escalate those matters under the existing Riley and Daniela boundaries.
- Decision status: leave the September 24 decision open. The intervention is evidence for that review, not a disposition of whether Ines’s independently owned lane should continue.

Independently authored intervention — Ines, August 19, 2025

Record this as a second operator-guidance intervention authored independently by Ines, not as an authority approval, a new reliability control, or a new messaging permission:
- Trigger/context: a second internal Customer Success draft stated, “Once external authority is verified, setup reminders are authorized across the account.” Ines caught and corrected the draft before it reached operators.
- Guidance/version: verified external-system authority establishes readiness to perform the selected connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action. It does not create blanket contact permission.
- Intended operator behavior: do not treat external-system authority as authorization for setup reminders across the account. Apply each message’s applicable messaging rules and the current governed state before outreach.
- Owner/author: Ines. The correction is independently authored evidence within her existing lifecycle-governance and messaging-state alignment lane.
- Exposure/delivery and observed response: the draft was corrected before reaching operators; no operator exposure, adoption, outcome, exception, reversal, or effectiveness is established by this record. Record any later evidence separately and only when supported.
- Boundary note: this intervention does not broaden Ines’s review-closure, exception, customer-correction, disputed-semantics, cross-surface, incident-stop, release, or rollback authority. Daniela retains engineering release and rollback control; Riley retains exception authority and ownership of disputed meanings and higher-risk decisions.
- Decision status: leave the September 24 decision open. This second intervention is evidence for the September 19 lock and September 24 review, not a decision that routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews or operator guidance have already been approved to remain in Ines’s independently owned lane.

3. Daniela — source-reliability and rollback evidence

Maintain the reliability and control register:
- source freshness/age checks by governed field and consumer, including threshold, checked_at, source snapshot/version, and result.
- pre-breach warnings, late-source incidents, fail-closed holds, affected decisions, and whether any warning was mistaken for a release signal.
- record whether the source-age alert was actually deployed, live, delivered, evaluated, and effective; do not infer any of those facts from the measurement rule or from a warning-history row.
- release/deployment/configuration record, change owner, approval state, and rollback readiness/test evidence.
- rollback execution or non-execution, trigger, time, resulting state, affected decisions, and verification.
- evidence-limit prompt: Does the record show reliability of the source/control, or merely absence of observed failure in this sample/window?
- evidence-limit prompt: Are warnings, fresh checks, holds, and rollback evidence kept distinct from eligibility, final outcomes, or authority decisions?

4. Riley — bounded interpretation

Maintain the interpretation and claim register:
- claim, supporting primary rows/history links, scope, confidence/qualification, and explicit counterevidence.
- what the evidence supports, does not support, and leaves unresolved.
- cross-surface consequences, disputed meanings, customer corrections, higher-risk conditions, stop decisions, and executive-language review.
- identify denominator/cohort limits, missing evidence, selection effects, and alternative explanations.
- evidence-limit prompt: Is this an observation, an operational control result, a causal claim, an authority decision, or an executive conclusion? Use only the supported category.
- evidence-limit prompt: Is any alert/warning being treated as a separate decision, hold, functioning control, or effective intervention? If yes, correct the accounting and qualify the claim.
- evidence-limit prompt: Does any wording imply Ines’s independent routine-review authority is already approved, or imply that a warning/hold/fresh check changed a boundary? If yes, rewrite and escalate.

Continuous maintenance cadence

At each scheduled decision window:
1. Create or confirm one primary decision row before processing.
2. Attach source snapshots and fresh checks available at decision time.
3. Append alerts/warnings, holds, interventions, dispositions, and reevaluations as linked history, preserving separate event timestamps and states.
4. Reconcile Owen’s denominator and hold ledger; report warning/alert event totals separately and record any correction as history, not silent replacement.
5. Apply the guard against counting one scheduled decision both as an alert and as an additional hold or decision.
6. Review reliability and rollback evidence with Daniela when a threshold, release, stop, or rollback condition is implicated.
7. Add bounded interpretation only after primary rows and linked evidence exist.

arguments.title: Final Helio Start Authority-Diagnostic Closeout
arguments.body:
Final Helio Start Authority-Diagnostic Closeout

Closeout date
December 12, 2024

Scope and completion
The final Helio Start diagnostic window is closed. All 60 enrolled workspaces completed their full 45-day post-admission support windows.

Complete results

• 17 of 60 workspaces contacted support during the window.
• Those workspaces generated 486 post-admission human support minutes.
• 7 contacts were authority cases involving owner-level permission, network allowlisting, or another external-authority dependency.
  • 301 post-admission human minutes.
  • 3.6-business-day median resolution time.
  • 12 substantive repeat contacts.
• 10 contacts were product-guidance cases.
  • 185 post-admission human minutes.
  • 1.4-day median resolution time.
  • 6 substantive repeat contacts.

The categories reconcile to the full observed support population: 7 authority cases plus 10 product-guidance cases equals 17 contacted workspaces, and 301 plus 185 equals 486 human minutes.

Supported interpretation
The diagnostic supports treating external-system authority as a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication.

Every authority case had already passed the Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication checks. The subsequent owner-level permission, network-allowlist, or other external-authority dependency therefore represents a distinct dependency outside those Helio checks—not evidence that the Helio admission checks were ineffective or that the workspace failed Helio authentication.

The result is a bounded readiness interpretation: Helio admission evidence can establish Helio administrator authority and connector authentication, while readiness may still depend on authority held in an external system. Both inputs matter, and they should not be collapsed into one check.

Operating boundaries remain unchanged

• Existing Helio Start admission rules remain unchanged. No new admission gate or revised eligibility threshold is established by this closeout.
• Existing routing rules remain unchanged. Authority cases continue to be handled through the existing external-authority/owner or network-allowlist path; product-guidance cases continue through the existing product-guidance path.
• External-system authority remains a separately classified dependency. It is not reclassified as a Helio admin-proof or connector-authentication failure.
• The diagnostic results do not authorize automatic changes to onboarding, support routing, or operating scope.
• The results must not be generalized into a claim that onboarding or support demand as a whole is broken. The observed population includes seven authority cases and ten product-guidance cases, with distinct causes and resolution patterns.

Closeout conclusion
The 45-day diagnostic is complete for all 60 enrolled workspaces. It establishes a clear, limited finding: external-system authority created a meaningful but separately bounded source of post-admission work even after Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication checks passed. The existing admission and routing rules, classifications, and operating boundaries remain in force.

arguments.title: Helio Start internal triage FAQ
arguments.body:
Helio Start internal triage FAQ

Purpose
Apply the established eligibility, pending-state, assistance, and refusal rules consistently. Do not infer permission, eligibility, or authority from a nearby signal.

What are the three checks?

1. Helio admin proof
This is the required evidence that the person meets the Helio admin-proof requirement for the relevant eligibility decision. It is an eligibility input, not a substitute for connector authentication or verified authority in an external system.

2. Connector authentication
This is the authentication/setup state for connecting to the relevant external system. Successful authentication means the connector can authenticate; it does not by itself establish Helio eligibility, admin proof, or authority to act in that external system.

3. External-system authority
This is the verified authority state in the external system needed for connector readiness. It is connector-readiness state only—not permission for automated contact, other outreach, or any action outside the established product flow.

What is the ordinary product-guidance path?
Use the docs-first path for ordinary, supported product guidance: point to the applicable documentation and provide guidance within the documented self-serve flow. Do not use assistance to bypass an unmet eligibility requirement, pending state, refusal, or an unresolved authority question.

How do we handle assistance?

• Pending assistance before admission: Keep the account pending when a required field is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting. Preserve the reason at the field level. Provide only the permitted docs-first/product guidance; do not treat assistance or a Proceed signal as admission or as blanket permission to contact the account.

• Supported admission: Admit only when the established eligibility requirements are satisfied and the required state is verified and current. Then provide supported product guidance within the documented path. Connector readiness still does not authorize automated contact or other outreach.

• Routing outside self-serve: If the request is not ordinary supported guidance, cannot be resolved through the docs-first path, or requires authority or handling not available in self-serve, route it through the established non-self-serve path. Do not improvise a workaround or override a refusal.

Fail-closed rules
Missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state remains fail-closed. Keep the corresponding field pending, retain its specific pending reason, and do not manually release it based on adjacent evidence. A verified external authority signal does not change this rule and does not grant outreach permission.

Refusal boundary
Refuse requests that would bypass eligibility, pending-state, assistance, or refusal rules; expose or act on authority that has not been verified; or initiate automated contact or other outreach merely because connector readiness is present.

arguments.title: Working annual self-review — 2024
arguments.body:
Working annual self-review — 2024

This is a working draft for Priya, not a polished promotion case.

What I completed

• I closed the 60-workspace Helio Start diagnostic with a specific readiness finding: external-system authority is a separate readiness input from Helio admin proof and connector authentication. I kept the conclusion narrow rather than turning the result into a broad onboarding claim.

• I delegated routine lifecycle releases while retaining authority over incident stops, customer corrections, state-changing sends, ambiguous cases, and higher-risk sends. Ines owns routine, non-state-changing sends within her authority and routine preflights. Daniela retains engineering release controls, and Ines does not have engineering release-control access. This clarified operational ownership without weakening the safety boundary.

• I handled the stale-retry-manifest correction without overstating its cause. I focused on correcting the operational issue and kept the explanation within what the evidence supported.

• I repeatedly corrected metric definitions before unsupported claims reached leadership. This included checking what each measure actually counted and separating supported conclusions from interpretations that the underlying data could not establish.

Improvement area

I need to reduce late-stage manual interpretation by specifying ownership and evidence boundaries earlier. In practice, that means defining who can decide, what evidence is required, and what remains out of scope before work reaches final review or release. This should make corrections less dependent on my intervention late in the process.

Overall reflection

My strongest contribution this year was making operational decisions more precise: narrowing claims to the evidence, separating readiness inputs, and delegating routine work while preserving explicit controls for higher-risk actions. The next step is to make those boundaries legible earlier so the system and team carry more of that precision without late-stage manual interpretation.

Can you draft feedback in three buckets: safe to adapt now, depends on eligibility or support policy, and do not touch until the boundaries are decided?

Ines — this is useful, especially the parts where we can reuse existing product-event email patterns. To keep the map moving without rewriting copy that may be excluded later, let’s triage the branches this way:

1. Safe to adapt now

Please continue adapting existing product-event emails when the message:

- Is triggered by a reliable product event we already use.
- Gives standard product guidance or a self-serve next step.
- Does not assume a particular account type, team structure, CSM assignment, or support entitlement.
- Does not imply a Helio Start launch date or broader availability.
- Can use the existing CTA pattern, such as connecting an integration, completing setup, or returning to the product.

For these, preserve the existing trigger and eligibility behavior where possible. We can refine wording later without reopening the operating model.

2. Depends on eligibility or support policy

Please leave the copy structure in place, but mark these branches as policy-dependent rather than rewriting them:

- Import stalled or failed.
- Billing mismatch or payment-related issues.
- Accounts that may or may not qualify for Helio Start.
- Whether a user has an assigned CSM, implementation lead, or other named contact.
- Whether single-team accounts should receive team-invite or multi-team messaging.
- Webinar, live onboarding, or other assisted-help CTAs.
- Any path where the action differs for sub-50-seat accounts versus other segments.

For each one, annotate the open decision we need: eligible population, support owner, allowed channel, response expectation, and fallback if the user is not eligible. The measurement table should state the eligibility and deployment shape explicitly, including the sub-50-seat threshold.

3. Do not touch until the boundaries are decided

- “Offer live CS help.”
- “Reply to your CSM.”
- Promises of implementation or one-to-one onboarding.
- Any implied response-time or guaranteed human follow-up.
- Routing users to a named support role they may not have.
- Billing escalation language that assumes ownership or resolution authority.
- Any branch that requires a new support workflow, staffing commitment, or exception process.

arguments.body:
Helio Start November 1 final-launch checklist

STATUS AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARY

Status: OPEN — every verification item remains open.

Priya approved one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch on October 16, 2027. This is a bounded conditional approval, not immediate launch authority. Paid traffic remains off. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start; it is not a launch date. No traffic begins before Daniela signs off and the other required owner confirmations and current-state checks are recorded.

This checklist does not authorize a production change, customer-facing activation, pipeline target, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, automatic extension, replenishment, or any additional paid batch.

1. BOUNDED RUN AND CLOSE RULE — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Priya / acquisition-operating owner: verify the approved scope is exactly one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch.]

[OPEN — Finance/acquisition owner: verify the $8,000 amount is the maximum paid-search spend ceiling, inclusive of applicable media costs and directly attributable fees, and is not treated as committed spend before launch authorization and actual spend initiation under standard accounting treatment.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: verify the admission bound is no more than 25 admitted workspaces.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: verify the batch closes at the earlier of the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces, with no automatic extension, replenishment, or exception that expands the approval.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: verify the admission definition: an admitted workspace must pass the current, fresh eligibility and routing evaluation and enter the admitted path. Assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed routes must not be silently counted as admissions.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: record pacing, admission definition, exception handling, stop/pause authority, escalation path, and restart rule before any start.]

2. PAID-SOURCE RECONCILIATION — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Daniela: confirm the current attribution endpoints and their production ownership before any start.]

[OPEN — Measurement/engineering owner: verify continuous paid-source reconciliation for every paid-source eligibility-flow start from the beginning of the eligibility flow through the final terminal route, including:
- final admitted route;
- final assisted route; and
- final ineligible route.]

[OPEN — Measurement owner: verify that held and suppressed outcomes are visible and not converted into untracked or silently admitted endpoints.]

[OPEN — Measurement/engineering owner: verify the operating record captures paid-source reconciliation status, route, source, timestamps, discrepancies, delayed or missing events, and owner-certified corrections.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: verify that prior shadow, preflight, or historical results are not reused as a substitute for current authoritative evaluation.]

3. PRODUCTION ENABLE AND ROLLBACK — DANIELA — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Daniela: confirm current production release controls and the exact production enable path.]

[OPEN — Daniela: confirm current rollback controls, rollback trigger, rollback owner, rollback execution path, and evidence that the path is usable before any start.]

[OPEN — Daniela: complete the separate production release and launch check.]

[OPEN — Daniela: confirm instrumentation and engineering-control evidence, including the ability to stop paid traffic and keep it off while an incident, discrepancy, correction, validation, or restart decision is pending.]

[OPEN — Daniela: sign off explicitly before any traffic begins. No traffic begins before this sign-off.]

4. CUSTOMER SUCCESS OWNER-AND-BACKUP ROTA — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Customer Success: name the primary owner for Monday through Friday coverage, 8:00am–6:00pm Central.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: name the backup for every covered period; the backup is the on-duty Customer Success manager unless a named current-state rota says otherwise.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify continuous Monday–Friday coverage from 8:00am–6:00pm Central for the approved operating bound.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify that after-hours cases queue to the named backup at the next service opening. After-hours handling must not create an unowned route or reset the support clock.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify handoff begins when an admitted workspace needs owner action after admission, and that handoff context includes connector, authority state, required action, route, first-contact time, and notes.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify the initial response target is within two business hours and that the Customer Success lead escalates if no owner accepts within that response window.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify account-level support minutes run continuously from first contact, including handoff and after-hours treatment; neither handoff nor after-hours handling resets the clock.]

5. HARD STOPS — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Riley/Daniela: verify and implement the immediate hard stop if an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path. Keep paid traffic off pending incident review, correction, validation, and an explicit restart decision.]

[OPEN — Acquisition-operating owner: verify the hard close at the earlier of $8,000 paid-search spend or 25 admitted workspaces. Do not admit another workspace after the applicable cap is reached.]

[OPEN — Daniela: verify the technical stop path can disable the paid source and prevent further entry while the hard-stop condition is investigated.]

6. PAUSE CONDITIONS — OPEN VERIFICATION

The following conditions remain controlling. Each is an open verification item, and each keeps paid traffic off until the responsible owner documents the issue, correction, validation, and explicit restart decision:

[OPEN — Measurement/engineering owner: pause if paid-source reconciliation cannot be completed continuously from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.]

[OPEN — Customer Success/measurement owner: after at least 10 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes.]

[OPEN — Daniela/measurement owner: pause for any material attribution discrepancy.]

[OPEN — Ines/lifecycle owner: pause for any lifecycle or suppression bypass.]

[OPEN — Ines/lifecycle owner: pause for any unresolved governed-state conflict.]

[OPEN — Measurement/engineering owner: pause for missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state. The affected state must remain visible and fail closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.]

[OPEN — Ines/acquisition-operating owner: pause for a routing disagreement.]

[OPEN — Daniela/Customer Success: pause for any failure of the staffed handoff or continuous support-clock design.]

[OPEN — Daniela/measurement owner: pause for any routing or instrumentation failure that blocks paid-source reconciliation.]

[OPEN — Responsible owner: verify that a template-only override is not a correction. Restart requires documented correction, validation, fresh evaluation, and explicit owner confirmation; prior preflight or shadow outcomes cannot substitute for current decisions.]

7. UNCHANGED OPERATING RULES — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Ines: confirm existing eligibility rules remain unchanged.]

[OPEN — Ines: confirm existing refusal rules remain unchanged; candidates that do not satisfy the current authorized eligibility and routing conditions must be refused or fail closed.]

[OPEN — Ines/connector owner: confirm existing connector-access rules remain unchanged.]

[OPEN — Ines/external-authority owner: confirm existing external-authority rules remain unchanged, including the need for the appropriate owner-level permission or network action where required.]

[OPEN — Ines: confirm existing lifecycle rules remain unchanged, including governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, suppressions, routing, freshness, and handoff semantics.]

[OPEN — Daniela/measurement owner: confirm existing instrumentation rules remain unchanged and that assisted-setup and unsupported-routing outcomes remain visible in instrumentation.]

[OPEN — Ines/Customer Success: confirm existing assisted-routing rules remain unchanged. Applicants who need assistance or fall outside the criteria must continue to receive the appropriate assisted or ineligible outcome; a batch pause does not change eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, or routing rules.]

[OPEN — Lifecycle owner: confirm missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state remains visibly held and fail-closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.]

[OPEN — Customer Success/lifecycle owner: confirm candidates with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work remain suppressed from the candidate path.]

[OPEN — Daniela: confirm no production connection, customer-facing activation, or additional production consumer is created without separate release approval.]

[OPEN — Responsible owner: confirm affected records remain held until authoritative correction is completed, validated, and documented, and any unaffected audience receives its own complete preflight.]

8. MEASUREMENT AND SUPPORT RECORD — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Measurement owner: define and certify the final attribution, outcome metric, observation window, and reconciliation/reporting plan before any start.]

[OPEN — Operating owner: verify the run record includes spend; admitted, assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed counts; paid-source reconciliation through the final route; support minutes from first contact; stop/pause events; and owner-certified corrections.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: verify support minutes are account-level and continuous from first contact, including pre-admission contact where applicable, admission, handoff, and after-hours handling, without resetting the clock.]

[OPEN — Measurement owner: verify attribution, lifecycle, support, and outcome reporting remain separate from pipeline and forecast treatment.]

9. COMMERCIAL AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Marcus Vail: verify there is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. None follows automatically from Priya's approval, spend, admissions, assisted routes, support evidence, or operating results.]

[OPEN — Priya/acquisition owner: verify no additional Helio Start paid-search batch is authorized beyond this one bounded batch.]

[OPEN — Riley/Tomás: verify no board or narrative expansion follows automatically from this approval or from the historical Q2 evidence.]

[OPEN — All owners: verify no meeting invitation, evidence certification, source-readiness check, staffing readiness, or operational attendance silently transfers or expands authority.]

10. DAY-90 MATURE-CLAIM LIMIT — OPEN VERIFICATION

[OPEN — Measurement and outcome owners: verify that operating results from this newly approved batch remain unavailable for mature claims until its fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows.]

[OPEN — Outcome owners: verify that paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support outcomes, causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast impact, and general paid-growth capacity are not reported as mature before the complete day-90 windows and applicable owner certifications.]

[OPEN — Reporting owner: keep the new batch's results distinct from certified historical Q2 2027 descriptive evidence and from nonproduction preflight evidence.]

11. FINAL PRE-START GATE — ALL OPEN

No traffic begins before every item in this checklist is explicitly verified and the record contains:

[OPEN — Priya: approval of exactly one batch, the $8,000 ceiling, the 25-admission bound, and the earlier-cap close rule.]

[OPEN — Daniela: confirmation of current attribution endpoints, production enable controls, rollback controls, instrumentation/control evidence, staffed owner-and-backup rota, and separate launch sign-off.]

[OPEN — Riley: approval of final operating claims and customer-action scope.]

[OPEN — Ines: confirmation of eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, suppression, hold, freshness, routing, and handoff semantics.]

[OPEN — Customer Success: named Monday–Friday 8:00am–6:00pm Central owner-and-backup rota, next-service-opening after-hours handling, response/escalation path, and continuous first-contact support-minute treatment.]

[OPEN — Measurement owners: certification of attribution, outcome metric, observation window, support-minute treatment, and reconciliation/reporting plan.]

[OPEN — Acquisition/operating owner: confirmation of pacing, admission definition, cap watch, stop/pause authority, escalation, and restart rules.]

[OPEN — Marcus Vail: any separate pipeline or forecast decision; absent an explicit decision, there is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.]

November 1, 2027 remains only the earliest conditional start. Until these items are closed and Daniela signs off, paid traffic remains off.

FINAL NO-AUTHORIZATION STATEMENT

This document records the final-launch checklist for Priya's bounded conditional approval. It does not authorize immediate launch, traffic before November 1, traffic before Daniela's sign-off, any production change outside separately approved controls, customer-facing activation, a pipeline target, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, an automatic extension, or an additional paid batch.

arguments.body:
Helio Start bounded paid-search proposal — October 2027 working draft

APPROVED BOUNDED DECISION — AUTHORITY AND LAUNCH BOUNDARY

Priya approved one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch after reviewing this completed proposal and its certified Q2 2027 mature evidence. The approval is strictly bounded and conditional. It authorizes one batch only within the limits and gates below; it does not mean that paid traffic is live or authorize immediate launch.

Paid traffic remains off. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start date. Before any start, Daniela must confirm the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and the staffed owner-and-backup rota. All other required owner decisions, current-state checks, and launch controls remain in force.

1. Certified Q2 2027 evidence and claim boundary

Certified Q2 2027 mature descriptive evidence covers a fixed cohort of 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 2027, with complete day-90 windows:

- Customer Success certified 18 of 25 paid-active; 3 canceled; 2 past due; and 2 on billing hold.
- Owen certified $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Customer Success certified account-level support effort of 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; 5 of 25 workspaces exceeded 90 minutes.
- Daniela certified paid-source attribution for all 61 paid-source starts, with no unsupported applicant entering the admitted path, and certified the source as reliable.
- Ines certified that no lifecycle hold or suppression was bypassed.

This evidence is descriptive evidence from the fixed Q2 2027 cohort. It supports reporting the observed historical cohort outcomes and an operational support signal. It does not establish causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue or forecast impact beyond the stated collected-cash record, or that an owner checklist causes improved support. The cohort had no randomized comparison.

The prior bounded execution record is distinct: its approved test budget cap was $8,000, certified final paid-search spend was $7,640, the vendor invoice was paid in full with zero balance and $0 taxes/fees, service ran April 12–May 17, 2027, and the fixed test cohort closed at 25 admitted workspaces across 61 starts (25 admitted, 18 assisted, 18 ineligible). Traffic is off and no later batch was authorized before this decision. The prior spend, cap, staffing reference, and this approval do not create authority beyond the single batch and boundaries recorded here.

2. Certified nonproduction preflight and staffed design

Daniela and Ines certified a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight consisting of 8 expected admissions, 8 expected assisted routes, and 8 expected fail-closed, held, or suppressed outcomes. Certification covered paid-source final-route attribution; governed-state meanings; lifecycle branches, holds, and suppression; setup-step exposure; coordination ownership and backup behavior; handoff; after-hours handling; and continuous account-level support-minute treatment. All expected routes, attribution, holds/suppressions, ownership, support clock, handoff, and support-minute behavior matched design.

This is nonproduction evidence. It does not authorize traffic, a production connection, customer-facing activation, pipeline treatment, forecast credit, an eligibility/routing/ownership change, or a later launch. Any run requires a fresh evaluation; prior preflight outcomes must not be reused as a substitute for current admission decisions.

Customer Success coordination assumptions for the fixed cohort:

- Primary owner: Customer Success setup desk.
- Backup: on-duty Customer Success manager.
- Coverage: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central.
- After-hours cases queue to the named backup at the next service opening.
- Handoff begins when an admitted workspace needs owner action after admission.
- Handoff context includes connector, authority state, required action, route, first-contact time, and notes.
- Initial response target: within two business hours.
- Customer Success lead escalates if no owner accepts within the response window.
- Account-level support minutes continue from first contact; handoff and after-hours treatment do not reset the clock.

These assumptions describe coordination readiness only. Daniela's pre-start confirmation of the current staffed owner-and-backup rota is still required. The assumptions are not evidence of paid-growth capacity beyond the approved operating bound, causal lift, revenue, pipeline, or forecast impact.

3. Approved budget, admission bound, and run-close rule

- Approval owner: Priya.
- Approved scope: one new high-intent Helio Start paid-search batch only.
- Spend ceiling: no more than $8,000 in paid-search spend, inclusive of applicable media costs and any directly attributable fees.
- Admission bound: no more than 25 admitted workspaces.
- Run-close rule: close the batch at the earlier of the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces.
- November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start; it is not a launch date or traffic authorization.
- No automatic extension, replenishment, or second/additional paid batch is authorized.
- Spend pacing, admission definition, and exception handling must be recorded by the acquisition/operating owner before launch. An admitted workspace is one that passes the current, fresh eligibility and routing evaluation and enters the admitted path; assisted, ineligible, held, and suppressed routes are not silently counted as admissions.

4. Stop, pause, staffing, and support-clock conditions

Hard stop:

- If an unsupported applicant enters the admitted path, stop the batch immediately and keep paid traffic off pending incident review, correction, and an explicit restart decision.
- Close the batch when either the $8,000 spend ceiling or 25 admitted workspaces is reached, whichever occurs first.

Pause:

- Pause if paid-source reconciliation cannot be completed from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- After at least 10 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceed 90 account-level support minutes.
- Pause for any material attribution discrepancy, lifecycle or suppression bypass, unresolved governed-state conflict, missing/stale required state, routing disagreement, or failure of the staffed handoff/support-clock design.

A pause keeps paid traffic off until the responsible owner documents the issue, correction, validation, and restart decision. A template-only override is not a correction. Restart requires fresh evaluation and explicit owner confirmation; prior preflight or shadow outcomes cannot substitute for current decisions.

The staffed operating design remains intact: Customer Success setup desk primary owner; on-duty Customer Success manager backup; Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Central coverage; next-opening queue for after-hours cases; two-business-hour initial response target; escalation if no owner accepts; and continuous account-level support minutes from first contact without a clock reset at handoff or after hours. Daniela must confirm the staffed owner-and-backup rota before any start.

5. Attribution, lifecycle, eligibility, and operational safeguards

Any run under this approval must preserve all of the following:

- Reconcile paid source from eligibility-flow start through the final admitted, assisted, or ineligible route.
- Daniela must confirm the current attribution endpoints before any start.
- Evaluate every candidate from current authoritative state; do not reuse prior shadow or preflight outcomes.
- Keep eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, suppression, freshness, handoff, and assisted-routing rules unchanged unless separately approved by the relevant owner.
- Keep governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, suppressions, routing, freshness, and handoff semantics unchanged.
- Hold missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state visibly and fail-closed pending fresh authoritative evaluation.
- Refuse or fail closed any candidate that does not satisfy the current authorized eligibility and routing conditions.
- Suppress candidates with active Customer Success adoption or renewal work.
- Do not create a production connection, customer-facing activation, or additional production consumer without separate release approval.
- Daniela must confirm the current release and rollback controls before any start; rollback approval and execution remain with Daniela.
- Measure account-level support minutes continuously from first contact, including handoff and after-hours treatment.
- Hold affected records until authoritative correction is completed, validated, and documented.
- Give any unaffected audience its own complete preflight.
- Keep attribution, lifecycle, support, and outcome reporting separate from pipeline and forecast treatment unless Marcus Vail makes a separate explicit decision.

6. Measurement and claim limits

The operating record for this batch must include spend, admitted/assisted/ineligible/held/suppressed counts, paid-source reconciliation through final route, support minutes from first contact, stop/pause events, and owner-certified corrections.

The operating results of this newly approved batch are unavailable for mature claims until its fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows. Do not report its paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, support outcomes, causal lift, scalable acquisition, revenue, pipeline, forecast impact, or general paid-growth capacity as mature before those windows are complete and the applicable owners certify the results.

Permitted current claims are limited to the certified historical Q2 2027 evidence, the certified nonproduction preflight, the stated Customer Success coordination design, and the fact of Priya's bounded conditional approval. No randomized control exists for the cited historical cohort. The new batch's results must remain distinct from the certified Q2 2027 historical outcomes.

7. Decision owners and remaining launch gates

- Priya: approval owner for the one new batch, the $8,000 spend ceiling, the 25-workspace admission bound, and the earlier-cap close rule.
- Riley: final operating claims and claim boundaries; customer-action scope; bounded customer corrections; incident-stop decisions; disputed-semantics decisions; and board-readiness judgment.
- Daniela: current attribution endpoints; source and release reliability; instrumentation and engineering-control evidence; separate production release and launch check; current release and rollback controls; rollback approval and execution; and engineering incident-stop execution. Daniela must confirm the staffed owner-and-backup rota before any start.
- Ines: lifecycle-governance authority for eligibility, routing, suppression, holds, freshness, and handoff semantics.
- Customer Success setup desk/on-duty manager: staffed coordination execution within the approved operating design, if the conditional run starts.
- Marcus Vail: any pipeline treatment or forecast credit; none follows automatically from this approval.
- Tomás: any final board-narrative treatment; no narrative expansion follows automatically.
- Owen: routine source-readiness/source-completeness lane only; source readiness is not claim approval, production approval, paid-traffic authorization, or forecast judgment.

Before any start, the record must explicitly contain Priya's approval; Daniela's confirmation of the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and staffed owner-and-backup rota; Riley's approval of final operating claims and customer-action scope; Ines's confirmation of final eligibility, routing, suppression, hold, freshness, and handoff semantics; measurement-owner certification of the attribution, outcome metric, observation window, and reconciliation/reporting plan; and named acquisition/operating owner confirmation of pacing, admission definition, stop/pause authority, escalation, and restart rules. Any separate Marcus Vail decision on pipeline or forecast treatment is absent unless explicitly recorded; therefore there is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. No meeting invitation, evidence certification, staffing readiness, or source-readiness check silently transfers or expands authority.

8. Approved decision and final boundary

Priya approved exactly one new high-intent paid-search batch bounded at no more than $8,000 or 25 admitted workspaces, whichever comes first, with all proposed stop, pause, staffing, attribution, lifecycle, support-clock, eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, instrumentation, and assisted-routing conditions intact.

This approval is not immediate launch authority. Paid traffic remains off. November 1, 2027 is only the earliest conditional start, and the batch cannot start until Daniela confirms the current attribution endpoints, release and rollback controls, and staffed owner-and-backup rota, together with the other required launch gates and current-state checks. No additional paid batch is authorized. There is no pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. The operating results of this batch remain unavailable for mature claims until its fixed cohort has complete day-90 windows.

NO-AUTHORIZATION BEYOND THE BOUNDED DECISION

This document records Priya's bounded conditional approval of one batch only. It authorizes no live traffic at this time, no immediate launch, no additional paid batch, no production change beyond separately approved release controls, no customer-facing activation, no pipeline target or treatment, and no forecast credit. Any start remains separately gated by the recorded owner confirmations and Daniela's launch check.

input.body:
Helio Start pending external-authority quick reference

FIELD USE

State: external_authority = pending
Meaning: the required owner-level permission, network-allowlist action, or other authority in the relevant external system has not yet been verified. Keep the case pending and fail closed until current, verifiable evidence is available and rechecked.

DO NOT CONFLATE IT WITH

- Helio admin proof: separate eligibility evidence about the Helio administrator. External authority is tracked separately.
- Connector authentication: authentication can succeed while the external system still lacks the required owner-level permission or network action.
- Generic onboarding friction or bad instrumentation: label unclear ownership, permissions, or administrator role specifically; do not erase the authority dependency in a broad friction bucket.
- Admitted, ready, or operational: pending authority does not establish admission or finished setup. Do not call the workspace fully ready or operational.
- Declined/refused: pending is unresolved state, not a refusal. Preserve the field-specific pending reason.
- Contact permission: verified external authority is connector-readiness state only. It is not blanket permission for automated contact, setup reminders, or other outreach.

FAST PATH

1. Confirm the current authoritative evaluation and the exact pending field/reason.
2. Record external_authority = pending; retain the evidence gap, owner/action needed, source, and as-of time.
3. Keep any dependent admission or setup state held. Do not manually release it from adjacent evidence such as admin proof or authenticated connector state.
4. Use only the governed pending-state message, if the applicable fresh evaluation allows a display.
5. Re-evaluate after verifiable owner-level evidence is supplied. Do not reuse a prior preflight, shadow result, or stale state.

ROLE CARD: LIFECYCLE / OPERATING OWNER — RECORDING

Owns the governed state and its semantics.

- Record the field-specific state as external_authority = pending, with the specific reason and required owner-level action.
- Keep the record visibly held and fail closed while required authority is missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting.
- Preserve the distinction from Helio admin proof, connector authentication, eligibility, and refusal.
- Do not mark the workspace admitted, release setup, or substitute a template-only override for authoritative correction.
- After evidence arrives, perform a fresh evaluation and record the new authoritative result.

ROLE CARD: SETUP / CUSTOMER-SUCCESS MESSAGE OWNER — DEPENDENT SETUP MESSAGING

Owns the dependent setup message, not the authority decision.

- Treat pending authority as a remaining setup dependency; do not write or send copy that says setup is fully ready or operational.
- Keep dependent setup prompts held when the governed record is held. A held record is not a queued delivery.
- For every possible display, run the applicable fresh evaluation; send only if that evaluation allows it.
- If messaging is allowed, state the remaining authorization step plainly and avoid implying admission, completion, or a guaranteed human follow-up.
- Do not infer outreach permission from external-authority status. Each message still depends on its applicable messaging rules and current governed state.
- Once authority is verified, do not assume all messaging is automatically released; recheck every other required state and the message-specific rules.

ROLE CARD: MEASUREMENT / REPORTING OWNER — REPORTING

Owns definitions, reconciliation, and readout boundaries.

- Report pending authority as its own field-specific state and route; keep pending, held, assisted, ineligible, and admitted outcomes separate.
- Identify the dependency as external owner permission, network allowlisting, or administrator-role/permissions review—not generic onboarding friction and not automatically an instrumentation defect.
- Do not count a pending or held record as an admission, completed setup, or operational workspace.
- Keep the authority response separate from Helio admin-proof and connector-authentication measures.
- Preserve source, timestamps, pending reason, evidence status, and owner-certified corrections in the operating record.
- Do not turn a pending count into a broad claim that onboarding or support demand as a whole is broken; report the bounded category and its route.

OPERATOR CHECK

If external authority is pending, the correct posture is: record the field-specific hold; keep dependent setup messaging governed and non-ready; report the category separately; and wait for fresh, verifiable owner-level evidence before changing state.

BOUNDARY TO REMEMBER

External-system authority establishes readiness for the selected connector’s required external owner action. It does not replace Helio admin proof or connector authentication, does not itself admit the workspace, and does not authorize automated contact or other outreach.

Date: 2028-01-01

Expansion Assist — first-pilot cohort integrity note

Operational exposure maximum
The exact approved operational exposure maximum was 30 accounts. This is an operational cap: once 30 accounts had been exposed, exposure was closed and no further prompts or exposures could be added.

Locked primary reporting denominator
The locked primary reporting denominator was 30 randomized primary accounts, analyzed as the primary intention-to-treat cohort with their original assignments. This denominator is distinct from operational exposure counts and must remain fixed; post-randomization ineligibility, non-exposure, suppression, failure, or later protocol status does not silently remove an account from the locked primary cohort.

Prompts during outcome maturation
After the operational maximum was reached, the exposure phase remained closed while each account’s approved 45-day outcome window matured. No further prompts were sent and no additional exposures were scheduled during this maturation period. The experiment could remain open solely for observation. Analysts must classify events by their source timestamp relative to exposure: an in-window help or options request is eligible when its source event occurs from 0 through 45 × 24 elapsed hours after exposure, inclusive; events before exposure or more than 45 × 24 elapsed hours after exposure are outside the approved 45-day outcome window. Closing exposure does not invalidate a valid response received through the existing help path. Post-window commercial outcomes may be retained as later observed context, but must not be counted as approved 45-day outcomes or treated as caused by the prompt.

Reserve-exposure handling
Reserve accounts are a separate operational cohort and must never be merged into, substituted for, or used to rewrite the locked primary denominator. A reserve may fill a vacant operational slot only when that slot remains vacant under the prespecified rule. Selection must follow the next position in the separately randomized, prespecified reserve order; the order must not be silently bypassed or rewritten. Before use, the selected reserve must pass a fresh retained-mid-segment eligibility check and all normal operational exclusions. Reserve accounts must not be exposed to Customer Success as reserves; activation is made centrally under the existing reserve rule.

If a reserve is actually run after a primary failure or vacancy, record it as a distinct reserve operational exposure, with its reserve status, eligibility decision, exposure disposition, timestamps, and protocol-deviation status preserved. Report reserve exposures separately from the primary exposure population and keep them out of the locked primary intention-to-treat denominator. Do not backfill a primary account, relabel a reserve as primary, or treat a reserve exposure as evidence that changes the fixed 30-account primary cohort.

Reuse rule for mature-window reporting
For any mature-window report, place the fixed 30-account primary denominator before the outcome summary. Restrict approved outcome rates to accounts with complete 45-day windows, state the observation window and denominator for every rate, and show reserve exposures in a separate labeled section. Preserve account-level membership flags for primary ITT, reserve cohort, post-randomization ineligibility, exposure disposition, and protocol deviation so analysts can reproduce the same mature-window population without changing cohort membership.

One-page outline

Eligibility versus product constraints
Purpose: Establish the bounded population for the June operating-model assessment; this is not a Q3 launch commitment.

1. Definitions

Eligibility
Who is allowed into the assessment or evaluation population.

Product constraint
A product, operational, support, or instrumentation condition required to serve that eligible population safely and repeatably.

Key principle:
Engineering should size the constraints and dependencies against an explicit candidate population. Engineering should not define eligibility implicitly through implementation difficulty.

Proposed starting point:
- Sub-50-seat self-serve accounts under evaluation.
- Narrow to the smallest population the team is willing to assess now.
- Exclude accounts that require bespoke implementation, undefined migration work, or unsupported operating-model exceptions.
- Treat the June gate as a decision on whether discovery should continue, not as approval to launch.

- Seat band and account type
- Self-serve versus sales-assisted motion

- Whether imports are in scope

- Eligibility question: Which account profiles are in scope?
- Product-constraint question: Can the product support them without bespoke implementation?
- Gap/risk: Account-profile boundaries may be inferred from implementation complexity.
- Decision needed: Approve the bounded candidate population.

- Eligibility question: What level of customer-side ownership is required?

- Decision needed: Define supported admin assumptions and exclusions.

messages.content: [2024-02-14T10:15:00-06:00] Customer Success got the clarifications I asked for, and the five sub-50 cancellations still do not collapse into one mechanism. Account A had no alternate admin and never asked its IT provider to approve the integration. Account C needed about 70,000 contacts plus legacy tags mapped and imported, so that should have been assisted onboarding from the start. At Account E, the original champion's email was disabled before workspace ownership or the setup invitation moved to the successor. The other two are still a seasonal pause and a project that ended. I want a direct judgment on whether five clarified cases like this justify an experiment or whether they should stay descriptive operating evidence, plus concise language I can use in the churn readout that is denominator-aware and doesn't overclaim.

Direct judgment: keep these as descriptive operating evidence, not an experiment.

Five cases are too few for a segment-wide or causal claim, and they do not identify one coherent mechanism:

- Account A: missing alternate-admin and IT-approval path
- Account C: implementation complexity that warranted assisted onboarding
- Account E: ownership/champion handoff failure
- Two accounts: seasonal pause and completed project

The cases support targeted process improvements and better classification—not testing that one intervention reduces churn. Account C may justify reviewing assisted-onboarding eligibility, but this set alone does not establish that assisted onboarding would have prevented cancellation.

Suggested churn-readout language:

“Among the five clarified cancellations below 50 seats, we found five distinct circumstances rather than a common churn mechanism: administrative/IT dependency, an onboarding scope that warranted assistance, a failed ownership handoff, a seasonal pause, and a completed project. These are descriptive case findings, not an estimated churn rate or causal result; the five cases should not be generalized to the broader sub-50 segment. They do identify operational follow-ups around alternate-admin coverage, assisted-onboarding qualification, and ownership-transfer controls.”

Shorter version:

“We reviewed five clarified sub-50 cancellations and found heterogeneous circumstances, not a single explanatory mechanism. The cases are useful operating evidence for improving admin coverage, assisted-onboarding triage, and ownership handoffs, but are insufficient to support a segment-wide or causal churn claim.”

If a denominator is available, add:

“Of [N] sub-50 cancellations in the review period, five were sufficiently clarified for this qualitative review ([5/N]); this is a case review, not a prevalence estimate.”

arguments.title: Mid-seg churn spike -- Feb 2023 investigation
arguments.body:
Mid-segment churn investigation — update as of 2023-02-14

Signal

The 50–200-seat mid-segment churn signal remains 5.1% monthly versus 2.1% trailing six-month baseline. Owen rechecked the cut; this is not being treated as a cohort-definition bug.

Numbered hypotheses

1. Pricing artifact — packaging, discounting, or contract-mix effects.
2. Competitor cycle.
3. Onboarding timing.
4. CS coverage gap.

2023-02-14 — Tier-segmented pass (Owen 1:1)

Mid-segment monthly churn is consistent across tiers: entry 5.0%, standard 5.2%, plus 5.1% (20 bps spread). This is not the pattern expected if the pricing-page effect were carrying the signal: entry should be disproportionately elevated while standard and plus sit closer to baseline.

Call: pricing artifact is downgraded as the primary explanation, but not ruled out; it does not carry the whole story. Keep this analysis separate from Marcus’s concurrent pricing-page experiment to avoid contaminating the read.
